care_analyses.generated_html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

Allergies: I am allergic to penicillin and Endone (oxycodone).

Cardiac device: I have a heart device that will trigger if my heart stops (implanted defibrillator-type device as described by me).

Falls risk: I had a recent fall at the front while taking bins out (lost footing). I have a history of falls and diabetic foot numbness that can affect balance.

Respiratory: I have emphysema with shortness of breath on exertion.

Diabetes foot care: I have Type 2 diabetes and must wear footwear and monitor my feet/hands daily for wounds.

Resuscitation preference: If I am unresponsive while supports are provided, call 000 and commence resuscitation. Please notify my cousin Dean.

Access/safety: I often leave my front door unlocked when I am home. I do not have a key lockbox. If there is no response at a scheduled visit, call me first; if I do not answer, you have my permission to enter and check on me.

Medication: I self-manage my medicines (including Lasix). I am open to a Webster pack if needed in future.

Personal alarm: I currently use an Apple Watch that notifies my cousin. I am open to a specialist falls pendant with 24/7 monitoring.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 01 September 2025

Preferred Name: Les

Full Name: Leslie Palmer

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this care plan with my Care Partners (Thomas and Katherine). My cousin Dean was discussed as an important support person. I am the decision-maker for my care.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I do not identify any religious or cultural requirements. My core value is my independence. I do not have specific diversity-related needs to note at this time.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer workers who support my independence and routine. I would like services after 11:00 AM because I go to bed late and sleep in.

I am comfortable with phone calls first before entry. If I do not answer and a visit is scheduled, you may enter to check on me.

I would like consistency of worker where possible. If available, I would like “Nani” as my regular worker for domestic assistance and companionship.

I prefer podiatry as an outing at my usual clinic rather than in-home visits at present.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Cousin: Dean (primary support and emergency contact to be notified).

Sister: Important to me, though we have some issues at times.

Adopted/step-daughter: Important to me.

Contact details: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Informal Supports

I currently manage independently and do not have regular informal support in the home. My cousin Dean is local and supportive if needed.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I came to Australia from Ashford, Middlesex (England) when I was 19 for a holiday and stayed with my aunt and uncle. I worked repairing tyres for many years and then drove trucks around Melbourne for about 10–15 years. I was forced to retire after I had a heart device implanted.

I have two brothers and one sister. One brother is in Victoria, one brother is based in South Africa and travels for work, and another is in Waverton, Surrey. I have two daughters with whom I am currently estranged, and I have an adopted/step-daughter who is important to me.

Interests

I enjoy photography (I used to be in two camera clubs and want to restart), four-wheel driving, travelling, snooker/pool, and watching AFL (Richmond Tigers). My village has a clubhouse with a gym, pool, spa, theatre (Netflix/Foxtel), and a snooker club on Tuesday evenings and Saturday mornings. There is also a Men’s Shed on Thursdays at 9:00 AM (too early for me at present).

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have emphysema with shortness of breath on exertion.

I have Type 2 diabetes (tablets only) with some foot numbness at times.

I have cardiac failure and a heart device that will trigger if my heart stops.

I had a left hip fracture with a pin inserted in December 2024. I have occasional hip pain (around 5/10) that settles with rest.

I have high blood pressure and high cholesterol (on medication).

I drink on weekends only.

Medication

I self-manage my medicines daily. I take my morning tablets with breakfast and another tablet around 9–10 AM with coffee. I am taking Lasix as part of my cardiac management, with other routine medicines for blood pressure and cholesterol.

I monitor my blood sugar myself. I am open to using a Webster pack if I need support in the future.

Allergies: Penicillin; Endone (oxycodone). No known issues with codeine or Panadeine.

Mobility and Equipment

I am independent with mobility. I can walk 100 metres without stopping, but I get short of breath if I exert myself and then rest before continuing. I sometimes use a walking stick for confidence and safety (often left in the car).

Equipment at home: Two lift chairs (lounge and bedroom), walking stick, two quad walkers (one is not mine), handrails at the front and in the toilet. I do not currently have a shower chair.

Falls: I recently fell at the front while taking the bins out (lost footing). I have diabetic foot numbness at times which can affect balance. I always wear shoes outside and usually at home as advised.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Turaj Chammacham (as spelled in transcript) at Stetho Health Cranbourne Medical and Dental Centre. Phone: (03) 5996 3188.

Pharmacy: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No. Living with disability (mobility): Yes – independent with occasional stick; history of falls and diabetic foot numbness. Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Mild risk – I sometimes feel isolated and have about one “bad day” per week.

Specific Risks

  • Falls risk at home and outside (recent fall, diabetic neuropathy, handrail gap from house to garage).
  • Respiratory exacerbation (emphysema; shortness of breath on exertion).
  • Cardiac risk (heart failure; implanted device).
  • Foot and skin integrity risk (Type 2 diabetes; reduced sensation in feet; minor hand wound recently).
  • Medication management (I sometimes feel “a bit lazy” with timing, but I am managing).
  • Home access and security (I often leave the door unlocked; no key lockbox; no formal emergency plan).
  • Driving safety (I still drive; sometimes find getting in/out of the car a little hard).
  • Social isolation (I value “someone to talk to” and regular, predictable support).

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Primary contact: Cousin Dean (notify in an emergency).

Additional supports: Sister; adopted/step-daughter.

Contact numbers: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Emergency instructions while supports are being provided: If I am unresponsive or not breathing, call 000 immediately and commence resuscitation. After calling 000, please call my cousin Dean.

Unscheduled concern or no response at a scheduled visit: Call me first (I may be down the street). If I do not answer, you have my permission to enter and check on me. I usually leave my front door unlocked when at home.

Advance care planning: I do not have an advance care plan or directive in place yet.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will restart my photography as an outing I enjoy by attending my Berwick camera club at least twice in the next 12 weeks and having one additional social outing (snooker club Tuesday evening or Saturday morning) each fortnight.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I still drive and mobilise independently but get short of breath on exertion. I sometimes feel isolated and want “someone to talk to.”

How will we do this? (Tasks): Arrange weekly 3-hour companionship/transport after 11:00 AM on Fridays to plan and support photography club attendance (Mondays) and one snooker session each fortnight; confirm any membership/subscription needs and support booking; provide taxi card or transport if I prefer not to drive; encourage pacing and rest breaks for breathlessness.

Who is responsible?: Me, with support from my care provider (preferred worker Nani) for transport/companionship. When will it be done?: Over the next 12 weeks (quarter). How much will it cost?: Service hours from my package; any club fees or transport fares as agreed from my plan budget.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will reduce my falls risk at home by completing an OT assessment, installing a handrail from the house to the garage, and trialling a monitored personal alarm pendant within 8 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Recent fall at the front; diabetic foot numbness; I value my independence and want to keep doing my bins and errands safely.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Book OT assessment within 4 weeks to review walking aids, rails, and home layout; install required handrail(s) and discuss a flyscreen door for airflow; organise a Live Life-style monitored pendant (SIM, GPS, fall detection) after OT recommendation; reinforce footwear and pacing; review after any falls.

Who is responsible?: Me; Occupational Therapist; care provider coordination; maintenance/installer. When will it be done?: OT within 4 weeks; rail and pendant within 8 weeks. How much will it cost?: OT, rails, and alarm funded via my package as applicable; annual alarm subscription as advised.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: I want my home to feel manageable without getting overwhelmed by cleaning. Each week for the next 12 weeks I will have my floors vacuumed, sheets changed, laundry done, dishes cleared, and my bathroom cleaned at least fortnightly.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I break tasks into parts and manage some chores, but sheet changes and heavier tasks are difficult. I sometimes feel stressed when cleaning builds up.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Provide 1 hour domestic assistance weekly (vacuum, dishes, laundry, change bed sheets) and bathroom clean at least fortnightly; follow-on 1 hour for escorted/shopping tasks (groceries/errands) weekly; schedule after 11:00 AM; maintain the same worker where possible (prefer Nani).

Who is responsible?: Me and my care provider (domestic assistant). When will it be done?: Weekly for 12 weeks, then review. How much will it cost?: Service hours from my package.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will keep on top of my health routines by taking my prescribed medicines daily and checking my feet and my blood sugar at least 5 days per week for the next 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I self-manage medicines but can be “a bit lazy” at times. I have diabetes with foot numbness and emphysema.

How will we do this? Care Plan

Care Alerts

  • I am living with dementia (assessed by a geriatrician) and may experience frustration or agitation at times.

  • I have had a hip replacement approximately 12 months ago.

  • I have a recent history of a few falls and I sometimes use a walking stick.

  • I experience shortness of breath and fatigue after walking the dog around the block.

  • I have mild hearing loss and I am hard of hearing in my right ear; please speak clearly and, if possible, on my left side.

  • I avoid pork and chicken as a dietary preference.

  • I am allergic to “tartan” (as reported by my family).

  • Emergency preference: if I am unconscious and not breathing, call triple zero (000) first, then contact Andrew, and perform CPR if needed.

  • I do not currently have a personal alarm; I would like one arranged. I agree to a lockbox being installed for safe access.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 01/09/2025

Preferred Name: Pauline

Full Name: Pauline Stegelman

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Interpreter required?: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan with support from my daughter Wendy and my son-in-law Andrew during an assessment conversation with Tom from Selvio Home Care. I understand that Mav will likely act as my head case manager, with support from Archie and Fraulein.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I am Anglican but I am not currently attending services.

I came to Australia in 1943 and value my family connections and daily routine.

For food preferences, I avoid pork and chicken.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer workers to speak clearly and to my left side as I am hard of hearing in my right ear.

I prefer morning visits for regular services around 10 a.m. to fit my routine.

I would like flexibility to arrange ad hoc social support and transport (for example, outings to the market, shops, cemetery, or appointments) with as much notice as possible.

I agree to the installation of a lockbox for safe access once advised by OT, and I would like a personal alarm arranged.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

My primary contact is Andrew (son-in-law).

My secondary contact is my daughter Wendy (mobile 0418 583 606).

Other important people to me include Peter, Colin, and Jenny.

Informal Supports

My family lives nearby and provides day-to-day support.

Andrew provides most transport and all meal preparation and nutrition support.

My grandson James is a nurse and lives about two minutes away.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I came to Australia in 1943. I used to clean houses (including running my own work) and I used to sew.

I have two sons and two daughters, and several grandchildren.

Interests

I enjoy walking my dog, reading books and the newspaper, and I like going out with Andrew when I can.

I used to enjoy going to Queen Victoria Market on the train and would like the option to visit again.

My dog makes me happy, and keeping to my daily routine makes for a good day.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have a diagnosis of dementia (assessed and followed by a geriatrician, Dr Hamid).

I had a hip replacement approximately 12 months ago.

I have mild hearing loss and am hard of hearing in my right ear.

I have had a few falls and can be short of breath after exertion.

My weight is approximately 62.8 kg and my height is approximately 155 cm.

I am allergic to “tartan” (as reported by my family).

Medication

I have a medication plan in place.

I am not currently taking regular pain medication.

I have no known food allergies or intolerances documented; I avoid pork and chicken as a preference.

Mobility and Equipment

I mobilise independently for short distances and sometimes use a walking stick.

I become tired and out of breath after walking the dog around the block.

I have had a few falls; an OT assessment has been requested to review home safety and equipment needs (including placement of a lockbox).

I would like a personal alarm device arranged so I can press a button if I fall and no one is home.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr. Memritt Abrahams (female), Good Shepherd Medical, 108 North Road. Phone: 9570 0085.

Pharmacy: Hawthorne Road Pharmacy, 600 Hawthorne Road, Brighton East. Phone: 9596 8500.

Allied Health: I see a podiatrist every 10 weeks through Medica.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: I migrated to Australia in 1943; I identify as Anglican. No interpreter needs were discussed.

Living with disability (mobility): I sometimes use a walking stick, have a history of a few falls, and experience shortness of breath with exertion.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I am content with my routine, and my family would like me to increase social interaction; I may experience frustration related to dementia.

Specific Risks

  • Falls risk due to prior falls, recent hip replacement, and exertional breathlessness.

  • Cognitive risk related to dementia, including possible agitation or frustration.

  • Hearing impairment in the right ear may affect communication and safety.

  • Lack of a current personal alarm and emergency plan; lockbox not yet installed.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If there is a medical emergency: call triple zero (000) first, then contact Andrew.

If I am found unconscious and not breathing: commence CPR while calling triple zero (000), then notify Andrew.

If there is no response on arrival for a scheduled visit: call Andrew (primary contact) to check on me.

I agree to the installation of a lockbox for safe entry by care workers and emergency services (location to be advised by OT).

Primary Contact: Andrew (son-in-law).

Secondary Contact: Wendy (daughter) – Mobile 0418 583 606.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep walking my dog most mornings and feel less out of breath after the walk around the block, while staying safe.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can walk independently with a stick when needed but I get tired and short of breath after a block and I have had a few falls.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Plan a morning walk route around the block; use my walking stick when needed; add one mid-walk rest if required; practice breathing and pacing; schedule rest and a drink before and after; support worker to prompt safe pacing on social support days.

Who is responsible?: Me; family encouragement; support worker on social support days. When will it be done?: 5 mornings per week for the next 12 weeks; review at 3 months. How much will it cost?: Included within existing social support time (no additional cost beyond scheduled hours).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 2 Goal: I will reconnect with the community by visiting Queen Victoria Market with support at least once this quarter.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I enjoy the market and trains; I may tire with longer outings and I may need help with transport and pacing.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Book a Friday 10 a.m. social support session (2–4 hours as budget allows); decide on car or train with the worker; plan rests and a coffee stop; carry my stick; family or worker to confirm return time.

Who is responsible?: Me; support worker to arrange transport and pacing; family to help choose the date. When will it be done?: One completed visit within 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: Worker time and transport under package; I will pay for personal purchases and any parking.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: I will reduce my falls risk at home by completing an OT home safety assessment and having a lockbox and personal alarm arranged and tested.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have had a few falls and get breathless with exertion; I am agreeable to a lockbox and personal alarm.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Book OT assessment (including lockbox placement and mobility aids review); arrange installation of lockbox; arrange and test a personal alarm; keep a simple falls log (date/time/circumstances) for review.

Who is responsible?: Provider to coordinate OT and equipment; me and my family to use/test devices. When will it be done?: OT within 4 weeks; lockbox and alarm installed and tested within 8 weeks; review at 3 months. How much will it cost?: OT under Clinical Care (government funded); devices through package as per inclusions.

Service Category: Clinical Care / Independence Support

GOAL 4 Goal: I will keep my home clean and safe without overexerting myself by using regular domestic assistance.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can do some tasks but I tire; bathrooms, floors, blinds, and vacuuming are heavier tasks.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Domestic assistance for bathrooms (including shower, seat, toilet), wash floors, dust Venetian blinds, and vacuuming.

Who is responsible?: Support worker to complete tasks; I will guide priorities. When will it be done?: Every fortnight on Wednesdays at 10 a.m. for 2 hours; review at 3 months. How much will it cost?: Covered within my package allocation for Everyday Living services.

Service Category: Everyday Living

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

  • Clinical Care: Occupational Therapy assessment and clinical falls prevention advice.

  • Independence Support: Social support, transport to community activities, personal alarm and lockbox coordination.

  • Everyday Living: Domestic assistance (clean bathrooms, wash floors, dust blinds, vacuuming).

Quarterly Budget Allocation: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Prepared By

Name: __________ | Role: Care Partner, Date: Today | Review Date: Quarterly (every 3 months) | Signature: __________

Standard 1 – Consumer dignity and choice

I stated my preferences, including Anglican faith (not currently attending), dietary choices (no pork or chicken), and my desire to keep my routine and walk my dog.

I confirmed emergency choices: call 000 first, then contact Andrew; perform CPR if I am unconscious and not breathing.

I prefer clear communication on my left side due to hearing loss in my right ear.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers

I participated in planning with my daughter Wendy and son-in-law Andrew alongside the provider.

My plan includes an OT assessment (including lockbox placement and falls prevention), social support options, and regular domestic assistance, with quarterly reviews.

My clinical information includes dementia diagnosis, hip replacement, mild hearing loss, and history of falls and exertional breathlessness.

I have a GP (Dr. Memritt Abrahams) and a regular pharmacy, and I have a medication plan in place.

Domestic assistance is booked fortnightly on Wednesdays at 10 a.m. for 2 hours (bathrooms, floors, blinds, vacuuming).

Social support is scheduled for Fridays around 10 a.m. for 2 hours on an ad hoc basis for outings such as markets, shops, or the cemetery.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment

A lockbox will be installed for safe access, and a personal alarm device will be arranged to support safety at home.

I can contact Mav (head case manager), or Archie and Fraulein if needed; Tom provided contact information and a magnet number for the team.

I do not have preferences regarding the age of the worker.

If a worker arrives and I do not answer the door, please phone Stuart.

I am comfortable using support workers for community access (for example to go for a coffee, visit local venues, or attend activities) if I feel trapped indoors.

My Preferred Support People

Stuart (main point of contact for my care and documents).

June (partner).

I also have friends I sometimes see: Julian Vyde and Graham Dawson, and my neighbour Cynthia across the road.

June supports me at home.

My family includes three children and eleven grandchildren; I enjoy watching my grandkids play football.

I sometimes catch up with friends (e.g., Julian and Graham).

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Hamilton and moved to Portland as a child. I grew up on a farm with a brother and a sister. I have worked for a builder, at the Meatworks (boning), and later owned a small farm, a dairy farm, and then a hobby farm before moving to my current home.

I once had a significant financial loss on an investment which affected us at the time. Family is important to me and I feel happiest when my family is going well.

Interests

I enjoy walking, gardening, going out for a coffee, and watching football. I like getting outside and doing something physical on good days.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have had a hernia operation.

I had five weeks of radiation treatment in Geelong.

I have had multiple skin cancers removed, including from my ear, which has affected my hearing. I currently have a spot on my neck that may need removal.

I have prostate-related nocturia that causes me to get up regularly during the night.

I have not been recently assessed for dementia; my doctor previously advised I do not have dementia. I get frustrated when I cannot recall names.

My current weight is about 82 kg and my height is about 5 foot 10 inches.

I have no known allergies.

Medication

I am not taking any prescribed medications.

I take multivitamins and I sometimes take a Panadol before bed to help with headaches and to get a few hours of sleep without needing to get up to the toilet.

Mobility and Equipment

I am independent with mobility and do not use a walking stick or frame.

I can get in and out of the car without assistance.

I have a gopher (used previously on the golf course) available if I needed it, but I do not use it routinely.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr. Mayna, South Portland Medical Centre.

Pharmacy: South Portland Pharmacy.

Allied Health: I receive physiotherapy (one hour).

Dental: I attend the dentist approximately every 12 months.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No specific CALD considerations documented.

Living with disability (mobility): No – I am independent, with some reduced endurance compared to the past.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes – I can feel low if I am stuck indoors (e.g., in bad weather) and miss social interaction.

Specific Risks

  • Hearing impairment in both ears (history of cancer removal from ear) – I need clear, slow, louder communication.

  • History of multiple skin cancers; ongoing skin surveillance required (current neck spot for review).

  • Occasional headaches (around 6/10), sometimes triggered by stress or tension.

  • Prostate-related nocturia – getting up at night increases fatigue and night-time trip/fall risk.

  • Past fall from a ladder; I report doing window cleaning at home – ladder use presents a risk.

  • Social isolation risk on bad weather days when I cannot get outdoors.

If there is an emergency, call 000 first.

After calling emergency services, contact Stuart (main point of contact).

My advance care plan is held by Geelong Hospital. My children hold enduring power of attorney. Copies may be requested from the solicitor if required by a hospital.

I do not have a separate personal medical emergency plan documented.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with mobility, but I cannot walk as far as I used to. Bad weather and headaches can limit me. Night-time waking for the toilet can affect energy the next day.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will walk for 20 minutes at a comfortable pace at least 4 days per week. I will do light gardening for 20 minutes at least 2 days per week. Service Category: Everyday Living

Abilities and considerations (risks): My headaches are occasional (about 6/10) and can be triggered by stress/tension. I sometimes take Panadol before bed. Nocturia causes me to get up regularly at night.

When will it be done?: Diary kept for the next 12 weeks; GP review within 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: GP/clinical review under Clinical Care; minor environmental supports within my package hours.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will tell all new staff and visitors to speak slowly, clearly, and a little louder, preferably on my left side. I will check hearing aid batteries weekly and wear my aids during visits and outings.

Care Plan

Care Alerts

I wear hearing aids in both ears (my right ear is worse after cancer removal). Please speak loudly, clearly and slowly so I can understand.

I have an Advance Care Plan lodged with Geelong Hospital. Stuart is my main point of contact if urgent decisions are needed.

I have no known allergies.

I experience occasional headaches (around 6/10) often triggered by stress or tension. I usually take a Panadol at night.

I have prostate trouble that causes frequent night-time toileting (nocturia).

I have a history of multiple skin cancers removed and ongoing sun-damaged skin spots.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 01/09/2025

Preferred Name: Ralph

Full Name: Ralph Wakely

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I participated in this assessment and planning discussion.

June (my partner) contributed to the conversation.

Stuart (my son) is my main point of contact and will be involved in decisions if needed.

A care partner/interviewer facilitated the assessment.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I do not have any specific cultural, diversity, values or belief requirements for matching me with workers.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer workers to speak loudly, clearly and slowly due to my hearing loss.

I am comfortable with any appropriately skilled worker; I do not require an older worker or any specific gender preference.

I value getting outside for a walk or doing something in the garden when the weather is good.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Stuart – my son and main point of contact.

June – my partner.

Cynthia – my neighbour across the road.

Friends: Julian Vyde and Graham Dawson.

Informal Supports

I have three children and eleven grandchildren who are important in my life.

I sometimes go out with friends for social interaction, and I enjoy watching my grandkids play football.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Hamilton and moved to Portland when I was about three. I grew up on a farm and later worked for a builder and at the Meatworks (boning). I owned a small farm on Penny’s Road, then a dairy farm, and later a hobby farm before moving to my current home. I once had a significant financial loss from an investment which affected our lives.

My childhood was during the war and was “pretty good.” I have a brother and a sister. Pets have been important to me over my life, and losing them has been emotional.

Interests

I enjoy walking, gardening, going out for a coffee, and watching football. I like watching my grandkids play football. Meeting friends helps a lot. A good day for me is when I get a walk in and can do something physically outside. Bad days can be due to headaches or being stuck indoors because of bad weather.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have had a hernia operation (years ago), five weeks of radiation treatment in Geelong, and multiple skin cancers removed (including from around my ear, which affected my hearing). I currently have a spot on my neck that may need removal. I report prostate trouble with frequent night-time urination. I have not been recently assessed for dementia; my GP previously said I do not have dementia. I get frustrated when I cannot remember people’s names.

Medication

I do not take any prescribed medications.

I take multivitamins. I sometimes take a Panadol before bed.

I have no known allergies.

Mobility and Equipment

I am independent with mobility and do not use a walking aid. I can get in and out of the car without assistance. I have walking sticks available (from prior family use) but do not use them. I used to use a gopher around the golf course. I report reduced walking distance and energy compared to before. I have no significant falls history noted (one fall off a ladder in the past).

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Mayna, South Portland Medical Centre.

Pharmacy: South Portland Pharmacy.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: I am not from a culturally and linguistically diverse background and do not need an interpreter.

Living with disability (mobility): I am independent but cannot walk as far as I used to and have less energy.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I can feel low or “a bit depressed” when I am stuck indoors or see less of friends; social interaction helps a lot.

Specific Risks

Hearing impairment increases communication risks (I need loud, clear, slow speech).

Night-time toileting (nocturia) may increase falls risk in low light.

History of multiple skin cancers requires ongoing surveillance.

Occasional headaches (6/10) can limit activities and may affect sleep.

Gardening and window cleaning involve manual tasks; prior ladder use led to a fall in the past.

Periods of bad weather and reduced social contact increase isolation risk.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If I am found unwell or unresponsive: call Triple Zero (000) immediately, then contact Stuart (main contact).

Refer to my Advance Care Plan held with Geelong Hospital if needed.

I do not have a separate personal medical emergency plan documented.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will stay socially connected by getting out for coffee, meeting friends (including at the golf club even if I am not playing), or attending my grandkids’ football so I am not “stuck indoors.”

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with mobility but have reduced endurance and occasional headaches. Bad weather and hearing loss can make socialising harder.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo support workers will provide Social Support and Transport to and from chosen community activities; speak loudly, clearly and slowly; assist with planning simple outings on days with good weather or provide companionship at home with a cuppa and time in the garden when weather is poor; monitor fatigue and take rest breaks.

Who is responsible?: I am, supported by Salveo HomeCare Social Support workers. When will it be done?: 2 hours fortnightly for the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: $85/hour = $340/month, plus $1.40/km transport as incurred.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 2 Goal: I will keep my garden tidy and my home safe by maintaining monthly gardening and completing agreed home maintenance (gutters, outside windows, and cleaning the air-con filters twice).

Abilities and considerations (risks): I enjoy gardening and usually manage light tasks. Ladder use and manual work can increase falls and strain risks.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo Light Home & Gardening Maintenance will attend monthly for lawn/garden tasks I choose on the day; Salveo Home Maintenance will complete gutter/outside window cleaning as scheduled and clean the air-con filters twice during this quarter (minimum 1-hour visit per service).

Who is responsible?: I am, supported by Salveo HomeCare maintenance workers. When will it be done?: Gardening 1 hour monthly; air-con filters cleaned twice within this 3‑month period. How much will it cost?: Gardening $85/month. Air-con filter cleans: 2 visits x 1 hour = $170 this quarter (time-limited), billed at $85/hour.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: I will work on improving my walking stamina so I can walk a bit further and feel better after getting outside.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with walking but have less energy and occasional headaches triggered by tension.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will attend a 1‑hour Allied Health (Physiotherapy) session to review and update a home exercise/walking program tailored to me; I will keep a simple walking log (minutes per walk, 3 times a week) and practice any stretches or exercises provided.

Who is responsible?: I am, supported by a Salveo Allied Health Therapist (Physio). When will it be done?: One 1‑hour session within the next 3 months, with home exercises ongoing. How much will it cost?: $180 for the session this quarter (equivalent to $60/month averaged).

Service Category: Clinical Care

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category:

Clinical Care (100% government funded): Allied Health Therapist (Physio) – 1 hour this quarter ($180 one-off this quarter; funding per program rules).

Independence Support: Social Support and Transport – 2 hours fortnightly ($340/month) plus $1.40/km as incurred.

Everyday Living: Light Home & Gardening Maintenance – 1 hour monthly ($85/month). Home Maintenance – air-con filter cleaning twice this quarter ($170 total this quarter), and gutters/outside windows as scheduled at $85/hour.

Quarterly Budget Allocation: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

I participated in developing this plan and agree to the supports described. I understand how my information will be used and shared with service providers involved in my care. Copies of this plan will be provided to me and, with my consent, to my nominated contacts and involved health providers.

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance: I understand I can raise feedback or complaints with my provider at any time. Care Alerts: I have no known allergies (as reported).

Care Alerts: I experience occasional headaches (around 6/10) and prostate-related nocturia that wakes me at night.

Care Alerts: If I am found unresponsive: call Triple Zero (000) first, then call Stuart.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 01 Sep 2025

Preferred Name: Ralph

Full Name: Ralph Wakely

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No. I prefer people to speak slowly, clearly and a little louder due to my hearing impairment.

People involved in developing my care plan

I participated in developing this plan. Stuart is my main point of contact and holds Enduring Power of Attorney with my children. A Care Partner facilitated the assessment discussion.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I do not have any specific cultural, diversity, values or belief considerations for worker matching or service delivery.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I do not have preferences about the age or background of workers.

Please communicate by speaking slowly, clearly and a little louder. Address me on my left side when possible because of my hearing loss.

I value practical support that helps me keep active outdoors (walking, gardening) and to connect socially on days I feel “stuck indoors.”

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Stuart (main point of contact/EPOA).

Friends: Julian Vyde and Graham Dawson.

Neighbour: Cynthia (across the road).

My three children and eleven grandchildren.

Informal Supports

I sometimes go out with friends (e.g., Julian and Graham). I see family and enjoy watching my grandkids play football. I currently do not need assistance with transport.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Hamilton and moved to Portland as a child. I grew up on a farm with a brother and a sister. Over my life I worked for a builder, at the Meatworks (boning), owned a small farm, then a dairy farm, later a hobby farm, and then moved to my current home. I experienced a significant financial loss from an investment which affected us at the time.

Interests

I enjoy walking, gardening and going out for a coffee. I like watching football and especially watching my grandkids play. A good day is when I “get a walk in” and do something outside. Bad days include headaches or being stuck indoors due to bad weather. Social interaction helps me a lot.

My Medical Information

Medical History

Medical History: Past hernia operation; radiation treatment in Geelong; multiple skin cancer removals (including right ear, contributing to hearing loss). I currently have a spot on my neck that may need review/removal. I report prostate trouble with frequent night waking. I have not been recently assessed for dementia; my GP indicated I did not have dementia a couple of years ago. I feel frustrated when I cannot recall names.

Medication

Medication: I do not take prescribed medicines. I take multivitamins. I occasionally take Panadol before bed which helps me get through a few hours without needing to toilet.

Mobility and Equipment

Mobility: I am independent with mobility and do not use walking aids. I can get in and out of the car without assistance. I have walking sticks at home (not in use) and previously used a “gopher” around the golf course. I reported a past fall from a ladder. I have no pressure injuries and no foot problems.

Oral and Skin Care: I see the dentist every 12 months. I report some skin issues but I do not currently use prescribed ointments.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr. Mayna, South Portland Medical Centre.

Pharmacy: South Portland Pharmacy.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Living with disability (mobility): I am independent; I do not use aids. I walk less distance than I used to and fatigue can limit me on some days.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I feel low when stuck indoors and when social contact is limited; social interaction helps me a lot.

Specific Risks

  • Hearing impairment (both ears; right ear worse after cancer removal). Communication needs: speak slowly, clearly and louder, preferably on my left side.
  • Headaches (occasional, about 6/10). Triggers include stress/tension and boredom.
  • Prostate-related nocturia with frequent night waking.
  • Skin cancer history; current neck spot may need follow-up/removal.

  • Social isolation risk on bad-weather days when I feel “trapped indoors.”

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Emergency Instructions: If I am found unresponsive or in an emergency: call Triple Zero (000) first, then call Stuart (main contact/EPOA).

Advanced Care Planning: My Advanced Care Plan is held by Geelong Hospital. Copies of my Enduring Power of Attorney may be requested from Stuart/the solicitor if needed.

Personal Emergency Plan: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my garden safe and manageable so I can “get a walk in” and enjoy being outside most days.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with mobility and enjoy gardening, but I tire more easily than I used to and I have a past fall from a ladder. Headaches and bad weather can limit outdoor time.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Light Home & Gardening Maintenance to mow lawns, tidy paths, clear minor trip hazards and assist with light gardening as needed during visits.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will increase my social interaction so I don’t feel “trapped indoors,” including going out for a coffee or to meet friends over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Social contact helps my mood; I do not currently need transport assistance but bad weather and headaches can limit me. Hearing impairment requires clear, slow and louder speech.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Social Support to accompany me to local community outings I choose (e.g., café, catching up with friends, attending the local club or watching grandkids play). I will keep a simple weekly note of outings completed.

Who is responsible?: Me (choosing destinations and booking support); Salveo support worker (companionship and community access). When will it be done?: 2 hours fortnightly for the next 3 months (review at 6 weeks). How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $340/month ($1,020 per quarter) plus transport at $1.40/km if used (variable).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: I will maintain my walking and gardening capacity with physiotherapy so I can continue to “get a walk in” on more days each week.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent but cannot walk as far as I used to. I currently receive physiotherapy (one-hour session recorded). Headaches and fatigue can limit activity.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Continue Allied Health Therapy (Physiotherapy) focusing on strength, balance and pacing for outdoor activity. I will note the number of days I complete a walk each week to track change across the quarter.

Service Category: Clinical Care

Abilities and considerations (risks): I prefer not to use ladders due to a past fall. I want good air quality and reduced dust to help comfort and sleep.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will complete two air-con filter cleaning visits and visually check for obvious dust build-up around vents. Any higher or ladder work will be done by workers with appropriate equipment.

Who is responsible?: Salveo support worker (filter cleaning); Me (allow access, identify units). When will it be done?: Two 1-hour visits during this quarter (total 2 hours). How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $170 per quarter (average $56.67/month) with Salveo HomeCare.

Service Category: Everyday Living

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

  • Independence Support: Social Support – 2 hours fortnightly at $85/hour ($340/month; $1,020/quarter) + transport $1.40/km if used (variable).

  • Everyday Living: Home maintenance (air-con filter cleaning) – two 1-hour visits this quarter at $85/hour ($170/quarter; average $56.67/month).

Quarterly Budget Allocation: Planned services total $1,985 per quarter (plus any transport kilometres at $1.40/km if used).

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I participated in developing this care plan and I agree with the goals and services listed for the next 3 months. I consent to share this plan with my Support at Home provider (Salveo HomeCare) and Stuart (main contact/EPOA) so supports can be coordinated. My Advanced Care Plan is held by Geelong Hospital.

Prepared By (Name: __________ | Role: Care Partner, Date: Today | Review Date: Quarterly (every 3 months) | Signature: __________)

I expressed what a good day and bad day look like for me, my preferences for communication (speak slowly, clearly and louder), and the activities that matter to me (walking, gardening, social interaction). I provided information about my medical history, current symptoms, daily routines, risks, and supports. My plan includes quarterly review, clear goals using SMARTA principles, and alignment to the Support at Home Program. My Advanced Care Plan and EPOA arrangements were noted.

My clinical risks (headaches, nocturia, skin cancer history, hearing impairment) were documented. I will continue physiotherapy to maintain mobility for walking and gardening. I have no prescribed medications; I use multivitamins and occasional Panadol.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living

I will receive Light Home & Gardening Maintenance to keep my outdoor areas safe and manageable and to complete air-con filter cleaning. Social Support will help me maintain community access and reduce isolation on days I feel “trapped indoors.”

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment

Workers will communicate in ways that suit me (slow, clear, louder speech; address my left side when possible). Tasks involving height (ladders) will be completed safely by workers with appropriate equipment.

Summary 
The meeting involved an assessment for home care services for an elderly Cambodian woman, conducted between a care coordinator from Salvio Care and the client's daughter, Jenny, who serves as her primary caregiver. The assessment aimed to establish the client's needs, background, and care requirements to set up appropriate home care services. 
The coordinator began by gathering cultural and background information about the client, noting she values honesty, respect, and prefers calm caregivers who speak either Cambodian or Mandarin. Jenny provided her mother's Medicare and pension card details and discussed her role as the decision-maker, though she doesn't currently have power of attorney. 
Jenny shared her mother's life history, revealing they fled Cambodia during the war in 1975, experiencing four years of slave labor and hardship before eventually being sponsored to come to Australia in 1980. The client lost two children during this period and has experienced significant trauma, which sometimes manifests as PTSD symptoms. 
The assessment covered the client's health conditions, including chronic back and knee pain (rated 8-9/10 daily), hearing loss (70% in both ears), plantar fasciitis, gum disease, and occasional ear infections. The client has experienced two significant falls in the past two years - one resulting in fractured ribs and facial injuries, and another related to high blood pressure. She takes medication for anxiety and depression, which has helped manage her mental health. 
The client currently uses several mobility aids including an electric bed, a new chair, and a walker for outside use. She has limited mobility and requires assistance with some activities but remains independent with personal care, though Jenny stays nearby during showering for safety. The client needs incontinence products (Poise pads) and uses a personal alarm from National Health Australia. 
The coordinator and Jenny discussed the services to be provided through the home care package, including domestic assistance (vacuuming, mopping, bathroom cleaning) and gardening services scheduled for Tuesdays from 10 AM to 12 PM. They also discussed continuing the client's massage therapy on Saturdays, which helps with her pain management, and potentially adding podiatry services six times per year to help with her foot health. 
The meeting concluded with discussions about emergency procedures and the client's preferences for communication with care workers. Jenny emphasized that her mother prefers consistency in caregivers and becomes anxious with frequent changes or rushed interactions. 
Chapter 
Cultural Background and Personal Values ‎ 00:00:00
The meeting began with the care coordinator inquiring about the client's cultural background and values. Jenny indicated that her mother values honesty, respect, and "doing good deeds." When asked about religious or spiritual beliefs, Jenny reiterated that her mother primarily values honesty and being straightforward. The coordinator asked about cultural factors to consider when matching her with a worker, and Jenny explained that her mother is anxious and needs someone calm, kind, and understanding who doesn't rush. She noted her mother is quite traditional and would ideally need a caregiver who speaks either Cambodian or Mandarin. 
Administrative Information and Decision-Making ‎ 00:03:01
The coordinator collected administrative information, including Jenny's address (6 Wellesley Road in Ringwood Mall, postcode 3134). Jenny confirmed she is responsible for making decisions for her mother but doesn't have power of attorney yet, though she's considering getting it as "everybody seemed to ask that question." The coordinator explained that legally, while her mother is of sound mind, they would have to follow her mother's instructions if they differed from Jenny's. Jenny was designated as the emergency contact. 
Medical History and Assessment ‎ 00:05:42
The coordinator inquired about income testing and cognitive assessments. Jenny mentioned her mother had a brain scan that revealed a mini stroke but noted it "doesn't affect anything." She also mentioned her mother is starting to forget things. The coordinator explained that if dementia is diagnosed, they could access an additional $7,000 in funding. Jenny indicated she might get her mother tested. The coordinator offered to liaise with the doctor if needed and explained the cognitive test is very basic. 
Client Rights and Consents ‎ 00:10:58
The coordinator obtained Jenny's consent for various aspects of care. Jenny agreed to having Salvio Care staff present during services but declined having third parties or students present as her mother doesn't like having many people around. She consented to participating in Salvio Care's audits and compliance activities, and to Salvio Care recording the meeting for care planning purposes. She also agreed to Salvio Care contacting her mother's GP to discuss health information but declined consent for photos or videos for social media. 
Medical Practitioner and Pharmacy Information ‎ 00:16:36
Jenny provided details about her mother's medical practitioner, Dr. Brian O'Hias at Progress Medical Centre at the Pines on Reynolds Road (phone: 9841-6111). She also mentioned her mother gets medications from a pharmacy called "Gang Kong" and has a personal alarm from National Health Australia that was paid for outright at $525. Jenny confirmed her mother doesn't have a key lockbox and prefers to be present when support workers enter her home. 
Emergency Planning ‎ 00:20:07
The coordinator asked about emergency planning. Jenny hadn't specifically planned for disasters like fires but mentioned her mother has supportive neighbors who have helped during medical emergencies in the past. Jenny stays in regular contact with her mother and tracks her location using a live 360 app. In case of a scheduled visit where her mother doesn't answer, Jenny requested that the support worker call her. For medical emergencies, Jenny instructed that support workers should perform resuscitation if needed, then call emergency services, and then call her. 
Important People and Communication ‎ 00:24:41
Jenny identified the important people in her mother's life as her four children, eight grandchildren, neighbors, and friends she talks to on the phone. Her mother stopped attending social groups due to driving limitations. Jenny mentioned that support workers should be aware that her mother gets anxious, so they should ask questions one at a time, speak clearly and loudly, and not rush her. Her mother has 70% hearing loss but can hear at 80% capacity with her hearing aid. 
Client's Daily Life and Well-being ‎ 00:27:44
Jenny described what keeps her mother healthy and safe: gardening, cooking, maintaining a positive mindset, and avoiding negative people. A good day for her mother involves getting good sleep (which is difficult due to incontinence), sunbathing for vitamin D, taking meals and medication on time, and not having family issues to worry about. Jenny explained that the family only shares positive news with her mother to avoid causing her stress. Bad days involve lack of sleep, anxiety, and conversations with her sister who recently lost a daughter, which affects her mother mentally. 
Life History and Trauma ‎ 00:37:16
Jenny shared her mother's difficult life history. The family was originally from Cambodia and experienced the war in 1975, enduring four years of slave labor, hardship, and torture. Her mother lost two children during this time. The family risked everything to flee to Thailand but were sent back to Cambodia, walking over mountains filled with landmines. They fled to Thailand again, where the Red Cross provided assistance, and were eventually sponsored to come to Australia in 1980. Jenny's parents worked hard to build a life and educate their four children. Her father passed away in 2001, which was difficult for her mother. 
Health Conditions and Behaviors ‎ 00:45:09
Jenny described her mother's behavioral changes, including frustration and anger, which are managed with anti-depression and anxiety medication. She identified PTSD as a trigger, noting her mother becomes aggressive and hostile when thinking about the past. The family manages these episodes by taking her out for coffee or meals and focusing on positive aspects of life. Her mother takes prescribed medication, which Jenny helps organize in weekly pill containers. She experiences chronic pain in her lower back, knees, and has migraines and tinnitus, rating her pain at 8-9 out of 10 daily. 
Mobility and Falls History ‎ 00:56:55
Jenny described her mother's mobility as limited, with difficulties walking, bending, and getting up. She uses an electric bed, a walker when outside, and cannot get up from the ground without assistance. Jenny detailed two significant falls: one at Bimby Park where her mother fell face-down after getting dizzy, resulting in facial injuries and fractured ribs; and another six months later related to high blood pressure that required ambulance assistance. Her mother needs help getting in and out of the car, using a walking stick with assistance. 
Personal Care and Assistance Needs ‎ 01:03:01
Jenny explained that her mother can shower independently but needs someone present for safety. She doesn't currently need assistance with oral care but does have gum disease and is under dental care. She has no current skin problems but uses incontinence products (Poise pads). Jenny indicated interest in podiatry services (six times yearly) to help with her mother's bunions and flat feet. Her mother is pre-diabetic and requires a low-salt, no-sugar diet. She has 70% hearing loss in both ears and wears hearing aids. 
Service Planning and Scheduling ‎ 01:14:58
The coordinator and Jenny finalized service scheduling, with domestic assistance and gardening both set for Tuesdays from 10 AM to 12 PM. Jenny confirmed her mother wants to keep her current gardener and mentioned her mother receives massage therapy on Saturdays, which she prefers to continue. The coordinator explained they would need clinical justification from a physio or doctor to cover massage therapy through the package and would need documentation from the current gardener before they could continue using their services. 
Action Items 
Jenny to consider getting power of attorney for her mother as many services request this. ‎ 00:05:26
Jenny to arrange cognitive testing for her mother to potentially access additional funding ($7,000) if dementia is diagnosed. ‎ 00:07:33
Coordinator to liaise with the doctor regarding cognitive assessment results if testing is done. ‎ 00:07:50
Coordinator to ensure continuity of care with consistent support workers for domestic assistance. ‎ 00:32:53
Coordinator to arrange domestic assistance and gardening services for Tuesdays from 10 AM to 12 PM. ‎ 01:14:58
Coordinator to arrange podiatry services six times per year. ‎ 01:05:14
Coordinator to collect documentation from the current gardener before continuing their services. ‎ 01:16:45
Coordinator to obtain clinical justification from a physio for massage therapy to be covered by the package. ‎ 01:16:45
Coordinator to try to find Cambodian or Mandarin-speaking support workers for the client. ‎ 00:40:07

care_analyses.generated_html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have a high risk of falls due to orthostatic dizziness and limited mobility. I sustained facial injuries and 3–4 fractured ribs from a fall two years ago and had another ambulance-attended episode related to high blood pressure about six months later.

I live with chronic pain rated 8–9/10 daily (lower back, knees “bone-on-bone,” migraines, tinnitus). Pain and fatigue increase my falls risk and disturb my sleep.

I have 70% hearing loss in both ears. With hearing aids I hear at about 80% capacity. Please speak clearly, a little louder, one question at a time, and do not rush me.

I prefer support workers who are calm, kind, consistent, and who speak Cambodian (Khmer) or Mandarin. Frequent changes and rushed interactions make me anxious.

I have a history of significant trauma (PTSD). Conversations about war, death, and past losses can trigger distress, agitation, or anger. Please use a calm, reassuring approach and redirect to positive topics.

I use incontinence products (Poise pads/liners) and follow a low-salt, no-sugar diet as I am pre-diabetic and have a history of high blood pressure.

I currently do not have a key lockbox and do not want support workers entering my home without me. If I do not answer the door, please call Jenny (my daughter) first.

Emergency instruction: If I am unconscious or not breathing, perform resuscitation/first aid immediately, then call 000 (triple zero), then call Jenny.

I have no known medication or food allergies documented. Some topical anti-inflammatory rubs can irritate my skin and cause rashes.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 01 September 2025

Preferred Name: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Full Name: Yuk Chien

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: Cambodian (Khmer) or Mandarin. I also speak English as a second language.

Interpreter required?: Yes. I prefer Cambodian (Khmer) or Mandarin support and clear, louder speech due to hearing loss.

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan with my daughter Jenny (primary caregiver and emergency contact) and a Salveo HomeCare Care Partner during the home care assessment discussion.

My GP, Dr Brian O’Hias (Progress Medical Centre at The Pines), may be consulted for health information and care coordination as I have consented.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I am Cambodian and quite traditional. I value honesty, respect, “doing good deeds,” and straightforward communication.

I prefer calm, kind, patient workers who do not rush me and who can speak Cambodian (Khmer) or Mandarin.

I experienced severe trauma during the Cambodian war and displacement. I can become anxious or distressed if conversations focus on war, death, or past loss. Please focus on positive, practical topics.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer continuity of care with the same worker at the same time each week wherever possible. Frequent changes increase my anxiety.

I need workers to speak clearly and a little louder, one question at a time, and allow me extra time to respond due to hearing loss and language preferences.

I prefer that workers do not enter my home unless I am present. If I do not answer the door at a scheduled time, please call Jenny first.

I am independent with showering, but I prefer someone nearby for safety. I am not ready to accept personal care with showering at this time.

I prefer domestic assistance and gardening on Tuesdays from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM. I prefer my massage therapy on Saturdays.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

My four children, my eight grandchildren, and supportive neighbours are important to me. I also have friends I speak with by phone.

Informal Supports

Jenny organizes and reminds me about medications, appointments, and supports, and stays nearby during showering for safety.

My family visits regularly and often takes me out for coffee or a meal, which helps my mood and anxiety.

My neighbours are supportive and have assisted during past medical episodes. Jenny uses a location app (Live360) to check I am safe.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I am originally from Cambodia. My family and I lived through the 1975 war, four years of slave labour and hardship, and the loss of two of my children. We fled to Thailand twice and were assisted by the Red Cross before being sponsored to Australia in 1980. My husband passed away in 2001. These experiences affect me and can trigger PTSD symptoms.

Interests

I love gardening and cooking. Good days include sun for vitamin D, meals and medications on time, and peaceful family news. I prefer quiet and to live on my own. I try to keep my social circle positive and avoid stressful conversations.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have chronic lower back and knee pain (reported 8–9/10 daily). My knees are described as “bone-on-bone.”

I have a history of plantar fasciitis (improved with orthotics, exercises, proper shoes) and bunions on both feet with flat feet.

I have 70% hearing loss in both ears with a history of recurrent ear infections and perforated eardrums. I wear hearing aids.

I have migraines and tinnitus, which are worse at night and disrupt sleep.

I am pre-diabetic and follow a low-salt, no-sugar diet. I have a history of high blood pressure with two ambulance-attended episodes.

A brain scan showed a “mini stroke,” noted as not affecting my function. I am starting to forget things at times.

I experienced significant trauma and can have PTSD symptoms. Anxiety and depression are currently managed with prescribed medication.

Falls history: significant fall at Bimby Park with facial injuries and 3–4 fractured ribs (hospitalised), and another event six months later related to high blood pressure (ambulance attendance and medication adjustment).

I have gum disease and dental issues (bottom denture) and am under ongoing dental care.

I experience urinary incontinence and use Poise pads/liners and pull-ups when going out.

Medication

I take prescribed medication for anxiety and depression, and I use pain relief (e.g., anti-inflammatories, paracetamol as advised). After the rib fractures I used stronger pain relief prescribed by a doctor.

Jenny organizes my medications weekly in day-of-the-week containers and reminds me about different dosing times.

No drug or food allergies are documented. Some topical anti-inflammatory rubs can irritate my skin.

Mobility and Equipment

My mobility is limited. I have difficulty walking, bending, and getting up from low or ground level. I cannot get up from the floor independently.

I use an electric bed, a new supportive chair, and a walker when outside (with a seat for rest breaks). I use a walking stick with assistance for car transfers.

I use a personal alarm from National Health Australia (NHA), paid outright ($525).

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Brian O’Hias, Progress Medical Centre at The Pines (Reynolds Road). Phone: 9841-6111.

Pharmacy: “Gang Kong” pharmacy (local details held by Jenny).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Yes – Cambodian background, prefers Cambodian (Khmer) or Mandarin language support.

Living with disability (mobility): Yes – limited mobility, chronic pain, falls history.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes – PTSD history, anxiety/depression (currently managed), sleep disturbance.

Specific Risks

Falls risk due to orthostatic dizziness, chronic pain, limited mobility, and bathroom/slip hazards.

Communication barriers due to hearing loss and language preferences can impact safety and understanding.

PTSD triggers (war, death, past trauma) can lead to agitation and distress.

High blood pressure episodes have required ambulance attendance in the past.

Incontinence and nocturia contribute to sleep disruption and fatigue, increasing falls risk.

No key lockbox and preference not to allow entry without me present may delay emergency access; mitigated by personal alarm and contacting Jenny.

Social isolation risk due to no longer driving; language barrier with taxis.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Primary Emergency Contact: Jenny (daughter and decision support). I prefer all contact to go to Jenny first if I do not answer the door for a scheduled visit.

Emergency Procedures for Workers: If I am unconscious or not breathing, perform resuscitation/first aid immediately, then call 000 (triple zero), then call Jenny.

Missed Visit / No Answer: Call Jenny to assist with contact and access.

Community Support: My neighbours are supportive and have previously assisted by calling Jenny and an ambulance when needed.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my home clean and safe so I feel calm and less anxious, with consistent support every Tuesday 10:00 AM–12:00 PM for the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I become anxious if workers rush or change frequently. I have high falls risk and chronic pain (8–9/10). Hearing loss requires clear, louder speech and one question at a time.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Domestic Assistance focusing on vacuuming, mopping, bathrooms/toilet, light dusting and kitchen surfaces. Workers will be calm, consistent and speak clearly. No heavy furniture moving.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Domestic Assistance team; I will guide priorities; Jenny will provide feedback to ensure continuity. When will it be done?: 2 hours weekly on Tuesdays 10:00 AM–12:00 PM for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 2 hours/week ≈ $170/week, $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will maintain my garden safely so it brings me joy without increasing my pain, with support every Tuesday 10:00 AM–12:00 PM for the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Limited mobility, falls risk, and chronic pain. I prefer to keep my current gardener if they meet onboarding requirements.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Light Home & Garden Maintenance (weeding, sweeping, basic tidy-ups). Salveo will onboard my current gardener once compliance documents are received, or provide a Salveo gardener if needed.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Gardening; I will set priorities; Care Partner will complete onboarding if using my current gardener. When will it be done?: 2 hours weekly on Tuesdays 10:00 AM–12:00 PM for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 2 hours/week ≈ $170/week, $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: I will improve my walking capacity from around 10 metres to at least 30–50 metres with my walker (with one seated rest if needed) and complete my home exercise program 5 days/week by the end of 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Chronic knee/back pain, falls risk, dizziness on standing, limited strength in legs and arms, bunions/flat feet. I prefer Mandarin/Cambodian-speaking clinicians and direct, calm communication.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Allied Health Physiotherapy 1 hour fortnightly for progressive lower limb strengthening, balance, sit-to-stand practice, gait training with walker, and pain pacing strategies; daily home exercises 5 days/week; rest breaks as needed.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Social Support/Transport with a Cambodian or Mandarin-speaking worker for door-to-door transport, escorting with rest breaks, and clear communication; use walker with seat; plan outings in quieter periods.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 5 Goal: I will maintain comfortable, healthy feet and prevent recurrence of plantar fasciitis by receiving podiatry at home about every 2 months and following footwear/orthotic advice over the next 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Bunions both feet, flat feet, previous plantar fasciitis, limited mobility. I prefer home visits to avoid difficult travel.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Arrange home podiatry through Salveo network; nail/callus care as needed; footwear/orthotic review; reinforce foot/ankle exercises linked to my physio plan.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Podiatry) via network; I will follow advice; Care Partner will schedule. Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded)

Care Plan

Care Alerts

  • I have an Advance Care Plan on file with Geelong Hospital; my family (children) hold Enduring Power of Attorney, with Stuart as my main point of contact.

  • I am hard of hearing in both ears (right worse following cancer removal) and I wear hearing aids; please speak slowly, clearly and a little louder.

  • I report occasional headaches (around 6/10) often triggered by stress or tension; I sometimes take a Panadol at night.

  • I experience prostate-related nocturia and may be up several times overnight.

  • I have a history of multiple skin cancer removals and prior radiation therapy in Geelong; I currently have a skin spot on my neck pending review.

  • I have no known allergies documented.

  • I am independent with mobility and do not routinely use aids; I had a past fall from a ladder—please discourage ladder use and arrange maintenance support for gutters/windows.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 1 September 2025

Preferred Name: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Full Name: Steve Irwin

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Interpreter required?: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

People involved in developing my care plan

  • I participated in this assessment and planning discussion.

  • Stuart is identified as my main point of contact and participated in decisions/discussions.

  • June contributed information during the discussion.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I do not have any specific cultural or diversity considerations for worker matching or service delivery at this time.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

  • Please speak slowly, clearly and a little louder due to my hearing impairment; face me when speaking and check I have heard key information.

  • I do not have a preference about worker age or background.

  • If I do not answer the door or phone as expected for a scheduled visit, please call Stuart.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

  • Stuart – primary contact (family).

  • June – spouse/partner.

  • Cynthia – neighbour across the road.

  • Friends: Julian Vyde and Graham Dawson.

Informal Supports

I have three children and eleven grandchildren who are important in my life and provide informal support and connection.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Hamilton and moved to Portland at about three years of age.

I grew up on farms and later lived on a dairy farm at Gray West, then a hobby farm before moving to my current home.

I worked for a builder and at the Meatworks (boning) for several years, later owning a small farm and then a dairy farm.

I experienced a significant financial loss from an investment, which affected our lives.

Interests

I enjoy walking, gardening, going out for a coffee and watching football (including watching my grandkids play).

Social interaction helps me a lot; nice weather and being outside improve my day.

My Medical Information

Medical History

Past hernia operation.

Radiation treatment in Geelong (five weeks).

Multiple skin cancer removals on the face and neck; right ear cancer removal contributing to hearing loss.

Prostate-related nocturia (getting up regularly at night).

No known allergies documented.

Medication

I am not taking prescribed medications.

I take multivitamins and will sometimes take a Panadol before bed.

Mobility and Equipment

I am independent with mobility and do not currently use walking aids.

I can get in and out of the car without assistance.

I have hearing aids in both ears.

There are old walking sticks available at home (not routinely used), and I previously used a gopher at the golf course.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr. Mayna (South Portland Medical Centre).

Pharmacy: South Portland Pharmacy.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD: No specific cultural factors identified, Living with disability (mobility): Independent mobility, no routine aids, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I can feel low or “depressed” when trapped indoors or less socially connected.)

Specific Risks

  • Hearing impairment may affect communication and safety if I do not hear instructions or alerts.

  • Occasional headaches (around 6/10) triggered by stress/tension; may limit activity on bad days.

  • Night-time toileting due to prostate symptoms increases fatigue; consider night-time safety (lighting, clear pathways).

  • Skin cancer history requires ongoing monitoring; there is a current neck spot to be reviewed.

  • Past fall from a ladder; home maintenance tasks (gutters/windows) present avoidable risk.

  • Low mood and isolation risk if weather prevents outdoor activity or if social contact reduces.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If I am found unresponsive or in a medical emergency, call Triple Zero (000) first, then contact Stuart.

If workers attend and I do not answer as expected, please ring Stuart.

I do not have a personal medical emergency plan documented, and my Advance Care Plan is held by Geelong Hospital. Copies of Enduring Power of Attorney may be requested; Stuart is my primary contact.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will stay socially connected and get out of the house regularly so I don’t feel “trapped indoors,” by having planned outings for coffee, to watch my grandkids’ football, or to visit friends from golf over the next 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with mobility and prefer being outdoors; bad weather and headaches can limit me. I am hard of hearing, so clear communication is needed when we’re out in the community.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Schedule Social Support visits for community access; choose destinations I enjoy (coffee, football, visiting friends).
