care_analyses.generated_html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

Key safety and health alerts: I live with severe breathlessness due to emphysema and can only walk about 10 metres before I need to stop and rest. I have a recent history of falls and over-correcting my balance. I have a history of depression and I was admitted to a mental health ward for three weeks about six months ago after a suicide attempt.

Resuscitation preference: I stated I do not want CPR. I understand there is no formal Not‑for‑Resuscitation (NFR/DNR) order in place at this time, and that paramedics will attempt resuscitation unless a valid order exists. Staff are to call 000 first, then call my son Darryl. Staff are not to perform CPR.

Emergency access: I do not have an emergency lockbox. If I do not answer the door for a scheduled visit, please call me first; if no response, call Darryl and follow emergency procedures.

Personal alarm: I prefer a pendant-style personal alarm and have agreed to purchase one ($567 one-off). I plan to put it on in the morning with my medications and remove it when I go to bed.

Mobility and equipment: A four-wheel walker has been recommended, but I currently do not use it because I find it exhausting to take in and out of the car and to use. I have handrails in the toilet, bathroom, shower and at the back door. I do not have a shower chair, raised toilet seat, or bed transfer pole.

Smoking risk: I have smoked for over 60 years and continue to smoke. I experience breathlessness, particularly after using the heater overnight.

Driving: I continue to drive short distances. My breathlessness and fatigue present a potential risk when driving, especially on “bad days.”

Living situation and psychosocial factors: I feel distressed about my wife being in permanent care and about conflict with two of my children. I rely heavily on my son Darryl for support. I am at risk of social isolation and low mood, particularly when thinking about my wife.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Preferred Name: Ian

Full Name: Ian

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan together with Thomas (Salveo Care) and my son Darryl, during the assessment meeting.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I reported no specific cultural factors for matching workers or delivering supports. I value being treated respectfully and being listened to as the “boss” of my own care. I remain devoted to my wife who is in permanent care and this is central to my values and daily wellbeing.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer clear, respectful communication. If I don’t answer the door at a scheduled time, please call me first; if no response, call my son Darryl and follow emergency procedures.

I have no preference for the gender or age of the support worker. I agreed to a regular social support time on Wednesdays from 12:00 pm to 2:30 pm (2.5 hours).

I do not currently have a lockbox; entry should be coordinated by phone if needed.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

My wife (in permanent aged care) remains the most important person in my life. My son Darryl is my primary support person and contact.

I also have friends and neighbours including Bruce and Anne (across the road), and others mentioned (Josie, Glen, Terri, Kevin, Lincoln, Bernie, and Robin).

Informal Supports

Darryl helps me with many tasks including pension matters, organising meals (Light & Easy), transport at times, and general day-to-day assistance. Neighbours and friends check in periodically. I am exploring local social groups and I enjoy brief, low-cost outings (e.g., pokies with a $20 limit).

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I grew up in Melbourne, near the zoo, with two brothers and three sisters. I worked in a malt house in Collingwood (James Hood & Company) when I was young. Later, I owned a laundromat in Noble Park for about 19–20 years and sold it about 1.5 years ago. I have three children and five grandchildren. I remain strongly connected to my wife who now lives in permanent care.

Interests

I used to love playing tennis and going for walks. I enjoy spending time with my dog Rambo (throwing the ball in the yard), occasional pokies outings with a strict $20 limit, listening to music (e.g., Johnny O’Keefe), and sometimes using an amusement machine. I follow Collingwood, though I have not been to games recently due to mobility and access issues.

My Medical Information

Medical History: Emphysema with severe breathlessness and low energy (can walk about 10 metres before resting); history of prostate cancer with radiation (circa 2007; stage 3–4); history of depression; brain aneurysm considered too high risk for surgery due to age; recent admission to a mental health ward for three weeks about six months ago after a suicide attempt; history of falls (including a backwards fall landing on my buttocks with a cut to my leg). Reported weight ~50 kg; height ~5’6”. No known medication allergies recorded in this assessment.

Medication: My medications are supplied in a Webster/blister pack by Chemist Warehouse. I take medications morning and night. I also use inhalers for my breathing (as discussed in context of “puffer”). I do not require staff assistance for daily medication administration.

Mobility and Equipment: My mobility is limited by breathlessness and fatigue. I can walk about 10 metres then need to stop. A four-wheel walker has been recommended but I am not using it. I have handrails in the toilet, bathroom, shower, and at the back door. I do not have a shower chair, raised toilet seat, or bed transfer pole. I continue to drive short distances.

GP / Pharmacy: GP: Dr Atul Desai (Forest Hill Medical Centre). Pharmacy: Chemist Warehouse, 415 Springvale Road, Forest Hill (noted that this may change if I move to Darryl’s home).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not documented as applicable.

Living with disability (mobility): Yes – significant mobility intolerance and breathlessness; short-distance ambulation only.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes – diagnosed depression, prior suicide attempt, grief about wife, social isolation risk.

Specific Risks

Falls risk due to breathlessness, fatigue and not using a recommended walker; recent falls reported.

Respiratory risk due to emphysema and smoking; difficulty breathing after leaving the heater on overnight.

Suicide/self-harm risk (historical) with ongoing grief triggers (thinking about my wife).

Emergency readiness risk – currently no lockbox and no formal emergency kit; pendant alarm being purchased to mitigate risk.

Driving risk – I continue to drive short distances; breathlessness and fatigue may impact safety, especially on “bad days.”

Social isolation risk – low motivation on “bad days”; limited community engagement; conflict within family is distressing.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Primary emergency contact: Darryl (son) – call after 000 in medical emergencies, and if I do not respond at a scheduled visit.

If I do not answer for a scheduled visit: Call me first. If there is no response, call Darryl. Escalate to emergency services if you are concerned for my safety.

Medical emergency while staff are present: Do not perform CPR. Call 000 immediately and then call Darryl. I understand that without a formal DNR/NFR, paramedics will attempt resuscitation.

Evacuation/disaster planning: I do not have an emergency kit or plan. I would need full assistance in an emergency.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will have regular social support each week on Wednesdays (12:00 pm–2:30 pm, 2.5 hours) so I can visit my wife, attend a local social activity or the pokies (with my $20 limit), or have companionship at home to reduce isolation and improve my mood over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I get breathless and fatigued quickly and can only walk about 10 metres at a time. I have had recent falls and a history of depression with low motivation on “bad days.”

How will we do this? (Tasks): A Salveo support worker will attend weekly for 2.5 hours to provide social support and escorted transport as required (driving if needed, $1.40/km). We will use this time to visit my wife, go to a social group or the pokies, or provide companionship and light support in-home. We will track my attendance and note my mood before/after sessions.

Who is responsible?: Me, supported by Salveo HomeCare social support workers and Darryl. When will it be done?: Weekly for the next 3 months (13 weeks). How much will it cost?: Social Support $85/hour x 2.5 hours/week ≈ $212.50/week ≈ $850/month (plus $1.40/km if transport is used).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 2 Goal: I will maintain safe access to help in an emergency by wearing a pendant personal alarm every day (on in the morning with my medications, off at bedtime), and I will complete a monthly test call over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I live with falls risk and limited emergency readiness. I prefer a neck-worn pendant alarm and understand I must wear it consistently for it to help.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Purchase a pendant alarm ($567 one-off). I will wear it daily and perform a test once per month. During one social support visit each month, the worker will prompt me to test the alarm and review my emergency instructions (within my existing weekly 2.5-hour support time).

Who is responsible?: Me, with help from Salveo HomeCare (for ordering and monthly test prompts) and Darryl. When will it be done?: Purchase within 2 weeks; then daily wearing and monthly testing for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Personal alarm $567 one-off; staff prompts included within Goal 1 Social Support (no additional hourly cost beyond $850/month).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: I will keep my garden and lawns safely maintained to reduce trip hazards and make my home look lived-in (security) by having monthly lawn mowing/maintenance for the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot manage physical tasks due to breathlessness and fatigue. An untidy garden may increase falls risk and security concerns if I am away.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo to provide Light Home & Gardening Maintenance for mowing and basic yard upkeep monthly (about 1 hour) and adjust tasks to address hazards (e.g., path edges, debris).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare gardening staff. When will it be done?: Monthly for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Light Home & Gardening Maintenance $85/hour, ≈ $85/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will complete an Occupational Therapy (OT) home and mobility assessment to review the suitability of a lightweight 4‑wheel walker, wheelchair for outings (e.g., footy), and any small aids (e.g., shower chair) within the next 3 months (or at my new address if I move to Darryl’s).

Care Plan

Care Alerts

I live with Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). My MS symptoms are aggravated by heat, humidity and stress. On bad days I can feel weak, fatigued or off-balance.

I have a personal alarm (Live Life), currently paid via direct invoice/texts. I want the provider to take over payment once invoices are provided.

I do not have an emergency plan or kit. I prefer that in a medical emergency you call an ambulance (000) first and then call Samantha. I expressed a preference to not be resuscitated, but I do not have any formal advance care directive/DNR on file. Treat me as for full resuscitation unless a valid directive is supplied.

I have limited local supports. If there is no response during a scheduled visit, attempt to contact me and Samantha and escalate to 000 if you are concerned for my safety.

I have dogs at home (a boxer and a staffy). Workers must be dog-friendly and comfortable entering with dogs present.

I can mumble at times and cognition/memory can be an issue. Please speak clearly and check my understanding.

Key access: I do not use a key lock box and currently use an informal method stored at the meter box. This is less secure; handle access sensitively and do not disclose details beyond what is necessary for service delivery.

Cultural considerations: I identify as Jewish. Please avoid political or religious debate and be respectful of my identity.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 02 September 2025

Preferred Name: Graham

Full Name: Graham Knox

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan together with my care partner and my daughter, Samantha. I agreed to the goals and service schedule described below.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I identify as Jewish. I value humour, I dislike confrontation, and family is important to me. I prefer workers who are respectful and avoid political or religious debates. I do not practice a particular religion day-to-day.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I can mumble and my memory can be patchy. Please speak slowly, clearly and check that I’ve understood. I do not need an interpreter.

I have two dogs (boxer and staffy). Workers must be dog-friendly and comfortable with dogs in the home.

I prefer routine times for services: Thursdays 11:00–13:00 for cleaning and gardening; Tuesdays 11:00–13:00 for monthly shopping support.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Samantha (my daughter) is my main support person and emergency contact.

Informal Supports

I currently attend a social group at Bayside Care and Support (Leader Road) on Mondays and Wednesdays. The entry cost is $50 per session. I plan to continue attending twice weekly. I will provide invoices so the provider can pay the fees as arranged.

Outside of Samantha and my social group, I do not rely on local neighbours or other informal supports.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Australia and grew up in Sydney. In my 20s, I worked overseas as a tour guide for about four years, which was a highlight in my life. I have three children and became single in my 30s. I used to enjoy surfing, golf, and skiing.

Interests

I enjoy time with my family, my dogs, and attending my social group. A good day is when I wake without aches and can get on with what I want. A bad day is when I wake feeling exhausted. Rest, keeping cool, and reducing stress help me have more good days.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

I live with Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). I had a major episode about eight years ago, was found unconscious, and spent three weeks in critical care before moving to live with Samantha. I’ve had minor MS flare-ups since. I recently had pre-cancerous skin changes removed from my scalp/head. I am awaiting a cognition assessment (appointment pending). I have no known allergies.

Medication:

I take prescribed medications and manage them independently. I do not currently require assistance with medications, injections, patches or blood sugar monitoring. A medication plan/list can be provided on request.

Mobility and Equipment:

My mobility is independent without aids. I have an electric recliner chair and a personal alarm (Live Life). I do not have rails or bathroom equipment. I had a fall approximately 18 months ago; no significant injury reported.

GP / Pharmacy:

My GP is Dr Chris Sherman, Armadale Family Clinic (High Street, Armadale).

My pharmacy is Chemist Warehouse, Glenferrie Road, Malvern (around 120–128 Glenferrie Road).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not documented as CALD; I identify as Jewish.

Living with disability (mobility): I live with MS; mobility is currently independent. Heat/humidity/stress can worsen symptoms (weakness, vertigo-like feelings, fatigue).

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I report low maintenance mood and benefit from social group attendance twice weekly. Stress exacerbates symptoms; limited local supports may increase risk during emergencies.

Specific Risks

  • MS exacerbation triggered by heat, humidity and stress.
  • Falls risk (history of fall ~18 months ago) and potential balance issues during flares.
  • Emergency readiness gap: no key safe, no emergency plan or kit, limited local supports.
  • Communication: I can mumble; risk of miscommunication without clear speech and confirmation.
  • Dogs on premises; ensure safe entry procedures.
  • Personal alarm subscription continuity depends on provider receiving invoices.
  • Preference to avoid resuscitation without a formal directive on file; treat as full code until documentation is provided.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

In a medical emergency while services are being provided: call 000 (ambulance) immediately, then call Samantha (my daughter). I do not have a formal resuscitation directive; treat me as full code unless a valid directive is supplied.

If I do not answer the door for a scheduled visit: attempt to contact me and Samantha, and if you are concerned for my safety, call 000 for a welfare check.

Emergency contact details (phone/email): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my home clean, safe and manageable so I can live comfortably and reduce falls risk.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with mobility. My MS can flare with heat/stress, which can make me tired and off-balance. I prefer routine times for service and dog-friendly workers.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo workers will mop floors, clean bathrooms, wipe kitchen surfaces, change my bed linen weekly, and keep walkways free of clutter.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker | When will it be done?: 2 hours every Thursday 11:00–13:00 for the next 12 weeks | How much will it cost?: Domestic Assistance $85/hour, 2 hours weekly = $680/month (approx. $2,040/quarter).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will maintain and improve my balance and mobility affected by MS so I can walk safely and reduce near-falls.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Independent ambulation; heat/humidity/stress worsen symptoms. I respond well to routine.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Weekly physiotherapy to complete a progressive balance/strength program, gait training, and pacing strategies for hot days. Track outcomes using a Timed Up & Go (TUG) and near-fall diary.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Allied Health Therapist (Physiotherapist) | When will it be done?: 1 hour weekly for 12 weeks | How much will it cost?: $180/hour, $720/month (approx. $2,160/quarter). Target measures: reduce near-falls to 0/month; improve TUG by ≥2 seconds; walk 10 minutes on cool days without rest by end of quarter.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 3 Goal: I will keep my feet healthy and my thickened nails managed to prevent pain and falls.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Thickened nails; I currently do not see a podiatrist regularly.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Quarterly podiatry visit for nail cutting, skin/pressure assessment and footwear advice; escalate issues to GP if identified.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Allied Health – Podiatry (or contracted provider) | When will it be done?: 1 hour once this quarter | How much will it cost?: $180/hour, $180/quarter (average $60/month).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 4 Goal: I will complete my grocery and essential shopping each month so I don’t run out of staples and feel stressed.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent but benefit from support with errands. Heat and long outings can fatigue me.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Plan a shopping list in advance, transport to/from shops, complete shopping within 2 hours, unpack essentials, and ensure pantry staples are stocked.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker | When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly on Tuesdays 11:00–13:00 | How much will it cost?: Social Support $85/hour, $170/month (plus $1.40/km for transport as required; kms charged as incurred). Success measure: 0 stock-outs of key staples over the quarter.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 5 Goal: I will keep my garden and external walkways tidy to reduce trip hazards and feel proud of my home.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Falls risk increases with outdoor clutter or long grass.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Mow/trim as needed, clear paths and steps, remove green waste, and check lighting at entry points.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Home & Garden Maintenance worker | When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly on Thursdays 11:00–13:00 | How much will it cost?: Light Home & Gardening Maintenance $85/hour, $170/month (approx. $510/quarter). Outcome: walkways clear after each visit; no outdoor trip hazards.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 6 Goal: I will be emergency ready by setting up a simple plan and ensuring my personal alarm is active.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I currently have no emergency plan or kit and limited local supports. I prefer not to install a key safe at this time.

How will we do this? (Tasks): One dedicated session to co-create a one-page emergency plan (who to call, order of calls, medications list), prepare a fridge magnet, confirm my preferences, update my Live Life personal alarm account so invoices go to Salveo for payment, and discuss safe access options.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Care Partner/support worker (with me and Samantha) | When will it be done?: One 1-hour session this quarter | How much will it cost?: Social Support $85 for the session this quarter (+ personal alarm subscription cost: Not documented; to be paid on receipt of invoice).

Service Category: Independence Support

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded)

  • Allied Health Therapy – Physiotherapy: 1 hour weekly @ $180/hour = $720/month; approx. $2,160/quarter.
  • Allied Health – Podiatry: 1 hour per quarter @ $180/hour = $180/quarter (average $60/month).

Service Category: Independence Support

  • Social Support (Shopping): 2 hours monthly @ $85/hour = $170/month; approx. $510/quarter + $1.40/km transport (as incurred).
  • Social Participation – Bayside Care and Support group fees: $50 per session, Mondays and Wednesdays (approx. 2 sessions/week). Estimated 24 sessions/quarter = ~$1,200/quarter. Payment to be made on invoice.
  • Emergency Readiness session: 1 hour this quarter @ $85 = $85/quarter.

Service Category: Everyday Living

  • Domestic Assistance (cleaning, linen): 2 hours weekly @ $85/hour = $680/month; approx. $2,040/quarter.
  • Light Home & Gardening Maintenance: 2 hours monthly @ $85/hour = $170/month; approx. $510/quarter.
  • Personal alarm subscription (Live Life): Not documented; to be added upon receipt of invoice.

Quarterly Budget Allocation (estimated, excluding kms and any undisclosed subscription amounts)

  • Clinical Care: ~$2,160 + $180 = ~$2,340/quarter
  • Independence Support: ~$510 + $1,200 + $85 = ~$1,795/quarter (+ kms as incurred)
  • Everyday Living: ~$2,040 + $510 = ~$2,550/quarter
  • Estimated Total (known items): ~$6,685/quarter (plus km charges and personal alarm subscription once known)

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I have participated in developing this care plan and agree with the goals, services, and risk mitigations described. I consent to Salveo HomeCare coordinating and delivering my services under the Support at Home Program.

Copies to: Me (Graham Knox) and Samantha (my daughter). GP may receive a copy on my request.

Prepared By

Name: __________ | Role: Care Partner | Date: Today (02 September 2025) | Review Date: Quarterly (every 3 months) | Signature: __________

Transcript Summary – Graham Knox (map to Standards 1–8)

Standard 1 – Consumer dignity and choice: I stated my values (humour, family, no confrontation) and identity (Jewish). I chose dog-friendly workers, routine times, and to avoid a key safe for now. My resuscitation preference was documented with clarification about lack of a formal directive.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers: I co-designed this quarterly plan with my care partner and Samantha. It captures my MS history, triggers (heat, humidity, stress), risks (falls, limited supports), and SMARTA goals. Reviews are set quarterly.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care: My clinical needs are addressed via weekly physiotherapy and quarterly podiatry. I self-manage medications and will provide lists if requested. My GP and pharmacy are identified.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living: I will receive Domestic Assistance weekly, monthly shopping support with transport as needed, and monthly garden maintenance. My social participation at Bayside Care and Support will be funded as arranged.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment: Workers will be dog-friendly, communicate clearly, and respect my preferences. Entry will be managed safely given the dogs and current key access approach.

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance: I understand I can provide feedback or complaints at any time. Qualified personnel (support workers, allied health) will deliver services. Budgeting reflects the Support at Home quarterly cycle and categories, with transparency about km charges and pending subscription costs.

Dignity of Risk Assessment (Narrative + Table)

I understand that living at home with MS involves risks, especially during heat, humidity, and stressful periods. I have chosen not to install a key safe at this time and to continue using my current access method. I prefer not to be resuscitated but do not have a formal directive yet. I am awaiting a cognition assessment; I notice my memory has declined. I can sometimes be hard to understand as I mumble, and cognition can be an issue on some days.

I live with my daughter Samantha. I have limited local supports to rely on during emergencies.

I use a personal alarm (Live Life). I currently do not have a key safe and keep access arrangements informal; I understand this is less secure.

I prefer not to be resuscitated, but I do not have a formal Advance Care Directive/DNAR in place. In an emergency I want an ambulance called first, then contact Samantha. I understand emergency responders will follow legal requirements.

I have no known allergies. I am independent with mobility and activities of daily living. I have two large dogs in the home; workers must be dog-friendly and mindful of trip hazards.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 2 September 2025

Preferred Name: Graham

Full Name: Graham Knox

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

  • Me – Graham Knox (consumer)

  • Samantha (my daughter and primary support person, I live with her)

  • Care Partner (assessment interviewer)

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I identify as Jewish and a Zionist. I speak English and do not require an interpreter. I value humour, I do not like confrontation, and family contact is important to me. I do not practice a particular religion and I do not have specific spiritual care needs. I prefer care staff who are respectful and avoid political or religious debates.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

  • Workers must be dog-friendly. I have two large dogs (a boxer and a staffy) inside the home.

  • Please speak clearly and at a normal pace; I can mumble and cognition can be an issue at times.

  • Schedule preferences agreed in assessment: Domestic Assistance weekly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00; Shopping support monthly on Tuesdays around 11:00–13:00; Gardening monthly coordinated around Thursday 11:00–13:00 where possible.

  • Be mindful of heat sensitivity; morning/midday visits are preferred in summer and ensure I can keep cool.

  • Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

  • Samantha – my daughter (primary contact)

  • My brother

  • A friend in the city (college friend)

  • Members of my social group at Leader Road (Bayside Care and Support)

Informal Supports

I live with my daughter Samantha who provides informal support as needed. I currently do not rely on neighbours or other local supports in emergencies.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Australia and grew up in Sydney. In my twenties I worked overseas as a tour guide for four years, which was a pinnacle time in my life. I returned to Australia, had three children, became single in my thirties, taught for a number of years, and did various jobs. I enjoy the mountains and have skied in the past.

Interests

I enjoy contact with my family (many are overseas), attending my social group, spending time with my two dogs, watching TV, and keeping life low-stress. I previously enjoyed surfing and golf but no longer do these activities.

My Medical Information

Medical History: Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). MS flare-ups have been mostly minor in recent years. A major episode about eight years ago resulted in hospitalisation in critical care for three weeks; I moved to live with Samantha afterwards. Precancerous skin lesion removed from my head (recent). Awaiting cognition assessment; I notice some memory decline. No known allergies.

Medication: I take prescribed medications and manage them independently. I do not require assistance with injections, patches, or blood sugar monitoring. I report no ongoing pain medication needs.

Mobility and Equipment: I mobilise independently without aids. Last recorded fall was approximately 18 months ago; no major injury reported. I use a personal alarm (Live Life) and have an electric recliner chair. I do not have rails or shower equipment installed. Heat and humidity exacerbate MS symptoms (vertigo/weakness).

GP / Pharmacy: GP – Dr Chris Sherman, Armidale Family Clinic. Pharmacy – Chemist Warehouse on Glenfrew/Glenferrie Road, Malvern (around 120–128). Contact details not documented.

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: I identify as Jewish; I am English-speaking and do not require an interpreter.

Living with disability (mobility): I live with MS; I am currently independent with mobility but experience intermittent vertigo/weakness in heat. Last fall approx. 18 months ago.

Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have severe breathlessness from emphysema and can often only walk about 10 metres before I need to stop and rest.

I have a history of depression and was admitted to a mental health ward for three weeks about six months ago following a suicide attempt.

I have expressed a clear preference for “no resuscitation/CPR,” however I do not currently have a formal DNR/Advance Care Directive in place. I understand ambulance officers must commence resuscitation unless a valid directive is available.

I am at risk of falls and have had recent falls (“went backwards and landed on my arse,” with a cut to my leg).

I am currently not using my recommended four-wheel walker as I feel it uses too much of my energy.

I prefer and have agreed to a pendant-style personal alarm to be purchased (one-off $567) and worn daily once supplied.

I smoke and will step outside to do so.

I live with a small dog (Rambo) who may be excited when people arrive.

If a care worker arrives and I do not answer, I want them to call me first, then call my son Darryl, and if concerned for my safety, call 000.

care_analyses.generated_html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

Allergies: I have no known allergies.

Primary health condition: I live with Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). Heat, humidity and stress aggravate my MS symptoms (e.g., weakness, vertigo-like sensations). I pace myself and rest to avoid flare-ups.

Cognition: I am awaiting a cognition assessment; I have noticed increasing forgetfulness. Please speak clearly and give me time to respond.

Emergency preferences: In a medical emergency, call 000 (ambulance) first, then contact Samantha (my daughter). I have expressed that I do not want resuscitation; however, I do not have a formal Advance Care Directive/DNR. Paramedics will follow clinical protocols.

Falls: I have a history of falls, last reported around 18 months ago, without major injury.

Personal alarm: I have a Live Life personal alarm; I am not using it often but may need help with payments/top-ups as invoices arrive.

Access and pets: I have dogs in the home and prefer dog-friendly workers.

Home access: I do not have a key lock box. I currently use an insecure workaround for access.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 2 September 2025

Preferred Name: Graham

Full Name: Graham Knox

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Interpreter required?: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this care plan together with my care partner and my daughter, Samantha, during the assessment conversation.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I describe myself as a typical Aussie bloke. I identify as Jewish and as a Zionist culturally, though I do not actively practice a religion.

Humour matters to me. I avoid confrontation. Family is important to me.

Please be respectful and avoid political or religious debates during visits.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I can mumble and sometimes be hard to understand. Please speak clearly, at a normal pace, and check back for understanding.

I prefer dog-friendly workers as my dogs are part of my home life.

I feel worse in hot, humid weather. Where possible, please schedule services during cooler parts of the day and help me keep cool and reduce stress.

I prefer the following service times discussed in the assessment: Domestic Assistance weekly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00; Light Home & Gardening Maintenance monthly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00; Shopping Social Support monthly on Tuesdays around 11:00–13:00.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

Samantha (my daughter) is my primary support and contact person.

I have friends through my social group and a friend in the city I went to college with.

I do not rely on neighbours for support.

Informal Supports

I live with Samantha and receive day-to-day support from her as needed.

I attend a social group two days per week (Mondays and Wednesdays) at Leader Road through Bayside Care and Support (entry fee noted below).

My dogs are important companions for me.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Australia and grew up in Sydney. I worked overseas as a tour guide for about four years, which was a pinnacle time in my life. I later taught for a number of years and did other jobs in between.

I have three children and became single in my thirties. About eight years ago, after a major health episode, I moved to live with Samantha.

I have enjoyed skiing and previously surfed and played golf.

Interests

I enjoy contact with family (many are overseas), attending my social group, watching AFL, and spending time with my dogs.

A good day is when I have no aches and can just get on with what I want to do. A bad day is when I wake up feeling unwell or when it is hot and humid. Rest helps me have more good days. Heat and stress aggravate my MS symptoms; staying cool and reducing stress helps.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

I have Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). I experience minor flare-ups and had a major episode about eight years ago, when I was found unconscious and admitted to critical care for three weeks. I have had pre-cancerous lesions removed from my scalp/head.

I have no known allergies or medical alerts.

I report no ongoing pain and no breathing issues.

Medication:

I take prescribed medications and manage them independently. I report having a medication plan in place and do not need assistance with medications, injections, patches, or blood sugar monitoring.

Mobility and Equipment:

My mobility is independent and I do not use a walking aid. I can get in and out of a car. I have an electric recliner chair and a Live Life personal alarm. I do not have rails, shower chairs, or a key lock box.

GP / Pharmacy:

My GP is Dr Chris Sherman at the Armidale Family Clinic.

My pharmacy is Chemist Warehouse on Glenferrie Road, Malvern.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: I identify as Jewish but I do not require an interpreter (English-speaking).

Living with disability (mobility): I live with MS; I currently mobilise independently.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I have limited local supports and rely on my social group; heat and stress can worsen my MS symptoms.

Specific Risks

Heat, humidity, and stress exacerbate my MS symptoms.

I do not have a formal emergency plan or kit and would need full assistance in an emergency.

I do not have a key lock box and use an insecure access workaround.

I have a history of falls (last around 18 months ago, no major injury).

I have verbally expressed a wish not to be resuscitated but do not have a formal Advance Care Directive/DNR.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

In an emergency during service delivery: call 000 for an ambulance first. After calling 000, please contact Samantha (my daughter). Contact details are not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

If a scheduled visit occurs and there is no response at the door: please call my phone first. If there is still no response, contact Samantha. If you have immediate concerns for my safety, call 000. I do not have a key lock box.

My personal alarm is with Live Life; invoices may be texted to me. The provider can assist with payments once invoice details are supplied.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my home clean and comfortable so I can “just get on with my day” without fatigue from housework.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I live with MS; heat and stress aggravate symptoms. I am independent with mobility but benefit from conserving energy.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare to provide Domestic Assistance for vacuuming, mopping, bathroom clean, bed linen change, and general tidy.

Who is responsible?: Salveo support worker and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours weekly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00, for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour = $170/week, approximately $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will shop safely and efficiently once a month so my pantry and fridge are stocked and I can eat well.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I manage well on cooler days; heat and stress worsen MS. I prefer mornings/late morning.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare to provide Social Support (shopping assistance, list planning, carrying groceries, and transport if needed).

Who is responsible?: Salveo support worker and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly on Tuesdays around 11:00–13:00, for the next 3 months. How much will it be cost?: $85/hour = $170/month, plus mileage at $1.40/km as incurred.

Who is responsible?: Salveo gardener and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00, for the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: $85/hour = $170/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will maintain my balance and strength to stay independent with walking and reduce fall risk.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I live with MS; heat and stress aggravate symptoms. I am currently independently mobile.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will receive Physiotherapy with an Allied Health Therapist (Salveo) for assessment and a home exercise program. Service Category: Clinical Care

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have thickened toenails; no current wounds.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Podiatry (Allied Health) for nail care, skin integrity check, and foot health education.

The meeting transcript documents a comprehensive home care package assessment conducted by a Salvo Care representative with Kate, an elderly client who recently broke her ankle and had surgery. The assessment covers Kate's personal information, medical history, care needs, and service preferences to establish a tailored home care package. 
The Salvo Care representative begins by collecting Kate's personal information and discussing her cultural preferences and values. Kate identifies family, independence, and integrity/manners as her core values. When asked about cultural preferences for workers, Kate indicates she has no specific requirements, though the representative explains that some clients do have preferences based on cultural or religious backgrounds. 
The assessment includes a thorough review of Kate's medical history, which includes heart surgery with a pig valve replacement in 2014, hip replacement in 2015, and recent ankle surgery in March where plates were inserted after a fall at home. Kate describes herself as independent and mentions she's recovering well from her ankle surgery, though she can no longer kneel or garden, which she misses. 
Kate's family support network is discussed, with her son Stuart identified as her primary contact and enduring power of attorney. She also has another son named Russell. The representative confirms Kate has a personal alarm system and discusses emergency procedures, including her preference for a "Do Not Resuscitate" status, though she doesn't currently have legal documentation for this. 
The assessment covers Kate's daily routines, what constitutes good and bad days for her, and her current capabilities. Kate expresses that she worries frequently but generally manages well on her own. She can perform most personal care tasks independently but needs assistance with tasks requiring kneeling or bending. 
Kate shares details about her life history, including her childhood memories of her father returning from war, her career in dressmaking and fashion, her marriage and children, and her volunteer work after retirement. Her hobbies include crafts like crocheting and knitting. 
The representative and Kate discuss and agree on a service plan that includes: 
•	Physiotherapy: One hour fortnightly on Wednesday afternoons 
•	Podiatry: Eight times per year 
•	Domestic assistance: 1.5 hours fortnightly on Tuesdays at 10 AM 
•	Social support/shopping: Two hours fortnightly on Tuesdays (alternating with domestic assistance) 
•	Gardening: Two hours monthly 
•	Home maintenance: Three hours twice yearly for windows, gutters, and air conditioning units 
The meeting concludes with the representative confirming the service schedule and explaining that Kate has significant remaining budget ($12,000) that could be used for additional services if needed in the future.

The representative emphasizes that Kate should feel comfortable and safe in her own home, and they will try to match her with appropriate workers.

The representative reviews Kate's rights under the Aid Care Act, including her right to safe and high-quality care, to be treated with dignity and respect, to have her identity and culture valued, to live without abuse and neglect, to be informed about her care, to have control over her care choices, to have her privacy protected, and to complain without reprisal. Kate acknowledges these rights and confirms that her son Stuart should be involved in her care. The representative obtains Kate's consent for various aspects of care, including having third parties present during services, participating in auditing activities, and allowing Salvo Care to contact her GP for medical information.

The representative collects Kate's personal information, including her primary contact (son Stuart) and secondary contact (son Russell). They discuss Kate's medical practitioner (Dr. Nam) and pharmacy (Advantage in Lakeside). Kate mentions she has a personal alarm system but can't recall the brand name. The representative asks about emergency plans and local support in case of disasters or medical emergencies. Kate identifies her neighbor Brian as potential local support but primarily relies on her son Stuart in emergencies.

The representative discusses Kate's preferences in case of a medical emergency. Kate states she would want them to call an ambulance first and then contact her son Stuart. Kate explains that she worries about many things but generally manages well on her own. She mentions that being able to do her craft again and drive her car are working well for her currently, while not being able to kneel down is a challenge.

She describes her education and career path, starting with dressmaking at prestigious establishments in Melbourne, including working for French designers making high-end clothing. I have a personal alarm system in place (brand not recalled). I will advise when the subscription renewal is due so it can be paid through my package if appropriate.

I have expressed a preference not to be resuscitated if the outcome would leave me with no meaningful quality of life; I currently have no formal DNR documentation. In an emergency, my instruction is to call an ambulance first and then call my son Stuart.

Allergies: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 2 September 2025

Preferred Name: Kate

Full Name: Kate Weston

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I participated in this assessment and agreed to the supports described. My son Stuart (Enduring Power of Attorney) is my primary contact and is to be involved in my care. The Salveo HomeCare Care Partner conducted the assessment. My Monash Health case manager (Ellie Erskine) may be consulted as needed. My GP (Dr. Nam) may be contacted for medical information with my consent.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I value family, independence, and integrity/manners. I want to feel comfortable and safe in my home. I have no specific cultural or religious preferences for workers.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I like to get to know new people before receiving services. I prefer a female worker for shopping and social support, ideally someone with more life experience. I have no gender preference for cleaning. I prefer continuity, with the same worker attending where possible.

I agreed to the following schedule: Domestic Assistance 1.5 hours fortnightly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM (starting 19 September, 10:00–11:30). Social support/shopping two hours fortnightly on alternate Tuesdays (starting 25 September). Physiotherapy one hour fortnightly on Wednesdays from 1:00–2:00 PM (start date dependent on therapist availability). Gardening two hours monthly. Home maintenance three hours twice yearly for windows, gutters and air-conditioning units.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Primary contact: My son, Stuart Weston (Enduring Power of Attorney).

Secondary contact: My son, Russell Weston.

Other important people: Daughters-in-law Monique and Linda; granddaughter Amelia; grandsons Jared and Aaron; my neighbor Brian; my Monash Health case manager, Ellie Erskine.

I self-manage my medications and daily routines. My neighbor Brian can assist locally if needed. I rely primarily on my son Stuart in emergencies. I use a personal alarm system.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

My first memory is my father returning from war. I trained and worked in dressmaking and fashion in Melbourne, including high-end work with French designers. I married and had two sons and later divorced after 13 years. I worked in a factory making pillows and cushions until age 62 when the factory closed. After retirement I volunteered teaching crafts and helping with community outings.

Interests

I enjoy crafts such as crocheting and knitting, and I watch television. I avoid competitive reality shows because I dislike seeing people being unkind to each other. I used to enjoy gardening but I can no longer kneel, which I miss.

My Medical Information

Medical History: Open heart surgery with a pig valve replacement in 2014; hip replacement in 2015; ankle surgery with plates inserted in March after a fall at home; kidney stones removed many years ago. I am recovering well from my ankle surgery but occasionally experience twinges of pain.

Medication: I take my medications every morning. Specific medication names and doses are not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Mobility and Equipment: I use a walking stick outside but not inside. I cannot kneel and I avoid bending where possible. I have shower handrails and a non-slip mat. I have a personal alarm system.

GP / Pharmacy: My GP is Dr. Nam. My pharmacy is Advantage Pharmacy in Lakeside.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not identified.

Living with disability (mobility): Yes – recovering from ankle surgery; cannot kneel; uses a walking stick outside.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I worry frequently and many friends have died or moved away; I generally manage well but there is a mild risk of isolation or low mood.

Interests

I enjoy walking to the local shops for coffee most days and socialising. I used to paint (I have many paintings) but have stopped due to shaky hands. I have an interest in antiques and antiquities. I have a cat named Charlie.

My Medical Information

Medical History

Past car accident approximately eight years ago.

History of depression, including past suicidal ideation and being detained for safety more than five years ago; no recent events reported.

No recent hospital admissions reported. Not recently assessed for dementia/cognitive impairment.

No allergies or special dietary requirements reported.

Medication

I receive Webster-packed medicines from Chemist Warehouse and take them independently. I do not require assistance with medication, blood sugar monitoring, injections, or patches at this time.

Mobility and Equipment

I describe my mobility as independent. I occasionally use walking sticks. I have small hand weights at home. I have a personal alarm. I report no recent falls. I sometimes find getting into small taxis more difficult than in the past.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Isham, My Health Medical Centre, 28 Beach Street, Frankston.

Pharmacy: Chemist Warehouse (provider of Webster packs).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No – I speak English as my first language and identify as Christian.

Living with disability (mobility): Mild – I am independent but sometimes use walking sticks and find car ingress/egress harder than before.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes – I report a history of depression with past suicidal ideation over five years ago; I currently manage by staying active, keeping social contact, and engaging with my children.

Specific Risks

Hearing impairment (right ear) may affect communication and safety in the community.

History of depression with past suicidal ideation; current risk appears low but requires routine monitoring and prompt escalation if concerns arise.

Daily walks/coffee outings: risk of trip/fall or traffic hazards.

Spare key stored above door for worker access increases security exposure.

Firm preference to exclude Peninsula Health from care/referrals could limit local service options.

Use of taxis (CabCharge) for transport: potential risk when transferring in/out of vehicles.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Emergency actions: Perform CPR, call triple zero (000), and notify my family.

Access if no answer: Use spare key kept on the ledge above the door to enter and check on me.

Primary contact: Ben Switzer (son) – 0419 782 414.

Secondary contact: Beata Shields (daughter) – 0401 338 961.

Other: I have a personal alarm. I do not want Peninsula Health involved in my care.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my unit clean and comfortable so I can enjoy my days, with help on Wednesdays and Fridays for floors, bathroom, and weekly linen changes.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent but prefer help with heavier cleaning tasks. I am hard of hearing in my right ear, so clear communication helps. Security access via spare key is agreed if I don’t answer.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Domestic Assistance for vacuuming/mopping floors, cleaning the bathroom, changing and washing bed linen weekly, and coordinating pick-up/return of my external laundry service (Wettleswood).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Support Worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour Wednesday and 1 hour Friday starting 11:00 a.m. each week (for 3 months). How much will it cost?: $85/hour; 2 hours/week ≈ 8 hours/month = $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will get out for coffee and a chat twice a week after cleaning so I stay connected and feel less isolated.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I walk independently to local shops. I have a history of low mood; regular social contact helps. I use taxis when needed.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Social Support for companionship and local coffee outings after cleaning on Wednesdays and Fridays. Transport during the outing will be included as needed, with km charges as incurred.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Support Worker and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours Wednesday and 2 hours Friday from ~12:00 p.m. (for 3 months). How much will it cost?: Social Support $85/hour; 4 hours/week ≈ 16 hours/month = $1,360/month (+ $1.40/km if transport used).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: I will have about 10 prepared meals available each week so I eat well and have the energy to keep walking to the shops for coffee.

Abilities and considerations (risks): No special diet; I prefer medium-sized meals. I manage my own eating and heating of meals.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will coordinate meal delivery (Dynamic). I will order approximately 10 meals/week. I will store/freeze meals as needed and heat safely.

Who is responsible?: Me with Salveo HomeCare coordination. When will it be done?: Weekly ordering and deliveries for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Budget approx. $100/week total with a 70%/30% split (package approx. $70/week ≈ $280/month; my contribution approx. $30/week ≈ $120/month).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will maintain my strength and mobility so I can keep living independently and manage taxis and transfers safely.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with occasional use of walking sticks and find car ingress/egress a bit harder than before. No recent falls.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will arrange an Allied Health Therapist (Physiotherapist) initial assessment (2 hours), then provide 1-hour physiotherapy sessions fortnightly. I will participate in sessions and follow guidance as agreed with the therapist.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Physio) and me. When will it be done?: Initial 2-hour assessment in Month 1; then 1 hour fortnightly for 3 months. Service Category: Clinical Care

Abilities and considerations (risks): I walk independently and sometimes use walking sticks. I want to prevent falls and keep my independence.

risks.description: Limited mobility; uses walker frame; unsafe with walking sticks; cannot stand for long; no recent falls; prefers lower vehicles for transfers.
Osteoarthritis pain constant around 5/10 with flares to 10/10; heat worsens pain.
Atrial fibrillation with shortness of breath.
Type 2 diabetes; self-manages and sees an educator.
Lymphedema and occasional skin ulcers; uses DME skin products.
Hearing difficulties; requires workers to speak clearly and loudly.
Barrett’s esophagus; episodes of digestive upset requiring frequent toileting.
Does not want resuscitation during care; prefers staff to call 000 and notify family; no emergency kit prepared; relies on Craig in emergencies.

medical.gp: Dr. Dina Halawani (HAFI Medical Centre)
medical.medications: Takes regular prescribed medications in a Webster pack; osteoarthritis pain tablets taken once daily or up to three times daily during pain.

support.primaryContact: Craig (enduring power of attorney; emergency contact)
support.livingArrangement: Lives alone in Frankston with one cat

preferences.workerPreferences: Female workers for showering/personal care; otherwise open to any gender/age/culture (prefers a 'medium' age worker). Speak clearly and loudly due to hearing issues.
preferences.culturalConsiderations: Anglican (not practicing); values family, manners/morals, and independence; no specific cultural matching requirements.
preferences.serviceDeliveryPreferences: Personal care (shower assistance: back and hair) Monday/Wednesday/Friday 9–10 AM (female worker). Domestic assistance Mondays 10–11 AM (vacuuming, mopping, change bed sheets, bathroom cleaning). Transport/social support fortnightly Tuesdays 9 AM–12 PM for shopping/coffee (worker may stay). Meals via Choice Meals: diabetic diet, small portions; avoid lettuce, bananas, tomatoes (Barrett’s esophagus). Podiatry 8x/year; OT assessment; home maintenance twice yearly; taxi as needed. Start services 1 September. Access via side gate; advise visit times. No resuscitation—call 000 and family.

care_analyses.generated_html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have clearly stated that I do not want resuscitation (DNR) if I experience a medical emergency while care is being provided. Call 000 and notify my family (Craig) as per my preference.

I have Type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, osteoarthritis (constant pain usually 5/10, up to 10/10 during flares), and lymphedema. Heat can worsen my arthritis pain.

I am allergic to morphine, Acupan, Dacogridic, and Ghatran.

I have hearing issues; please speak clearly and loudly so I can hear you.

I am at increased risk of skin issues and occasional ulcers. Please monitor my skin integrity, especially on my legs.

I have limited mobility and use a walker (frame) as my preferred aid. I do not feel safe using walking sticks except when a walker cannot fit (e.g., at Claudette’s father’s place).

I prefer a female care worker for showering support.

I have a personal medical alarm (Live Life) and wear it for emergencies.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 02 September 2025

Preferred Name: Lydia

Full Name: Lydia Mae Goodwin

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan together with Thomas (Care Partner) during my intake assessment. I make my own decisions and have enduring power of attorney in place with Claudette and Craig.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I was born in Balclutha, New Zealand. I identify as Anglican (not currently attending services). I value family, good manners and morals, my independence, and peace in the world. I do not have specific cultural matching requirements for workers.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer care workers to speak clearly and loudly due to my hearing issues. On bad days (pain or digestive issues), I prefer to be left alone.

I prefer a female worker for showering support. I am open to any gender, age, or cultural background for other services.

My preferred times are mornings: showering on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 9:00am, and domestic assistance on Mondays at 10:00am. Transport/social support is every second Tuesday 9:00am–12:00pm.

Entry instructions: workers can walk down the side of the gate to my door. Please note I have one cat who may jump to greet people.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

Craig is my primary support person in an emergency. Claudette and Craig hold my enduring power of attorney.

Informal Supports

My family help if needed, although I try not to ask. I have previously received council supports (personal care, cleaning once monthly, and transport/social support).

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

My father died when I was four and I was raised in care homes. I met my husband at 17 and married in November 1962. I worked in retail, factory work, hospitals, and later a woollen factory before retiring. I moved from New Zealand to Australia on April 1 (arriving April 2) two years before this assessment. I have one child and two grandchildren. I later discovered I was one of 11 siblings; I know my youngest brother and sister.

Interests

I enjoy reading, crosswords, and playing word games on the computer. I have one cat. I love country music and used to attend a club; I also follow genealogy online.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have Type 2 diabetes, lymphedema, osteoarthritis, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, and atrial fibrillation (I can experience shortness of breath). I report constant pain from osteoarthritis (5/10 baseline; up to 10/10 during flares), worse in hot weather. I occasionally experience skin ulcers and need to monitor skin integrity. I have full dentures.

Medication

I take my medications regularly and receive them in a Webster pack from the in-house pharmacy at my medical centre. I take osteoarthritis pain tablets once daily and increase to three times daily during flares as needed. I do not need assistance with medication administration. I see a diabetes educator. I have allergies to morphine, Acupan, Dacogridic, and Ghatran.

Mobility and Equipment

My mobility is limited. I prefer to use a walker (frame). I have a wheelchair, walkers, crutches, a medical chair, a shower chair, bathroom handrails, and a ramp at the front of my home. I do not use a raised toilet seat because my toilet is higher set. I use my personal alarm (Live Life) for emergencies.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Dina L. Halawani, HAFI Medical Centre.

Pharmacy: HAFI Medical Centre in-house pharmacy (Webster packs supplied).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: I am New Zealand-born and English-speaking; no interpreter required.

Living with disability (mobility): I have limited mobility and rely on a walker; I cannot stand for long and use pacing (sit and rest) to manage pain.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I prefer to be left alone on bad days. I am currently a homebody and connect online, which may place me at some risk of isolation.

Specific Risks

Falls risk due to limited mobility and occasional need to use walking sticks where a walker cannot fit. I mitigate by pacing, sitting to rest when pain increases, and using installed rails and the shower chair.

Pain flares in hot weather due to osteoarthritis. I manage this with prescribed pain medication and rest.

Skin integrity risk (history of occasional ulcers; lymphedema). I use appropriate skincare products (DMEs) and monitor for new skin issues.

Cardiometabolic risks (Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, atrial fibrillation). I follow my medication regimen and diabetic diet and attend diabetes education.

Hearing impairment may affect communication; workers should speak clearly and loudly.

Emergency preference for no resuscitation (DNR). In an emergency, call 000 and notify Craig.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If I do not answer for a scheduled visit, follow provider protocol and attempt contact. If concerns persist, escalate to welfare check per policy.

During a medical emergency while providing care: do not perform resuscitation; call 000 and notify my family (Craig). Use my personal alarm (Live Life) if appropriate.

Entry: walk down the side of the gate to my door. Please be mindful that my cat may jump to greet you.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will feel clean, safe, and supported with showering while keeping my independence, with a female worker helping with my back and hair on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 9:00am over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can complete parts of my shower but need help with hard-to-reach areas due to pain and limited mobility. I prefer to be left alone on bad days. I have lymphedema and occasional skin ulcers, so gentle handling and skin checks are important.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Provide personal care support for showering (assist with back wash and hair wash; ensure bathroom safety using rails and shower chair; observe skin and report concerns; support pacing on pain days).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker (female) and me. When will it be done?: 3 x 1 hour weekly at 9:00am (Mon/Wed/Fri), starting 1 September. How much will it be?: Personal Care $85/hour (day). Estimated monthly cost (4 weeks): 12 hours/month × $85 = $1,020.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 2 Goal: I will keep my home tidy and safe by having vacuuming, mopping, bathroom cleaning, and bed linen changed every Monday at 10:00am so I can manage better with my pain over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot stand for long and need to pace tasks. Clean, dry floors and fresh bedding reduce slip and skin risks.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Domestic assistance for vacuuming, mopping, bathroom clean, and bed linen change immediately after my Monday shower.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour weekly on Mondays at 10:00am, ongoing from 1 September. How much will it be?: Domestic Assistance $85/hour (day). Estimated monthly cost (4 weeks): 4 hours/month × $85 = $340.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: Every second Tuesday I will go to Karingal to pick up my magazines, do a little shopping, and have a coffee so I stay connected and happy, aiming for 6 outings in the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): My mobility is limited and pain can flare. I use a walker and may need rest breaks.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Provide transport and social support for community access, including assistance with walking safely, carrying shopping, and taking rest breaks as needed.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me. When will it be done?: Fortnightly Tuesdays 9:00am–12:00pm (approximately 3 hours per outing), starting 1 September. How much will it be?: Social Support/Transport $85/hour (day). Estimated monthly cost (2 outings/6 hours): 6 × $85 = $510, plus mileage at $1.40/km as incurred.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 4 Goal: I will complete an Occupational Therapy assessment and implement agreed recommendations to make daily activities (shower, transfers, mobility at home) safer and easier within the next 8 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have a shower chair, rails, ramp, and walker. I need pacing due to pain and fatigue. I want to remain as independent as possible.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Arrange an in-home OT assessment; review current equipment and layout; co-design activity pacing strategies; implement practical changes (no structural works beyond agreed scope).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (OT) and me. When will it be done?: One 2-hour assessment within the first month; follow-up actions completed within 8 weeks. How much will it be?: Allied Health Therapist (OT) $180/hour × 2 hours = $360 (one-off this quarter).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 5 Goal: I will keep my feet healthy with regular podiatry because of my diabetes and hammer toes, aiming for two podiatry visits this quarter and eight per year.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Diabetes increases foot risk; I have foot issues including hammer toes. Skin integrity requires monitoring.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Schedule and receive podiatry visits; escalate any wounds/ulcers promptly; ensure safe nail and skin care.

Who is responsible?: Podiatry provider arranged by Salveo and me. When will it be done?: Approximately every 6–8 weeks (target 2 visits this quarter). How much will it be?: Clinical Care under Support at Home (government funded) – no client charge.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 6 Goal: I will keep my home safe with minor maintenance (gutters, windows, small repairs like loose nails/boards) completed as scheduled, with at least one 3-hour visit in the next 6 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot safely do ladder or repair work. Loose boards and protruding nails are tripping hazards.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Book Light Home & Gardening Maintenance for agreed tasks; confirm access; ensure safety clean-up after works.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare maintenance worker and me. When will it be done?: 3 hours per visit, twice yearly; schedule as needed. How much will it be?: Light Home & Gardening Maintenance $85/hour. Per visit: 3 × $85 = $255 (timing as scheduled; not a monthly recurring cost).

Service Category: Everyday Living

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

  • Domestic Assistance (Everyday Living): 1 hour/week at $85/hour. Estimated monthly (4 weeks): $340. Estimated quarterly (13 weeks): 13 hours × $85 = $1,105.

  • Occupational Therapy – Assessment (Clinical Care): One-off 2 hours × $180/hour = $360 (this quarter only, as scheduled).
  • Podiatry (Clinical Care): 8 visits/year (≈2 per quarter). Funded by government (no client charge).
  • Home Maintenance (Everyday Living): 3 hours/visit × $85 = $255 per visit, twice yearly (average across a quarter ≈ $127.50 if pro-rated; billed when delivered).
  • Personal alarm (Everyday Living/Equipment support): $75/year (≈$6.25/month; coverage arranged).

Clinical Care podiatry is government funded ($0 client charge). Mileage and any taxi use will be additional as incurred.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I confirm this care plan reflects my preferences, needs, and goals. I agree to the scheduled services and pricing stated for Salveo HomeCare services and understand that government-funded Clinical Care (e.g., podiatry) has no client charge. I consent to share this plan with my care team and my preferred support people as needed for my care.

Name: Thomas | Role: Care Partner | Date: 02 September 2025 | Review Date: Quarterly (every 3 months) | Signature: ____________________

Transcript Summary – Lydia (map to Standards 1–8)

Standard 1 – Consumer dignity and choice

I expressed my values (family, manners/morals, independence, peace), preferences (female worker for showering; clear, loud communication), and my right to make decisions (including DNR and being left alone on bad days). My cultural identity (Anglican, NZ-born) is respected.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers

A comprehensive intake covered my history, conditions, risks, equipment, routines, and supports. Services are scheduled from 1 September with quarterly review. My EPOA (Claudette and Craig) is documented.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care

Personal care is scheduled M/W/F at 9:00am with a female worker. Clinical needs include diabetes, AFib, lymphedema, osteoarthritis pain, skin integrity, and allergies. Podiatry is arranged (8/year). OT assessment is scheduled to optimise safety and function.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living

Domestic assistance weekly (vacuum, mop, bathroom, linen). Transport/social support fortnightly for shopping and coffee. Home maintenance twice yearly. Meals via Choice Meals with diabetic diet and specific exclusions.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment

Safety features in my home include ramp, shower chair, handrails. Entry is via side gate. I have a personal alarm (Live Life). No weapons in the home.

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance

I was advised that if a worker is not the right fit, I can request changes. Staff gender preference for showering is respected. Scheduling, safety, and emergency procedures are documented. Governance includes recognition of DNR and escalation to 000 and my family.

risks.description: Limited mobility; cannot stand or walk for long; uses walker frames (avoids sticks), has wheelchair and crutches.
Chronic osteoarthritis pain (baseline ~5/10; flares to 10/10), worsened by heat; requires pacing and rest breaks.
Atrial fibrillation with breathlessness.
Type 2 diabetes; independent with monitoring/management; workers should be aware of diabetic needs.
Lymphedema and occasional skin ulcers; uses emollients (DMEs).
Hearing difficulties; requires clear and loud speech.
On bad days may need very frequent toilet visits; Barrett’s oesophagus with dietary triggers (no lettuce, bananas, tomatoes).
Do not perform resuscitation (DNR). In emergencies call 000 and notify family.

medical.gp: Dr. Deena (Dina) Halawani at HAFI Medical Centre
medical.pharmacy: HAFI Medical Centre in-house pharmacy (Webster/Webstar pack)
medical.medications: Takes regular medications via Webster/Webstar pack; osteoarthritis pain tablets 1–3 times daily depending on pain; manages Type 2 diabetes independently; sees diabetes educator.

support.primaryContact: Craig (enduring power of attorney; emergency contact)
support.livingArrangement: Lives independently at home in Frankston; has one cat.

preferences.workerPreferences: Female worker for showering/personal care; otherwise open to any gender/age/cultural background.
preferences.culturalConsiderations: Anglican (not practicing); no specific cultural requirements for matching. Values family, good manners/morals, independence, and peace.
preferences.serviceDeliveryPreferences: Personal care (shower assist: back and hair) Monday, Wednesday, Friday 9–10 AM; domestic assistance Mondays 10–11 AM (vacuuming, mopping, change bed sheets, bathroom); transport/social support fortnightly Tuesdays 9 AM–12 PM for shopping/coffee (worker to stay); meals via Choice Meals, small portions, diabetic diet, avoid lettuce/bananas/tomatoes; start services from 1 September. On bad days prefers to be left alone; break tasks into smaller parts with rest; speak clearly and loudly.
