saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I live with Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). My MS symptoms are aggravated by heat, humidity and stress. On bad days I can feel weak, fatigued or off-balance.

I have a personal alarm (Live Life), currently paid via direct invoice/texts. I want the provider to take over payment once invoices are provided.

I do not have an emergency plan or kit. I prefer that in a medical emergency you call an ambulance (000) first and then call Samantha. I expressed a preference to not be resuscitated, but I do not have any formal advance care directive/DNR on file. Treat me as for full resuscitation unless a valid directive is supplied.

I have limited local supports. If there is no response during a scheduled visit, attempt to contact me and Samantha and escalate to 000 if you are concerned for my safety.

I have dogs at home (a boxer and a staffy). Workers must be dog-friendly and comfortable entering with dogs present.

I can mumble at times and cognition/memory can be an issue. Please speak clearly and check my understanding.

Key access: I do not use a key lock box and currently use an informal method stored at the meter box. This is less secure; handle access sensitively and do not disclose details beyond what is necessary for service delivery.

Cultural considerations: I identify as Jewish. Please avoid political or religious debate and be respectful of my identity.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 02 September 2025

Preferred Name: Graham

Full Name: Graham Knox

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan together with my care partner and my daughter, Samantha. I agreed to the goals and service schedule described below.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I identify as Jewish. I value humour, I dislike confrontation, and family is important to me. I prefer workers who are respectful and avoid political or religious debates. I do not practice a particular religion day-to-day.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I can mumble and my memory can be patchy. Please speak slowly, clearly and check that I’ve understood. I do not need an interpreter.

I have two dogs (boxer and staffy). Workers must be dog-friendly and comfortable with dogs in the home.

I prefer routine times for services: Thursdays 11:00–13:00 for cleaning and gardening; Tuesdays 11:00–13:00 for monthly shopping support.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Samantha (my daughter) is my main support person and emergency contact.

Informal Supports

I currently attend a social group at Bayside Care and Support (Leader Road) on Mondays and Wednesdays. The entry cost is $50 per session. I plan to continue attending twice weekly. I will provide invoices so the provider can pay the fees as arranged.

Outside of Samantha and my social group, I do not rely on local neighbours or other informal supports.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Australia and grew up in Sydney. In my 20s, I worked overseas as a tour guide for about four years, which was a highlight in my life. I have three children and became single in my 30s. I used to enjoy surfing, golf, and skiing.

Interests

I enjoy time with my family, my dogs, and attending my social group. A good day is when I wake without aches and can get on with what I want. A bad day is when I wake feeling exhausted. Rest, keeping cool, and reducing stress help me have more good days.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

I live with Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). I had a major episode about eight years ago, was found unconscious, and spent three weeks in critical care before moving to live with Samantha. I’ve had minor MS flare-ups since. I recently had pre-cancerous skin changes removed from my scalp/head. I am awaiting a cognition assessment (appointment pending). I have no known allergies.

Medication:

I take prescribed medications and manage them independently. I do not currently require assistance with medications, injections, patches or blood sugar monitoring. A medication plan/list can be provided on request.

Mobility and Equipment:

My mobility is independent without aids. I have an electric recliner chair and a personal alarm (Live Life). I do not have rails or bathroom equipment. I had a fall approximately 18 months ago; no significant injury reported.

GP / Pharmacy:

My GP is Dr Chris Sherman, Armadale Family Clinic (High Street, Armadale).

My pharmacy is Chemist Warehouse, Glenferrie Road, Malvern (around 120–128 Glenferrie Road).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not documented as CALD; I identify as Jewish.

Living with disability (mobility): I live with MS; mobility is currently independent. Heat/humidity/stress can worsen symptoms (weakness, vertigo-like feelings, fatigue).

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I report low maintenance mood and benefit from social group attendance twice weekly. Stress exacerbates symptoms; limited local supports may increase risk during emergencies.

Specific Risks

  • MS exacerbation triggered by heat, humidity and stress.
  • Falls risk (history of fall ~18 months ago) and potential balance issues during flares.
  • Emergency readiness gap: no key safe, no emergency plan or kit, limited local supports.
  • Communication: I can mumble; risk of miscommunication without clear speech and confirmation.
  • Dogs on premises; ensure safe entry procedures.
  • Personal alarm subscription continuity depends on provider receiving invoices.
  • Preference to avoid resuscitation without a formal directive on file; treat as full code until documentation is provided.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

In a medical emergency while services are being provided: call 000 (ambulance) immediately, then call Samantha (my daughter). I do not have a formal resuscitation directive; treat me as full code unless a valid directive is supplied.

If I do not answer the door for a scheduled visit: attempt to contact me and Samantha, and if you are concerned for my safety, call 000 for a welfare check.

Emergency contact details (phone/email): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my home clean, safe and manageable so I can live comfortably and reduce falls risk.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with mobility. My MS can flare with heat/stress, which can make me tired and off-balance. I prefer routine times for service and dog-friendly workers.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo workers will mop floors, clean bathrooms, wipe kitchen surfaces, change my bed linen weekly, and keep walkways free of clutter.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker | When will it be done?: 2 hours every Thursday 11:00–13:00 for the next 12 weeks | How much will it cost?: Domestic Assistance $85/hour, 2 hours weekly = $680/month (approx. $2,040/quarter).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will maintain and improve my balance and mobility affected by MS so I can walk safely and reduce near-falls.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Independent ambulation; heat/humidity/stress worsen symptoms. I respond well to routine.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Weekly physiotherapy to complete a progressive balance/strength program, gait training, and pacing strategies for hot days. Track outcomes using a Timed Up & Go (TUG) and near-fall diary.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Allied Health Therapist (Physiotherapist) | When will it be done?: 1 hour weekly for 12 weeks | How much will it cost?: $180/hour, $720/month (approx. $2,160/quarter). Target measures: reduce near-falls to 0/month; improve TUG by ≥2 seconds; walk 10 minutes on cool days without rest by end of quarter.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 3 Goal: I will keep my feet healthy and my thickened nails managed to prevent pain and falls.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Thickened nails; I currently do not see a podiatrist regularly.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Quarterly podiatry visit for nail cutting, skin/pressure assessment and footwear advice; escalate issues to GP if identified.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Allied Health – Podiatry (or contracted provider) | When will it be done?: 1 hour once this quarter | How much will it cost?: $180/hour, $180/quarter (average $60/month).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 4 Goal: I will complete my grocery and essential shopping each month so I don’t run out of staples and feel stressed.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent but benefit from support with errands. Heat and long outings can fatigue me.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Plan a shopping list in advance, transport to/from shops, complete shopping within 2 hours, unpack essentials, and ensure pantry staples are stocked.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker | When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly on Tuesdays 11:00–13:00 | How much will it cost?: Social Support $85/hour, $170/month (plus $1.40/km for transport as required; kms charged as incurred). Success measure: 0 stock-outs of key staples over the quarter.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 5 Goal: I will keep my garden and external walkways tidy to reduce trip hazards and feel proud of my home.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Falls risk increases with outdoor clutter or long grass.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Mow/trim as needed, clear paths and steps, remove green waste, and check lighting at entry points.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Home & Garden Maintenance worker | When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly on Thursdays 11:00–13:00 | How much will it cost?: Light Home & Gardening Maintenance $85/hour, $170/month (approx. $510/quarter). Outcome: walkways clear after each visit; no outdoor trip hazards.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 6 Goal: I will be emergency ready by setting up a simple plan and ensuring my personal alarm is active.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I currently have no emergency plan or kit and limited local supports. I prefer not to install a key safe at this time.

How will we do this? (Tasks): One dedicated session to co-create a one-page emergency plan (who to call, order of calls, medications list), prepare a fridge magnet, confirm my preferences, update my Live Life personal alarm account so invoices go to Salveo for payment, and discuss safe access options.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Care Partner/support worker (with me and Samantha) | When will it be done?: One 1-hour session this quarter | How much will it cost?: Social Support $85 for the session this quarter (+ personal alarm subscription cost: Not documented; to be paid on receipt of invoice).

Service Category: Independence Support

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded)

  • Allied Health Therapy – Physiotherapy: 1 hour weekly @ $180/hour = $720/month; approx. $2,160/quarter.
  • Allied Health – Podiatry: 1 hour per quarter @ $180/hour = $180/quarter (average $60/month).

Service Category: Independence Support

  • Social Support (Shopping): 2 hours monthly @ $85/hour = $170/month; approx. $510/quarter + $1.40/km transport (as incurred).
  • Social Participation – Bayside Care and Support group fees: $50 per session, Mondays and Wednesdays (approx. 2 sessions/week). Estimated 24 sessions/quarter = ~$1,200/quarter. Payment to be made on invoice.
  • Emergency Readiness session: 1 hour this quarter @ $85 = $85/quarter.

Service Category: Everyday Living

  • Domestic Assistance (cleaning, linen): 2 hours weekly @ $85/hour = $680/month; approx. $2,040/quarter.
  • Light Home & Gardening Maintenance: 2 hours monthly @ $85/hour = $170/month; approx. $510/quarter.
  • Personal alarm subscription (Live Life): Not documented; to be added upon receipt of invoice.

Quarterly Budget Allocation (estimated, excluding kms and any undisclosed subscription amounts)

  • Clinical Care: ~$2,160 + $180 = ~$2,340/quarter
  • Independence Support: ~$510 + $1,200 + $85 = ~$1,795/quarter (+ kms as incurred)
  • Everyday Living: ~$2,040 + $510 = ~$2,550/quarter
  • Estimated Total (known items): ~$6,685/quarter (plus km charges and personal alarm subscription once known)

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I have participated in developing this care plan and agree with the goals, services, and risk mitigations described. I consent to Salveo HomeCare coordinating and delivering my services under the Support at Home Program.

Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). Heat, humidity and stress aggravate my MS symptoms (vertigo/weakness). Summers are worse than winters for me.

I am awaiting a cognition assessment; I notice my memory has declined. I can sometimes be hard to understand as I mumble, and cognition can be an issue on some days.

I live with my daughter Samantha. I have limited local supports to rely on during emergencies.

I use a personal alarm (Live Life). I currently do not have a key safe and keep access arrangements informal; I understand this is less secure.

I prefer not to be resuscitated, but I do not have a formal Advance Care Directive/DNAR in place. In an emergency I want an ambulance called first, then contact Samantha. I understand emergency responders will follow legal requirements.

I have no known allergies. I am independent with mobility and activities of daily living. I have two large dogs in the home; workers must be dog-friendly and mindful of trip hazards.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 2 September 2025

Preferred Name: Graham

Full Name: Graham Knox

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

  • Me – Graham Knox (consumer)

  • Samantha (my daughter and primary support person, I live with her)

  • Care Partner (assessment interviewer)

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I identify as Jewish and a Zionist. I speak English and do not require an interpreter. I value humour, I do not like confrontation, and family contact is important to me. I do not practice a particular religion and I do not have specific spiritual care needs. I prefer care staff who are respectful and avoid political or religious debates.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

  • Workers must be dog-friendly. I have two large dogs (a boxer and a staffy) inside the home.

  • Please speak clearly and at a normal pace; I can mumble and cognition can be an issue at times.

  • Schedule preferences agreed in assessment: Domestic Assistance weekly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00; Shopping support monthly on Tuesdays around 11:00–13:00; Gardening monthly coordinated around Thursday 11:00–13:00 where possible.

  • Be mindful of heat sensitivity; morning/midday visits are preferred in summer and ensure I can keep cool.

  • Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

  • Samantha – my daughter (primary contact)

  • My brother

  • A friend in the city (college friend)

  • Members of my social group at Leader Road (Bayside Care and Support)

Informal Supports

I live with my daughter Samantha who provides informal support as needed. I currently do not rely on neighbours or other local supports in emergencies.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Australia and grew up in Sydney. In my twenties I worked overseas as a tour guide for four years, which was a pinnacle time in my life. I returned to Australia, had three children, became single in my thirties, taught for a number of years, and did various jobs. I enjoy the mountains and have skied in the past.

Interests

I enjoy contact with my family (many are overseas), attending my social group, spending time with my two dogs, watching TV, and keeping life low-stress. I previously enjoyed surfing and golf but no longer do these activities.

My Medical Information

Medical History: Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). MS flare-ups have been mostly minor in recent years. A major episode about eight years ago resulted in hospitalisation in critical care for three weeks; I moved to live with Samantha afterwards. Precancerous skin lesion removed from my head (recent). Awaiting cognition assessment; I notice some memory decline. No known allergies.

Medication: I take prescribed medications and manage them independently. I do not require assistance with injections, patches, or blood sugar monitoring. I report no ongoing pain medication needs.

Mobility and Equipment: I mobilise independently without aids. Last recorded fall was approximately 18 months ago; no major injury reported. I use a personal alarm (Live Life) and have an electric recliner chair. I do not have rails or shower equipment installed. Heat and humidity exacerbate MS symptoms (vertigo/weakness).

GP / Pharmacy: GP – Dr Chris Sherman, Armidale Family Clinic. Pharmacy – Chemist Warehouse on Glenfrew/Glenferrie Road, Malvern (around 120–128). Contact details not documented.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: I identify as Jewish; I am English-speaking and do not require an interpreter.

Living with disability (mobility): I live with MS; I am currently independent with mobility but experience intermittent vertigo/weakness in heat. Last fall approx. 18 months ago.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I prefer low-stress routines. Heat, humidity and stress trigger symptom flare-ups. I have limited local emergency supports but I attend a social group twice weekly, which supports my wellbeing.

Specific Risks

  • Heat/humidity trigger MS symptoms (vertigo/weakness).

  • History of a significant hospitalisation eight years ago; awaiting cognition assessment due to memory decline.

  • No formal emergency plan/kit; limited local support network.

  • No key lock box; current key access arrangements are informal and less secure.

  • Two large dogs in the home can increase environmental trip hazards during care tasks.

  • Personal CPR preference (no resuscitation) is not legally documented; must follow legal requirements in an emergency.

If there is a medical emergency while services are being provided: call an ambulance (000) first, then call Samantha (my daughter). I prefer not to be resuscitated, but I understand emergency responders will follow legal requirements unless a valid directive is in place.

If I do not respond at a scheduled visit: try calling me first. If no response, contact Samantha.

Primary emergency contact: Samantha (daughter) – phone: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

GP: Dr Chris Sherman, Armidale Family Clinic.

Pharmacy: Chemist Warehouse, Glenfrew/Glenferrie Road, Malvern.

My Goals

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent but MS symptoms are aggravated by heat, humidity and stress. I prefer help with mopping floors, cleaning bathrooms, and changing my bed linen.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Domestic Assistance to mop floors, clean bathrooms, and change bed linen weekly. Workers will be dog-friendly and mindful of heat sensitivity (work at cooler times where possible).

Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have severe breathlessness from emphysema and can often only walk about 10 metres before I need to stop and rest.

I have a history of depression and was admitted to a mental health ward for three weeks about six months ago following a suicide attempt.

I have expressed a clear preference for “no resuscitation/CPR,” however I do not currently have a formal DNR/Advance Care Directive in place. I understand ambulance officers must commence resuscitation unless a valid directive is available.

I am at risk of falls and have had recent falls (“went backwards and landed on my arse,” with a cut to my leg).

I am currently not using my recommended four-wheel walker as I feel it uses too much of my energy.

I prefer and have agreed to a pendant-style personal alarm to be purchased (one-off $567) and worn daily once supplied.

I smoke and will step outside to do so.

I live with a small dog (Rambo) who may be excited when people arrive.

If a care worker arrives and I do not answer, I want them to call me first, then call my son Darryl, and if concerned for my safety, call 000.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 02 September 2025

Preferred Name: Ian

Full Name: Ian Hood

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan with Thomas (Salveo Care), my son Darryl, and me (Ian). I am the decision-maker for my care.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I reported no specific cultural or matching preferences for workers.

I want my end-of-life wishes respected, including my preference for no resuscitation/CPR, and I want music such as Johnny O’Keefe songs played as part of my end-of-life preferences.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer my regular social support visit on Wednesdays from 12:00 pm to 2:30 pm (2.5 hours), starting on the 25th as agreed.

I have no preference for worker gender or age. Continuity is important to me; I value a companion-style worker similar to the previous support person who felt “like family.”

If I don’t answer the door at a scheduled time, please call me first, then call Darryl. If still concerned, call 000.

Please allow me time to catch my breath between tasks and keep conversations calm and unhurried on days when my breathing is worse.

Please be mindful that my dog Rambo may be excited when you arrive; I appreciate gentle reassurance and keeping gates/doors secured.

I understand the 24-hour cancellation policy and I was shown how to make complaints (to Archie, the CEO) if needed.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

My son Darryl is my primary support and contact.

My wife is in permanent residential care and remains the most important person in my life.

My other children are Paul and Laura (our relationship is currently strained, which causes me significant distress).

People I value include neighbours Bruce and Anne, and friends/contacts Josie, Glen, Terri, Kevin, Bernie and Robin. I also have five grandchildren (Madison is one I mentioned fondly).

Informal Supports

saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

Allergies: I have no known allergies.

Primary health condition: I live with Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). Heat, humidity and stress aggravate my MS symptoms (e.g., weakness, vertigo-like sensations). I pace myself and rest to avoid flare-ups.

Cognition: I am awaiting a cognition assessment; I have noticed increasing forgetfulness. Please speak clearly and give me time to respond.

Emergency preferences: In a medical emergency, call 000 (ambulance) first, then contact Samantha (my daughter). I have expressed that I do not want resuscitation; however, I do not have a formal Advance Care Directive/DNR. Paramedics will follow clinical protocols.

Falls: I have a history of falls, last reported around 18 months ago, without major injury.

Personal alarm: I have a Live Life personal alarm; I am not using it often but may need help with payments/top-ups as invoices arrive.

Access and pets: I have dogs in the home and prefer dog-friendly workers.

Home access: I do not have a key lock box. I currently use an insecure workaround for access.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 2 September 2025

Preferred Name: Graham

Full Name: Graham Knox

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Interpreter required?: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this care plan together with my care partner and my daughter, Samantha, during the assessment conversation.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I describe myself as a typical Aussie bloke. I identify as Jewish and as a Zionist culturally, though I do not actively practice a religion.

Humour matters to me. I avoid confrontation. Family is important to me.

Please be respectful and avoid political or religious debates during visits.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I can mumble and sometimes be hard to understand. Please speak clearly, at a normal pace, and check back for understanding.

I prefer dog-friendly workers as my dogs are part of my home life.

I feel worse in hot, humid weather. Where possible, please schedule services during cooler parts of the day and help me keep cool and reduce stress.

I prefer the following service times discussed in the assessment: Domestic Assistance weekly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00; Light Home & Gardening Maintenance monthly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00; Shopping Social Support monthly on Tuesdays around 11:00–13:00.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

Samantha (my daughter) is my primary support and contact person.

I have friends through my social group and a friend in the city I went to college with.

I do not rely on neighbours for support.

Informal Supports

I live with Samantha and receive day-to-day support from her as needed.

I attend a social group two days per week (Mondays and Wednesdays) at Leader Road through Bayside Care and Support (entry fee noted below).

My dogs are important companions for me.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Australia and grew up in Sydney. I worked overseas as a tour guide for about four years, which was a pinnacle time in my life. I later taught for a number of years and did other jobs in between.

I have three children and became single in my thirties. About eight years ago, after a major health episode, I moved to live with Samantha.

I have enjoyed skiing and previously surfed and played golf.

Interests

I enjoy contact with family (many are overseas), attending my social group, watching AFL, and spending time with my dogs.

A good day is when I have no aches and can just get on with what I want to do. A bad day is when I wake up feeling unwell or when it is hot and humid. Rest helps me have more good days. Heat and stress aggravate my MS symptoms; staying cool and reducing stress helps.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

I have Multiple Sclerosis (diagnosed May 1987). I experience minor flare-ups and had a major episode about eight years ago, when I was found unconscious and admitted to critical care for three weeks. I have had pre-cancerous lesions removed from my scalp/head.

I have no known allergies or medical alerts.

I report no ongoing pain and no breathing issues.

Medication:

I take prescribed medications and manage them independently. I report having a medication plan in place and do not need assistance with medications, injections, patches, or blood sugar monitoring.

Mobility and Equipment:

My mobility is independent and I do not use a walking aid. I can get in and out of a car. I have an electric recliner chair and a Live Life personal alarm. I do not have rails, shower chairs, or a key lock box.

GP / Pharmacy:

My GP is Dr Chris Sherman at the Armidale Family Clinic.

My pharmacy is Chemist Warehouse on Glenferrie Road, Malvern.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: I identify as Jewish but I do not require an interpreter (English-speaking).

Living with disability (mobility): I live with MS; I currently mobilise independently.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I have limited local supports and rely on my social group; heat and stress can worsen my MS symptoms.

Specific Risks

Heat, humidity, and stress exacerbate my MS symptoms.

I do not have a formal emergency plan or kit and would need full assistance in an emergency.

I do not have a key lock box and use an insecure access workaround.

I have a history of falls (last around 18 months ago, no major injury).

I have verbally expressed a wish not to be resuscitated but do not have a formal Advance Care Directive/DNR.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

In an emergency during service delivery: call 000 for an ambulance first. After calling 000, please contact Samantha (my daughter). Contact details are not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

If a scheduled visit occurs and there is no response at the door: please call my phone first. If there is still no response, contact Samantha. If you have immediate concerns for my safety, call 000. I do not have a key lock box.

My personal alarm is with Live Life; invoices may be texted to me. The provider can assist with payments once invoice details are supplied.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my home clean and comfortable so I can “just get on with my day” without fatigue from housework.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I live with MS; heat and stress aggravate symptoms. I am independent with mobility but benefit from conserving energy.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare to provide Domestic Assistance for vacuuming, mopping, bathroom clean, bed linen change, and general tidy.

Who is responsible?: Salveo support worker and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours weekly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00, for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour = $170/week, approximately $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will shop safely and efficiently once a month so my pantry and fridge are stocked and I can eat well.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I manage well on cooler days; heat and stress worsen MS. I prefer mornings/late morning.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare to provide Social Support (shopping assistance, list planning, carrying groceries, and transport if needed).

Who is responsible?: Salveo support worker and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly on Tuesdays around 11:00–13:00, for the next 3 months. How much will it be cost?: $85/hour = $170/month, plus mileage at $1.40/km as incurred.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: I will keep my garden and outdoor paths tidy to reduce trip hazards and keep access safe.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have a past fall (about 18 months ago). I remain independently mobile.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare to provide Light Home & Gardening Maintenance for basic yard tidy, sweeping paths, and light pruning as required.

Who is responsible?: Salveo gardener and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly on Thursdays around 11:00–13:00, for the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: $85/hour = $170/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will maintain my balance and strength to stay independent with walking and reduce fall risk.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I live with MS; heat and stress aggravate symptoms. I am currently independently mobile.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will receive Physiotherapy with an Allied Health Therapist (Salveo) for assessment and a home exercise program. Outcome measures such as Timed Up and Go (TUG) and 5-times sit-to-stand will be recorded at week 1 and week 12 to track maintenance or ≥10% improvement where appropriate.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Allied Health Therapist (Physio) and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour weekly for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $180/hour, approximately $720/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 5 Goal: I will keep my feet comfortable and free of skin problems so I can walk safely.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have thickened toenails; no current wounds.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Podiatry (Allied Health) for nail care, skin integrity check, and foot health education.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Allied Health Therapist (Podiatry) and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour every 3 months (once this quarter). How much will it cost?: $180 per session (pro-rata ≈ $60/month).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 6 Goal: I will have a simple emergency and heatwave plan so I feel confident managing on bad days.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I do not have an emergency plan/kit and would need full assistance in an emergency; heat and stress aggravate MS.

How will we do this? (Tasks): a) One Social Support session at home to co-design a one-page emergency/heatwave plan (who to call, cool-down steps). b) Install a coded key lock box for safe access if I agree.

Who is responsible?: Salveo support worker (planning) and Salveo home maintenance worker (installation), with me and Samantha. When will it be done?: One-off in Month 1 (planning 1 hour; installation 1 hour). How much will it cost?: Social Support $85 (1 hour) + Light Home & Gardening Maintenance $85 (1 hour) = $170 one-off. (Key safe purchase cost not documented.)

Service Category: Independence Support (planning) / Everyday Living (installation)

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

Clinical Care (Allied Health):

  • Physiotherapy: 1 hr/week at $180/hr ≈ $720/month.
  • Podiatry: 1 hr/quarter at $180/session ≈ $60/month (pro‑rated).

Independence Support:

  • Social Support – Shopping: 2 hrs/month at $85/hr = $170/month (+ mileage $1.40/km as incurred).
  • Emergency/heatwave plan (one-off Month 1): Social Support 1 hr at $85 = $85 (once).

Everyday Living:

  • Domestic Assistance: 2 hrs/week at $85/hr ≈ $680/month.
  • Light Home & Gardening Maintenance: 2 hrs/month at $85/hr = $170/month.
  • Social group entry fees (Bayside Care & Support): $50 per session, typically Mondays and Wednesdays ≈ 8 sessions/month = $400/month.
  • Personal alarm (Live Life) subscription/top-ups: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.
  • Key safe device purchase (if agreed): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Quarterly Budget Allocation

  • Clinical Care total (per quarter): ≈ $2,340.
  • Independence Support total (per quarter): Shopping ≈ $510 (+ mileage as incurred). One-off plan in Month 1: $85.
  • Everyday Living total (per quarter): Domestic Assistance ≈ $2,040; Gardening ≈ $510; Social group fees ≈ $1,200. (Personal alarm and key safe device costs not documented.)
  • Estimated subtotal per quarter (known items): ≈ $2,340 + $510 + $85 + $2,040 + $510 + $1,200 = ≈ $6,685, plus transport mileage and any approved device/subscription costs.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

I expressed my preferences for respectful communication, dog-friendly workers, cooler-time appointments, cultural identity (Jewish, non-practicing), and a desire to avoid confrontation. My goals reflect what matters to me: comfort at home, independence, and social connection.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers

This plan reflects assessment details: MS history, heat/stress triggers, falls history, independent mobility, current services (social group), and preferences for service days/times. A quarterly review cycle is in place, and a cognition assessment is pending.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care

Clinical supports include Physiotherapy and Podiatry with measurable outcomes. I manage my own medications and report no pain or wound care needs. Risks (heat, stress, falls) are addressed in goals and the Dignity of Risk section.

Domestic Assistance, Light Home & Gardening, and Shopping Social Support are scheduled to sustain my independence. Social participation (club fees) is supported to reduce isolation and maintain wellbeing.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment

Workers are asked to be dog-friendly and culturally respectful, to schedule in cooler periods, and to ensure safe access planning (key safe option). My communication needs (I may mumble) are identified.

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance

I understand services will be coordinated by a single provider under Support at Home. Feedback, complaints, and governance processes were not discussed in detail in this transcript; these will be provided to me by the provider.

saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

  • I recently had ankle surgery (March, plates inserted) after a fall at home; I use a walking stick outside and experience occasional ankle twinges.

  • I have a history of open heart surgery with a pig valve replacement (2014) and a hip replacement (2015).

  • I prefer not to be resuscitated if I would end up with no meaningful quality of life, but I do not currently have formal DNR documentation in place.

  • I have a personal alarm system at home.

  • My son Stuart is my primary contact and enduring power of attorney.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 02 September 2025

Preferred Name: Kate

Full Name: Kate Weston

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Interpreter required?: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan together with a Salvo Care representative, with my son Stuart (primary contact and enduring power of attorney) to be involved in my care decisions and updates.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I value family, independence, and integrity/manners.

I have no specific cultural or religious preferences for workers, but I want to feel comfortable and safe in my home.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I like to get to know new people before receiving services from them.

I have no gender preference for cleaning, but I prefer a female for shopping assistance, ideally someone with more life experience rather than someone very young.

I prefer continuity of care, with the same support worker allocated for shopping and domestic assistance where possible.

I have agreed service times: Domestic Assistance on alternating Tuesdays at 10:00 AM for 1.5 hours; Social Support/Shopping on the alternate Tuesdays for 2 hours; Physiotherapy on Wednesday afternoons from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM (fortnightly, start date subject to therapist availability).

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

My primary contact and enduring power of attorney is my son Stuart.

My other son is Russell.

My daughters-in-law are Monique and Linda.

My grandchildren are Amelia, Jared, and Aaron.

My neighbor Brian can provide local support in an emergency.

My case manager at Monash Health is Ellie Erskine.

Informal Supports

I generally manage well on my own.

I have a personal alarm system at home.

My son Stuart provides primary support and is involved in my care decisions.

My neighbor Brian is a local contact who may assist in urgent situations.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

My earliest memory is my father returning from war.

I worked in dressmaking and fashion, including making high-end clothing for French designers in Melbourne.

I married and had two sons, and later divorced after 13 years.

I worked in a factory making pillows and cushions until age 62 when the factory closed, then I volunteered teaching crafts and helping with community outings.

Interests

I enjoy crafts like crocheting and knitting, and I watch television.

I avoid competitive reality TV because I dislike seeing people being unkind.

I miss kneeling and gardening and would like to enjoy my garden safely.

Driving my car and doing my crafts are working well for me right now.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I had kidney stones removed many years ago.

I had open heart surgery with a pig valve replacement in 2014.

I had a hip replacement in 2015.

I had ankle surgery in March of this year after a fall at home, with plates inserted.

I am recovering well, with occasional ankle twinges.

Medication

I take my medications every morning.

Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Mobility and Equipment

I use a walking stick outside the house and do not need walking aids inside.

I cannot kneel and have difficulty with tasks that require bending.

I have handrails in the shower and a non-slip mat.

GP / Pharmacy

My GP is Dr. Nam.

My pharmacy is Advantage in Lakeside.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Living with disability (mobility): I am recovering from ankle surgery, cannot kneel, use a walking stick outside, and need help with tasks involving bending or kneeling.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I worry frequently; many of my friends have died or moved away, which may increase isolation risk, though I generally manage well.

Specific Risks

  • Falls risk due to history of fall and recent ankle surgery.

  • Emergency decision-making risk: I prefer not to be resuscitated in certain circumstances, but I do not currently have formal DNR documentation.

  • Home task risk: Kneeling/bending tasks (e.g., low cleaning, gardening) increase strain and falls risk.

  • Potential delay in emergency access because I am still considering a key lock box.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

In a medical emergency, call an ambulance first and then contact my son Stuart.

Primary contact: Stuart (son and enduring power of attorney).

Secondary contact: Russell (son).

Local support: Brian (neighbor).

I have a personal alarm system; I will let Salvo Care know when my subscription is due for renewal so it can be paid through my package if appropriate.

I have expressed a preference not to be resuscitated if I would have no meaningful recovery, but I understand that without legal documentation, emergency services will attempt resuscitation.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I want to keep my independence and get back to pottering in my garden (without kneeling) by improving my ankle strength and confidence walking outside.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I walk without aids inside and use a walking stick outside; I cannot kneel and have occasional ankle twinges; I am at some risk of falls outdoors.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will attend physiotherapy one hour fortnightly on Wednesday afternoons (1–2 PM) and complete my prescribed home exercises at least 5 days per week; paths will be kept clear of trip hazards via gardening support.

Who is responsible?: Me; Salveo HomeCare Allied Health Therapist (Physiotherapist); Care Partner for coordination. When will it be done?: Fortnightly for 12 weeks (one quarter), Wednesdays 1–2 PM, starting when the physiotherapist confirms availability. How much will it cost?: $180/hour, $360/month, $1,080/quarter (Clinical Care, 100% government funded).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 2 Goal: I want to keep my feet healthy so I can walk safely and comfortably in the community.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am mobile with a stick outdoors; foot issues could affect balance and increase falls risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will attend podiatry eight times per year for nail and skin care and pressure management; appointments will be scheduled approximately every 6–8 weeks.

Who is responsible?: Me; Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Podiatry via Salveo network). When will it be done?: Ongoing, approximately every 6–8 weeks within the next 12 months, with two appointments expected this quarter. How much will it cost?: Estimated at $180/hour per visit (for budgeting), $120/month on average, $360/quarter (Clinical Care, 100% government funded). Actual billed time may vary.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 3 Goal: I want my home to stay clean and safe without me having to bend or kneel.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I manage my personal care independently but have difficulty with low and heavy tasks; bending and kneeling increase falls and strain risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Domestic Assistance for bathrooms, floors, low surfaces, laundry/linen change, and rubbish removal on a set schedule.

Who is responsible?: Me; Salveo HomeCare Domestic Assistance worker. When will it be done?: 1.5 hours fortnightly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM (alternating weeks), for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $255/month, $765/quarter.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I want to shop safely in the community, keep my pantry stocked, and enjoy a friendly outing with a worker I’m comfortable with.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I prefer a female worker with more life experience for shopping; I worry at times and benefit from support planning and unhurried trips.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Social Support/Shopping on alternating Tuesdays for groceries and errands, with transport and pacing breaks as needed; we will shop at quieter times and maintain a running list.

Who is responsible?: Me; Salveo HomeCare Social Support worker (female preferred); Care Partner for scheduling continuity. When will it be done?: 2 hours fortnightly on Tuesdays (alternating with cleaning) over the next 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $340/month, $1,020/quarter, plus $1.40/km transport as incurred.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 5 Goal: I want my garden kept tidy and my paths clear so I can enjoy being outside without kneeling or risking a fall.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot kneel and have a history of a fall in the garden; uneven surfaces and debris increase falls risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Light Home & Gardening Maintenance to weed, prune, sweep paths, and remove green waste, focusing on trip hazards and access.

Who is responsible?: Me; Salveo HomeCare gardening worker. When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly, ongoing; at least one session this quarter. How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $170/month, $510/quarter.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 6 Goal: I want essential home maintenance (windows, gutters, and air conditioning units) completed regularly to keep my home safe and functional.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Tasks at height and heavy cleaning are unsafe for me to do; delayed maintenance can create hazards.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will schedule Home Maintenance twice yearly for windows, gutters, and air conditioning units; works will be coordinated in suitable weather.

Who is responsible?: Me; Salveo HomeCare home maintenance worker; Care Partner for booking. When will it be done?: 3 hours twice yearly (6 hours/year), with one booking in each half of the year; billed when delivered. I value family, independence, and integrity/manners.

I have no specific cultural or religious preferences for workers, but I want to feel comfortable and safe in my home.

I like to get to know new people before receiving services from them.

I have no gender preference for cleaning, but I prefer a female for shopping assistance, ideally someone with more life experience rather than someone very young.

I prefer continuity of care, with the same support worker allocated for shopping and domestic assistance where possible.

I have agreed service times: Domestic Assistance on alternating Tuesdays at 10:00 AM for 1.5 hours; Social Support/Shopping on the alternate Tuesdays for 2 hours; Physiotherapy on Wednesday afternoons from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM (fortnightly, start date subject to therapist availability).

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

My primary contact and enduring power of attorney is my son Stuart.

My other son is Russell.

My daughters-in-law are Monique and Linda.

My grandchildren are Amelia, Jared, and Aaron.

My neighbor Brian can provide local support in an emergency.

I generally manage well on my own.

Family Background and Life History

My earliest memory is my father returning from war.

I worked in dressmaking and fashion, including making high-end clothing for French designers in Melbourne.

I married and had two sons, and later divorced after 13 years.

I worked in a factory making pillows and cushions until age 62 when the factory closed, then I volunteered teaching crafts and helping with community outings.

Interests

I enjoy crafts like crocheting and knitting, and I watch television.

I avoid competitive reality TV because I dislike seeing people being unkind.

I miss kneeling and gardening and would like to enjoy my garden safely.

Driving my car and doing my crafts are working well for me right now.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I had kidney stones removed many years ago.

I had open heart surgery with a pig valve replacement in 2014.

I had a hip replacement in 2015.

I had ankle surgery in March of this year after a fall at home, with plates inserted.

I am recovering well, with occasional ankle twinges.

Medication

I take my medications every morning.

Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Mobility and Equipment

I use a walking stick outside the house and do not need walking aids inside.

I cannot kneel and have difficulty with tasks that require bending.

I have handrails in the shower and a non-slip mat.

GP / Pharmacy

My GP is Dr. Nam.

My pharmacy is Advantage in Lakeside.

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

In a medical emergency, call an ambulance first and then contact my son Stuart.

Service Category: Clinical Care

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am mobile with a stick outdoors; foot issues could affect balance and increase falls risk.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I manage my personal care independently but have difficulty with low and heavy tasks; bending and kneeling increase falls and strain risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Domestic Assistance for bathrooms, floors, low surfaces, laundry/linen change, and rubbish removal on a set schedule.

Who is responsible?: Me; Salveo HomeCare Domestic Assistance worker. When will it be done?: 1.5 hours fortnightly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM (alternating weeks), for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $255/month, $765/quarter.

Service Category: Everyday Living

Abilities and considerations (risks): I prefer a female worker with more life experience for shopping; I worry at times and benefit from support planning and unhurried trips.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Social Support/Shopping on alternating Tuesdays for groceries and errands, with transport and pacing breaks as needed; we will shop at quieter times and maintain a running list.

How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $340/month, $1,020/quarter, plus $1.40/km transport as incurred.

Service Category: Independence Support

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot kneel and have a history of a fall in the garden; uneven surfaces and debris increase falls risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Light Home & Gardening Maintenance to weed, prune, sweep paths, and remove green waste, focusing on trip hazards and access.

Who is responsible?: Me; Salveo HomeCare gardening worker. When will it be done?: 2 hours monthly, ongoing; at least one session this quarter. How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $170/month, $510/quarter.

Service Category: Everyday Living

Abilities and considerations (risks): Tasks at height and heavy cleaning are unsafe for me to do; delayed maintenance can create hazards.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will schedule Home Maintenance twice yearly for windows, gutters, and air conditioning units; works will be coordinated in suitable weather.

When will it be done?: Fortnightly sessions for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $180/hour, 1 hour fortnightly = approximately $360/month, $1,080/quarter (Clinical Care is government funded).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 2 Goal: I will keep my home clean and safe to my standard so I can focus on my recovery and crafts, with my bedroom/bathroom cleaned and bed linen changed at least once per fortnight for the next 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I manage most tasks but I cannot kneel or do heavy bending. Falls risk increases with clutter or wet floors.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Domestic Assistance for bathrooms, kitchen, floors, dusting, laundry and linen change; remove trip hazards; wipe commonly touched surfaces.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me to direct tasks. When will it be done?: 1.5 hours fortnightly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM (starting 19 September). How much will it cost?: $85/hour, 1.5 hours fortnightly ≈ 3 hours/month = $255/month, $765/quarter.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: I will complete my grocery shopping and enjoy a social outing every fortnight, with two successful shopping trips per month and my pantry and fridge maintained to my list for the next 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I drive and am independent but I prefer support for carrying, reaching and pacing. I prefer a female worker with life experience and continuity of worker. Mileage charges may apply.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Social Support and Transport for shopping, list-making, carrying groceries, putting items away, and a short coffee break if I choose. Alternate Tuesdays with cleaning.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me. When will it be done?: Two hours fortnightly on Tuesdays (starting 25 September). How much will it cost?: $85/hour, 2 hours fortnightly ≈ 4 hours/month = $340/month, $1,020/quarter, plus $1.40/km mileage as incurred.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 4 Goal: I will maintain a neat and safe garden without kneeling, with pathways kept clear of trip hazards and basic weeding/pruning completed monthly for the next quarter.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot kneel and have a falls risk on uneven ground.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Light Home & Gardening Maintenance to weed/prune, clear paths, and dispose of green waste; I will avoid kneeling and heavy tasks.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare gardener/maintenance worker and me to direct priorities. When will it be done?: Two hours monthly. How much will it cost?: $85/hour × 2 hours = $170/month, $510/quarter.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 5 Goal: I will keep my home maintained and reduce hazards, ensuring windows, gutters and air-conditioning filters are serviced within two visits over the next 12 months, with any work due this quarter booked and completed.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Working at heights is unsafe for me; professional support reduces risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Home maintenance visits for windows, gutters, and air-conditioning units as scheduled; tasks to be completed safely by workers.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare maintenance workers; scheduling by the provider with my agreement. When will it be done?: Three hours twice yearly; any due visit to be completed this quarter. How much will it cost?: $85/hour × 3 hours per visit = $255 per visit; $510/year (average $42.50/month; $127.50/quarter, billed when delivered).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 6 Goal: I will maintain healthy feet to support safe mobility, attending podiatry eight times per year with no new foot wounds or infections over the next 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am recovering from ankle surgery; comfortable footwear and regular podiatry help me stay mobile.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Podiatry appointments for skin/nail care and foot health checks; reinforce footwear and self-care advice.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Podiatry) and me. When will it be done?: As scheduled; average two visits per quarter. How much will it cost?: $180/hour per visit; eight visits/year ≈ $120/month average, $360/quarter (assumes 1-hour visits; to be adjusted if podiatrist sets a different duration).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 7 Goal: I will discuss and, if I choose, formalise my resuscitation preferences (Advance Care Directive/Resuscitation Plan) with my GP within the next 12 weeks so my wishes are clearly documented.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have stated a preference regarding resuscitation but currently have no formal documentation; without it, emergency services will attempt resuscitation.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will book a GP appointment to discuss options; Salveo can arrange a Registered Nurse to support education/completion and coordinate sharing the document with my son and provider.

Who is responsible?: I will lead the decision; GP Dr. Nam; Salveo HomeCare Registered Nurse if I request assistance. When will it be done?: Within 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: Registered Nurse support up to 1 hour once this quarter at $148.50 (one-off; ≈ $49.50/month averaged). GP appointment billed via usual channels.

  • Independence Support: Social Support/Shopping 2 hrs fortnightly ($85/hr) plus mileage $1.40/km as incurred.

Transcript Summary – Kate Weston (map to Standards 1–8)

Standard 1 – Consumer dignity and choice

I expressed my core values (family, independence, integrity/manners) and preferences for workers (female and experienced for shopping; continuity). I was informed of my rights and I consented to my son Stuart’s involvement. My wish to feel safe and comfortable at home is central to the plan.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers

A comprehensive assessment reviewed my history, abilities, routines, and risks. We co-designed services and set SMARTA goals with clear frequencies and costs. Reviews are set quarterly. My preferences about resuscitation and emergency actions are noted for follow-up with my GP.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care

Clinical supports include physiotherapy and podiatry with defined schedules. I self-manage medications. Risks (falls, exercise adherence) are identified with mitigation. Optional RN support is available to assist with advance care planning if I choose.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living

Domestic assistance, social support/shopping, gardening and home maintenance are scheduled to support safe, independent living and community participation, aligned to my preferences and routines.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment

Services will be delivered safely in my home, using equipment like shower rails and a non-slip mat. My preference for consistent workers and suitable scheduling has been incorporated.

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance

I understand how to provide feedback or make a complaint without reprisal. Workers will be appropriately screened and skilled. Service delivery, budgeting and risk management align with governance requirements of the Support at Home Program and Aged Care Quality Standards.

I accept some risks (for example, walking outdoors and continuing gardening tasks done by others) and I agree to reasonable strategies to reduce harm while respecting my choices. saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I prefer hard-copy documents and phone contact rather than email or online communication.

I am hard of hearing in my right ear. Please speak slowly, clearly and a little louder on my left side. I own hearing aids but rarely use them.

In an emergency I want CPR performed, triple zero (000) called, and my family notified.

If I do not answer the door at a scheduled visit, please use my spare key (kept on the ledge on top of the door) to gain access and check on me.

I have a personal alarm in my home.

I do not consent to Peninsula Health being involved in my care or referrals.

I do not consent to students or third parties being present during my services for observation or supervision.

Pet on premises: cat (Charlie).

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 2025-09-02

Preferred Name: Peter

Full Name: Peter Anthony Switzer

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I participated in developing this plan with my Salveo HomeCare Care Partner. I am responsible for making my own decisions. My family (Ben and Beata) were identified as my preferred support people and emergency contacts.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I was born in Mount Albert. I identify as Christian and usually attend Frankston Community Baptist Church. There are no additional cultural or diversity considerations documented.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer a fully managed service (not self-managed).

I prefer hard-copy documents (post) and phone calls over email.

Please attend on Wednesdays and Fridays at around 11:00 a.m. for cleaning, followed by social support around 12:00 p.m. for coffee/outings.

I do not have a gender preference. I prefer workers who are fit, friendly and punctual, and able to complete floor and bathroom cleaning, weekly linen changes, and laundry coordination.

Please communicate slowly, clearly and a little louder, standing to my left to accommodate my hearing loss on the right.

I do not consent to students or third-party observers during my services.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Primary: Ben Switzer (son) – Mobile: 0419 782 414 – Lives in Frankston (Oliver’s Hill/Mornington area). Next of kin and emergency contact.

Secondary: Beata Shields (daughter) – 6 Ronald Street, Frankston – Mobile: 0401 338 961.

I also keep in regular contact with my stepdaughter Sarah.

Informal Supports

My children (Ben and Beata) are important supports. I speak with my stepdaughter Sarah often. I chat with people when I go out for coffee daily.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I worked as a boat builder and later in antiques/antiquities. I have two children (Ben and Beata), stepchildren (including Sarah), and a large extended family. I have experienced significant bereavement (three wives and my eldest son died from cancer). I had a past car accident about eight years ago.

Interests

I enjoy walking to the local shops for coffee most days and socialising. I used to paint (I have many paintings) but have stopped due to shaky hands. I have an interest in antiques and antiquities. I have a cat named Charlie.

My Medical Information

Medical History

Past car accident approximately eight years ago.

History of depression, including past suicidal ideation and being detained for safety more than five years ago; no recent events reported.

No recent hospital admissions reported. Not recently assessed for dementia/cognitive impairment.

No allergies or special dietary requirements reported.

Medication

I receive Webster-packed medicines from Chemist Warehouse and take them independently. I do not require assistance with medication, blood sugar monitoring, injections, or patches at this time.

Mobility and Equipment

I describe my mobility as independent. I occasionally use walking sticks. I have small hand weights at home. I have a personal alarm. I report no recent falls. I sometimes find getting into small taxis more difficult than in the past.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Isham, My Health Medical Centre, 28 Beach Street, Frankston.

Pharmacy: Chemist Warehouse (provider of Webster packs).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No – I speak English as my first language and identify as Christian.

Living with disability (mobility): Mild – I am independent but sometimes use walking sticks and find car ingress/egress harder than before.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes – I report a history of depression with past suicidal ideation over five years ago; I currently manage by staying active, keeping social contact, and engaging with my children.

Specific Risks

Hearing impairment (right ear) may affect communication and safety in the community.

History of depression with past suicidal ideation; current risk appears low but requires routine monitoring and prompt escalation if concerns arise.

Daily walks/coffee outings: risk of trip/fall or traffic hazards.

Spare key stored above door for worker access increases security exposure.

Firm preference to exclude Peninsula Health from care/referrals could limit local service options.

Use of taxis (CabCharge) for transport: potential risk when transferring in/out of vehicles.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Emergency actions: Perform CPR, call triple zero (000), and notify my family.

Access if no answer: Use spare key kept on the ledge above the door to enter and check on me.

Primary contact: Ben Switzer (son) – 0419 782 414.

Secondary contact: Beata Shields (daughter) – 0401 338 961.

Other: I have a personal alarm. I do not want Peninsula Health involved in my care.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my unit clean and comfortable so I can enjoy my days, with help on Wednesdays and Fridays for floors, bathroom, and weekly linen changes.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent but prefer help with heavier cleaning tasks. I am hard of hearing in my right ear, so clear communication helps. Security access via spare key is agreed if I don’t answer.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Domestic Assistance for vacuuming/mopping floors, cleaning the bathroom, changing and washing bed linen weekly, and coordinating pick-up/return of my external laundry service (Wettleswood).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Support Worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour Wednesday and 1 hour Friday starting 11:00 a.m. each week (for 3 months). How much will it cost?: $85/hour; 2 hours/week ≈ 8 hours/month = $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will get out for coffee and a chat twice a week after cleaning so I stay connected and feel less isolated.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I walk independently to local shops. I have a history of low mood; regular social contact helps. I use taxis when needed.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Social Support for companionship and local coffee outings after cleaning on Wednesdays and Fridays. Transport during the outing will be included as needed, with km charges as incurred.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Support Worker and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours Wednesday and 2 hours Friday from ~12:00 p.m. (for 3 months). How much will it cost?: Social Support $85/hour; 4 hours/week ≈ 16 hours/month = $1,360/month (+ $1.40/km if transport used).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: I will have about 10 prepared meals available each week so I eat well and have the energy to keep walking to the shops for coffee.

Abilities and considerations (risks): No special diet; I prefer medium-sized meals. I manage my own eating and heating of meals.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will coordinate meal delivery (Dynamic). I will order approximately 10 meals/week. I will store/freeze meals as needed and heat safely.

Who is responsible?: Me with Salveo HomeCare coordination. When will it be done?: Weekly ordering and deliveries for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Budget approx. $100/week total with a 70%/30% split (package approx. $70/week ≈ $280/month; my contribution approx. $30/week ≈ $120/month).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will maintain my strength and mobility so I can keep living independently and manage taxis and transfers safely.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with occasional use of walking sticks and find car ingress/egress a bit harder than before. No recent falls.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will arrange an Allied Health Therapist (Physiotherapist) initial assessment (2 hours), then provide 1-hour physiotherapy sessions fortnightly. I will participate in sessions and follow guidance as agreed with the therapist.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Physio) and me. When will it be done?: Initial 2-hour assessment in Month 1; then 1 hour fortnightly for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Allied Health Therapist (Physio) $180/hour; initial 2 hours = $360 (one-off), then 2 hours/month = $360/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 5 Goal: I will complete an Occupational Therapy (OT) assessment to check if any walking aids or equipment would help me at home or in the community.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I walk independently and sometimes use walking sticks. I want to prevent falls and keep my independence.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will schedule a 2-hour OT assessment at home. Recommended aids or modifications will be discussed with me, and only implemented with my agreement.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (OT) and me. When will it be done?: 2-hour assessment in Month 1. How much will it cost?: Allied Health Therapist (OT) $180/hour; 2 hours = $360 (one-off).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 6 Goal: I will maintain comfortable, healthy feet so I can keep walking to the shops daily.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I report no major foot problems and see a podiatrist monthly.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will arrange monthly home podiatry visits (Stellar). I will attend each visit and follow advice.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Podiatry) and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour monthly for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Allied Health Therapist (Podiatry) $180/hour; 1 hour/month = $180/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

Monthly package costs (estimates):

  • Everyday Living – Domestic Assistance: $680/month (2 hours/week at $85/hour)
  • Everyday Living – Meals (Dynamic) package share: $280/month (approx. $70/week; client contributes approx. $120/month separately)
  • Everyday Living – Transport (CabCharge budget): $300/month
  • Independence Support – Social Support/Outings: $1,360/month (4 hours/week at $85/hour) + $1.40/km as incurred
  • Clinical Care – Physiotherapy ongoing: $360/month (2 hours/month at $180/hour)
  • Clinical Care – Podiatry: $180/month (1 hour/month at $180/hour)
  • Clinical Care – One-off assessments in first month: OT $360 (2 hours); Physio initial $360 (2 hours)

Quarterly Budget Allocation (3 months):

  • Everyday Living subtotal: ($680 + $280 + $300) × 3 = $3,780
  • Independence Support subtotal: $1,360 × 3 = $4,080
  • Clinical Care subtotal ongoing: ($360 + $180) × 3 = $1,620
  • Clinical Care one-off (Month 1): OT $360 + Physio initial $360 = $720
  • Total estimated package spend for quarter: $3,780 + $4,080 + $1,620 + $720 = $10,200 (plus Social Support km charges as incurred)
  • Expected client co-contributions (outside package): Meals approx. $120/month × 3 = $360

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I provided informed consent to the SalveoCare service agreement by typing my name as my signature.

I consent to SalveoCare contacting my GP (Dr Isham) to discuss my health needs.

I consent to SalveoCare audits and to the use of audio, video, or photographs for care planning and therapy. I consented to the use of images/media for electronic/social media as discussed.

I do not consent to any third-party observers (students/clinicians) being present during my services.

I prefer copies of agreements and care plans to be posted to me in hard copy. Phone contact is preferred over email.
