saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I prefer hard-copy documents and phone contact rather than email or online communication.

I am hard of hearing in my right ear. Please speak slowly, clearly and a little louder on my left side. I own hearing aids but rarely use them.

In an emergency I want CPR performed, triple zero (000) called, and my family notified.

If I do not answer the door at a scheduled visit, please use my spare key (kept on the ledge on top of the door) to gain access and check on me.

I have a personal alarm in my home.

I do not consent to Peninsula Health being involved in my care or referrals.

I do not consent to students or third parties being present during my services for observation or supervision.

Pet on premises: cat (Charlie).

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 2025-09-02

Preferred Name: Peter

Full Name: Peter Anthony Switzer

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I participated in developing this plan with my Salveo HomeCare Care Partner. I am responsible for making my own decisions. My family (Ben and Beata) were identified as my preferred support people and emergency contacts.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I was born in Mount Albert. I identify as Christian and usually attend Frankston Community Baptist Church. There are no additional cultural or diversity considerations documented.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer a fully managed service (not self-managed).

I prefer hard-copy documents (post) and phone calls over email.

Please attend on Wednesdays and Fridays at around 11:00 a.m. for cleaning, followed by social support around 12:00 p.m. for coffee/outings.

I do not have a gender preference. I prefer workers who are fit, friendly and punctual, and able to complete floor and bathroom cleaning, weekly linen changes, and laundry coordination.

Please communicate slowly, clearly and a little louder, standing to my left to accommodate my hearing loss on the right.

I do not consent to students or third-party observers during my services.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Primary: Ben Switzer (son) – Mobile: 0419 782 414 – Lives in Frankston (Oliver’s Hill/Mornington area). Next of kin and emergency contact.

Secondary: Beata Shields (daughter) – 6 Ronald Street, Frankston – Mobile: 0401 338 961.

I also keep in regular contact with my stepdaughter Sarah.

Informal Supports

My children (Ben and Beata) are important supports. I speak with my stepdaughter Sarah often. I chat with people when I go out for coffee daily.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I worked as a boat builder and later in antiques/antiquities. I have two children (Ben and Beata), stepchildren (including Sarah), and a large extended family. I have experienced significant bereavement (three wives and my eldest son died from cancer). I had a past car accident about eight years ago.

Interests

I enjoy walking to the local shops for coffee most days and socialising. I used to paint (I have many paintings) but have stopped due to shaky hands. I have an interest in antiques and antiquities. I have a cat named Charlie.

My Medical Information

Medical History

Past car accident approximately eight years ago.

History of depression, including past suicidal ideation and being detained for safety more than five years ago; no recent events reported.

No recent hospital admissions reported. Not recently assessed for dementia/cognitive impairment.

No allergies or special dietary requirements reported.

Medication

I receive Webster-packed medicines from Chemist Warehouse and take them independently. I do not require assistance with medication, blood sugar monitoring, injections, or patches at this time.

Mobility and Equipment

I describe my mobility as independent. I occasionally use walking sticks. I have small hand weights at home. I have a personal alarm. I report no recent falls. I sometimes find getting into small taxis more difficult than in the past.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Isham, My Health Medical Centre, 28 Beach Street, Frankston.

Pharmacy: Chemist Warehouse (provider of Webster packs).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No – I speak English as my first language and identify as Christian.

Living with disability (mobility): Mild – I am independent but sometimes use walking sticks and find car ingress/egress harder than before.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes – I report a history of depression with past suicidal ideation over five years ago; I currently manage by staying active, keeping social contact, and engaging with my children.

Specific Risks

Hearing impairment (right ear) may affect communication and safety in the community.

History of depression with past suicidal ideation; current risk appears low but requires routine monitoring and prompt escalation if concerns arise.

Daily walks/coffee outings: risk of trip/fall or traffic hazards.

Spare key stored above door for worker access increases security exposure.

Firm preference to exclude Peninsula Health from care/referrals could limit local service options.

Use of taxis (CabCharge) for transport: potential risk when transferring in/out of vehicles.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Emergency actions: Perform CPR, call triple zero (000), and notify my family.

Access if no answer: Use spare key kept on the ledge above the door to enter and check on me.

Primary contact: Ben Switzer (son) – 0419 782 414.

Secondary contact: Beata Shields (daughter) – 0401 338 961.

Other: I have a personal alarm. I do not want Peninsula Health involved in my care.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my unit clean and comfortable so I can enjoy my days, with help on Wednesdays and Fridays for floors, bathroom, and weekly linen changes.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent but prefer help with heavier cleaning tasks. I am hard of hearing in my right ear, so clear communication helps. Security access via spare key is agreed if I don’t answer.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Domestic Assistance for vacuuming/mopping floors, cleaning the bathroom, changing and washing bed linen weekly, and coordinating pick-up/return of my external laundry service (Wettleswood).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Support Worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour Wednesday and 1 hour Friday starting 11:00 a.m. each week (for 3 months). How much will it cost?: $85/hour; 2 hours/week ≈ 8 hours/month = $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will get out for coffee and a chat twice a week after cleaning so I stay connected and feel less isolated.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I walk independently to local shops. I have a history of low mood; regular social contact helps. I use taxis when needed.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Social Support for companionship and local coffee outings after cleaning on Wednesdays and Fridays. Transport during the outing will be included as needed, with km charges as incurred.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Support Worker and me. When will it be done?: 2 hours Wednesday and 2 hours Friday from ~12:00 p.m. (for 3 months). How much will it cost?: Social Support $85/hour; 4 hours/week ≈ 16 hours/month = $1,360/month (+ $1.40/km if transport used).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: I will have about 10 prepared meals available each week so I eat well and have the energy to keep walking to the shops for coffee.

Abilities and considerations (risks): No special diet; I prefer medium-sized meals. I manage my own eating and heating of meals.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will coordinate meal delivery (Dynamic). I will order approximately 10 meals/week. I will store/freeze meals as needed and heat safely.

Who is responsible?: Me with Salveo HomeCare coordination. When will it be done?: Weekly ordering and deliveries for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Budget approx. $100/week total with a 70%/30% split (package approx. $70/week ≈ $280/month; my contribution approx. $30/week ≈ $120/month).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will maintain my strength and mobility so I can keep living independently and manage taxis and transfers safely.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with occasional use of walking sticks and find car ingress/egress a bit harder than before. No recent falls.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will arrange an Allied Health Therapist (Physiotherapist) initial assessment (2 hours), then provide 1-hour physiotherapy sessions fortnightly. I will participate in sessions and follow guidance as agreed with the therapist.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Physio) and me. When will it be done?: Initial 2-hour assessment in Month 1; then 1 hour fortnightly for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Allied Health Therapist (Physio) $180/hour; initial 2 hours = $360 (one-off), then 2 hours/month = $360/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 5 Goal: I will complete an Occupational Therapy (OT) assessment to check if any walking aids or equipment would help me at home or in the community.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I walk independently and sometimes use walking sticks. I want to prevent falls and keep my independence.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will schedule a 2-hour OT assessment at home. Recommended aids or modifications will be discussed with me, and only implemented with my agreement.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (OT) and me. When will it be done?: 2-hour assessment in Month 1. How much will it cost?: Allied Health Therapist (OT) $180/hour; 2 hours = $360 (one-off).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 6 Goal: I will maintain comfortable, healthy feet so I can keep walking to the shops daily.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I report no major foot problems and see a podiatrist monthly.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will arrange monthly home podiatry visits (Stellar). I will attend each visit and follow advice.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Podiatry) and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour monthly for 3 months. How much will it cost?: Allied Health Therapist (Podiatry) $180/hour; 1 hour/month = $180/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

Monthly package costs (estimates):

  • Everyday Living – Domestic Assistance: $680/month (2 hours/week at $85/hour)
  • Everyday Living – Meals (Dynamic) package share: $280/month (approx. $70/week; client contributes approx. $120/month separately)
  • Everyday Living – Transport (CabCharge budget): $300/month
  • Independence Support – Social Support/Outings: $1,360/month (4 hours/week at $85/hour) + $1.40/km as incurred
  • Clinical Care – Physiotherapy ongoing: $360/month (2 hours/month at $180/hour)
  • Clinical Care – Podiatry: $180/month (1 hour/month at $180/hour)
  • Clinical Care – One-off assessments in first month: OT $360 (2 hours); Physio initial $360 (2 hours)

Quarterly Budget Allocation (3 months):

  • Everyday Living subtotal: ($680 + $280 + $300) × 3 = $3,780
  • Independence Support subtotal: $1,360 × 3 = $4,080
  • Clinical Care subtotal ongoing: ($360 + $180) × 3 = $1,620
  • Clinical Care one-off (Month 1): OT $360 + Physio initial $360 = $720
  • Total estimated package spend for quarter: $3,780 + $4,080 + $1,620 + $720 = $10,200 (plus Social Support km charges as incurred)
  • Expected client co-contributions (outside package): Meals approx. $120/month × 3 = $360

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I provided informed consent to the SalveoCare service agreement by typing my name as my signature.

I consent to SalveoCare contacting my GP (Dr Isham) to discuss my health needs.

I consent to SalveoCare audits and to the use of audio, video, or photographs for care planning and therapy. I consented to the use of images/media for electronic/social media as discussed.

I do not consent to any third-party observers (students/clinicians) being present during my services.

I prefer copies of agreements and care plans to be posted to me in hard copy. Phone contact is preferred over email.

Prepared By (Name: __________ | Role: Care Partner, Date: Today | Review Date: Quarterly (every 3 months) | Signature: __________)

I chose a fully managed service, set my preferred days/times, and set boundaries (no third-party observers, no Peninsula Health involvement). My communication needs (right-ear hearing loss) and preferences (hard copies) are respected.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers

My plan was co-designed with me. Allied health assessments (OT and Physio) are scheduled. My risks and preferences (CPR, emergency access, spare key) are documented, with quarterly review.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care

Clinical supports include physiotherapy, podiatry, and an OT assessment. I manage my own medications via Webster packs. There are no personal care needs at present.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living

Domestic Assistance (floors, bathroom, linen, laundry coordination), meal coordination (Dynamic), social support for coffee/outings, and transport via CabCharge are in place to maintain my independence and community participation.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment

saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have clearly stated that I do not want resuscitation (DNR) if I experience a medical emergency while care is being provided. Call 000 and notify my family (Craig) as per my preference.

I have Type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, osteoarthritis (constant pain usually 5/10, up to 10/10 during flares), and lymphedema. Heat can worsen my arthritis pain.

I am allergic to morphine, Acupan, Dacogridic, and Ghatran.

I have hearing issues; please speak clearly and loudly so I can hear you.

I am at increased risk of skin issues and occasional ulcers. Please monitor my skin integrity, especially on my legs.

I have limited mobility and use a walker (frame) as my preferred aid. I do not feel safe using walking sticks except when a walker cannot fit (e.g., at Claudette’s father’s place).

I prefer a female care worker for showering support.

I have a personal medical alarm (Live Life) and wear it for emergencies.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 02 September 2025

Preferred Name: Lydia

Full Name: Lydia Mae Goodwin

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan together with Thomas (Care Partner) during my intake assessment. I make my own decisions and have enduring power of attorney in place with Claudette and Craig.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I was born in Balclutha, New Zealand. I identify as Anglican (not currently attending services). I value family, good manners and morals, my independence, and peace in the world. I do not have specific cultural matching requirements for workers.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer care workers to speak clearly and loudly due to my hearing issues. On bad days (pain or digestive issues), I prefer to be left alone.

I prefer a female worker for showering support. I am open to any gender, age, or cultural background for other services.

My preferred times are mornings: showering on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 9:00am, and domestic assistance on Mondays at 10:00am. Transport/social support is every second Tuesday 9:00am–12:00pm.

Entry instructions: workers can walk down the side of the gate to my door. Please note I have one cat who may jump to greet people.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

Craig is my primary support person in an emergency. Claudette and Craig hold my enduring power of attorney.

Informal Supports

My family help if needed, although I try not to ask. I have previously received council supports (personal care, cleaning once monthly, and transport/social support).

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

My father died when I was four and I was raised in care homes. I met my husband at 17 and married in November 1962. I worked in retail, factory work, hospitals, and later a woollen factory before retiring. I moved from New Zealand to Australia on April 1 (arriving April 2) two years before this assessment. I have one child and two grandchildren. I later discovered I was one of 11 siblings; I know my youngest brother and sister.

Interests

I enjoy reading, crosswords, and playing word games on the computer. I have one cat. I love country music and used to attend a club; I also follow genealogy online.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have Type 2 diabetes, lymphedema, osteoarthritis, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, and atrial fibrillation (I can experience shortness of breath). I report constant pain from osteoarthritis (5/10 baseline; up to 10/10 during flares), worse in hot weather. I occasionally experience skin ulcers and need to monitor skin integrity. I have full dentures.

Medication

I take my medications regularly and receive them in a Webster pack from the in-house pharmacy at my medical centre. I take osteoarthritis pain tablets once daily and increase to three times daily during flares as needed. I do not need assistance with medication administration. I see a diabetes educator. I have allergies to morphine, Acupan, Dacogridic, and Ghatran.

Mobility and Equipment

My mobility is limited. I prefer to use a walker (frame). I have a wheelchair, walkers, crutches, a medical chair, a shower chair, bathroom handrails, and a ramp at the front of my home. I do not use a raised toilet seat because my toilet is higher set. I use my personal alarm (Live Life) for emergencies.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Dina L. Halawani, HAFI Medical Centre.

Pharmacy: HAFI Medical Centre in-house pharmacy (Webster packs supplied).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: I am New Zealand-born and English-speaking; no interpreter required.

Living with disability (mobility): I have limited mobility and rely on a walker; I cannot stand for long and use pacing (sit and rest) to manage pain.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I prefer to be left alone on bad days. I am currently a homebody and connect online, which may place me at some risk of isolation.

Specific Risks

Falls risk due to limited mobility and occasional need to use walking sticks where a walker cannot fit. I mitigate by pacing, sitting to rest when pain increases, and using installed rails and the shower chair.

Pain flares in hot weather due to osteoarthritis. I manage this with prescribed pain medication and rest.

Skin integrity risk (history of occasional ulcers; lymphedema). I use appropriate skincare products (DMEs) and monitor for new skin issues.

Cardiometabolic risks (Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, atrial fibrillation). I follow my medication regimen and diabetic diet and attend diabetes education.

Hearing impairment may affect communication; workers should speak clearly and loudly.

Emergency preference for no resuscitation (DNR). In an emergency, call 000 and notify Craig.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If I do not answer for a scheduled visit, follow provider protocol and attempt contact. If concerns persist, escalate to welfare check per policy.

During a medical emergency while providing care: do not perform resuscitation; call 000 and notify my family (Craig). Use my personal alarm (Live Life) if appropriate.

Entry: walk down the side of the gate to my door. Please be mindful that my cat may jump to greet you.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will feel clean, safe, and supported with showering while keeping my independence, with a female worker helping with my back and hair on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 9:00am over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can complete parts of my shower but need help with hard-to-reach areas due to pain and limited mobility. I prefer to be left alone on bad days. I have lymphedema and occasional skin ulcers, so gentle handling and skin checks are important.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Provide personal care support for showering (assist with back wash and hair wash; ensure bathroom safety using rails and shower chair; observe skin and report concerns; support pacing on pain days).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker (female) and me. When will it be done?: 3 x 1 hour weekly at 9:00am (Mon/Wed/Fri), starting 1 September. How much will it be?: Personal Care $85/hour (day). Estimated monthly cost (4 weeks): 12 hours/month × $85 = $1,020.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 2 Goal: I will keep my home tidy and safe by having vacuuming, mopping, bathroom cleaning, and bed linen changed every Monday at 10:00am so I can manage better with my pain over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot stand for long and need to pace tasks. Clean, dry floors and fresh bedding reduce slip and skin risks.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Domestic assistance for vacuuming, mopping, bathroom clean, and bed linen change immediately after my Monday shower.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour weekly on Mondays at 10:00am, ongoing from 1 September. How much will it be?: Domestic Assistance $85/hour (day). Estimated monthly cost (4 weeks): 4 hours/month × $85 = $340.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: Every second Tuesday I will go to Karingal to pick up my magazines, do a little shopping, and have a coffee so I stay connected and happy, aiming for 6 outings in the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): My mobility is limited and pain can flare. I use a walker and may need rest breaks.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Provide transport and social support for community access, including assistance with walking safely, carrying shopping, and taking rest breaks as needed.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me. When will it be done?: Fortnightly Tuesdays 9:00am–12:00pm (approximately 3 hours per outing), starting 1 September. How much will it be?: Social Support/Transport $85/hour (day). Estimated monthly cost (2 outings/6 hours): 6 × $85 = $510, plus mileage at $1.40/km as incurred.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 4 Goal: I will complete an Occupational Therapy assessment and implement agreed recommendations to make daily activities (shower, transfers, mobility at home) safer and easier within the next 8 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have a shower chair, rails, ramp, and walker. I need pacing due to pain and fatigue. I want to remain as independent as possible.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Arrange an in-home OT assessment; review current equipment and layout; co-design activity pacing strategies; implement practical changes (no structural works beyond agreed scope).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (OT) and me. When will it be done?: One 2-hour assessment within the first month; follow-up actions completed within 8 weeks. How much will it be?: Allied Health Therapist (OT) $180/hour × 2 hours = $360 (one-off this quarter).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 5 Goal: I will keep my feet healthy with regular podiatry because of my diabetes and hammer toes, aiming for two podiatry visits this quarter and eight per year.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Diabetes increases foot risk; I have foot issues including hammer toes. Skin integrity requires monitoring.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Schedule and receive podiatry visits; escalate any wounds/ulcers promptly; ensure safe nail and skin care.

Who is responsible?: Podiatry provider arranged by Salveo and me. When will it be done?: Approximately every 6–8 weeks (target 2 visits this quarter). How much will it be?: Clinical Care under Support at Home (government funded) – no client charge.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 6 Goal: I will keep my home safe with minor maintenance (gutters, windows, small repairs like loose nails/boards) completed as scheduled, with at least one 3-hour visit in the next 6 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot safely do ladder or repair work. Loose boards and protruding nails are tripping hazards.

saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have a Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) preference: I do not want resuscitation performed during a medical emergency while care is being delivered. Call 000 and notify my support people.

I am diabetic (Type 2) and follow a diabetic diet. I have Barrett’s oesophagus and cannot eat lettuce, bananas, or tomatoes. I prefer small portions.

I have allergies to: morphine, Acupan, Dacogridic, and Ghatran.

I have hearing issues; please speak clearly and loudly, and check my understanding.

I live with osteoarthritis pain (baseline 5/10; up to 10/10 with flares). Heat worsens my pain.

I have lymphedema and occasional skin ulcers; monitor skin integrity and avoid skin breaks.

I have atrial fibrillation and hypertension; monitor for shortness of breath and dizziness.

I have limited mobility and use a walker; I am at increased falls risk, especially in the bathroom and during transfers.

I have a Live Life personal alarm (subscription ~$75/year) and will use it in emergencies.

I prefer female workers for showering support.

I have a cat; please be mindful of a potential trip hazard on entry.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 2 September 2025

Preferred Name: Lydia

Full Name: Lydia Mae Goodwin

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I participated in this assessment and plan with Thomas (care partner/home care representative). I make my own decisions. Claudette and Craig hold my Enduring Power of Attorney. My GP is Dr Dina Halawani (HAFI Medical Centre). These people may be contacted to support my care, with my consent.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I was born in Balclutha, New Zealand. I identify as Anglican but I am not currently attending services.

My values include family, good manners/morals, my independence, and peace in the world.

I do not have any specific cultural match preferences for workers.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer female workers for showering support.

Please speak clearly and loudly due to my hearing issues, and confirm my understanding.

On bad days (pain or digestive issues), I prefer to be left alone and have privacy; please check what I want on the day.

Service times agreed: Personal Care Monday/Wednesday/Friday at 9:00–10:00; Domestic Assistance Mondays 10:00–11:00; Transport/Social Support every second Tuesday 9:00–12:00. Home maintenance twice per year (3 hours each).

Please do not schedule cleaning before the shower on Mondays; 10:00 a.m. is suitable after my 9:00 a.m. shower.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Craig – family support and emergency contact; Enduring Power of Attorney.

Claudette – family support; Enduring Power of Attorney.

Claudette’s mum – supportive.

My sisters and close friends (including friends in New Zealand, such as Sarah) are important to me.

Informal Supports

My family helps me as needed. I also use a personal alarm (Live Life) for emergencies.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was raised in care homes after my father died when I was four. I met my husband at 17 and married in November 1962. I worked in retail, factory work, hospitals, and later in a woollen factory before retiring. I moved from New Zealand to Australia on 1 April (arriving 2 April) two years before this assessment.

I have one child and two grandchildren. I later learned I am one of 11 siblings and came to know some siblings in adulthood.

Interests

I enjoy reading, crosswords, and playing word games on the computer. I like country music and previously belonged to a country music club. I also participate online in genealogy groups. I have one cat.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

Type 2 diabetes; lymphedema; osteoarthritis; hypercholesterolemia; hypertension; atrial fibrillation; Barrett’s oesophagus (dietary restrictions noted).

Pain: constant osteoarthritis pain (average 5/10; up to 10/10 during flares). Heat worsens my pain.

Skin: occasional ulcers; use of emollients (DMEs); no current wound dressings.

Cognition: no concerns raised in assessment.

Allergies: morphine, Acupan, Dacogridic, Ghatran.

Medication:

I take regular medications supplied in a Webstar pack from my medical centre’s in-house pharmacy. I take osteoarthritis pain tablets once daily, and up to three times daily during flares. I self-manage my medicines and do not require assistance. I see a diabetes educator as needed.

Mobility and Equipment:

I have limited mobility and primarily use a walker frame. I have walking sticks (used only when a walker won’t fit), a wheelchair, crutches, a medical chair, a shower chair, handrails in the bathroom, and a front ramp. I do not use a raised toilet seat because my toilet is higher-set. I can get in/out of a car if it is not too high. I wear full dentures.

GP / Pharmacy:

GP: Dr Dina Halawani, HAFI Medical Centre.

Pharmacy: HAFI Medical Centre in-house pharmacy (provides Webstar packs).

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No – I speak English and do not require an interpreter.

Living with disability (mobility): Yes – limited mobility; walker dependent; bathroom and transfer risks.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I prefer to be left alone on bad days; there is some risk of social withdrawal during pain or digestive flares.

Specific Risks

  • Falls risk related to limited mobility, osteoarthritis pain, and bathroom transfers.
  • Skin integrity risk due to lymphedema and occasional ulcers.
  • Cardiac/respiratory symptoms related to atrial fibrillation and hypertension.
  • Communication risk due to hearing issues – need clear, loud, and paced communication.
  • Nutritional risk if dietary restrictions are not followed (diabetes and Barrett’s oesophagus).
  • Heat exacerbates pain, increasing functional limitation on hot days.
  • Emergency preparedness: I rely on my personal alarm and family; I do not have a formal emergency kit.
  • Trip hazard on entry due to my cat and general home environment.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If I do not respond at a scheduled visit, please follow my safety plan: knock and call out, phone me and my nominated support people, and if concerned for my safety, call 000. I use a Live Life personal alarm and will activate it if needed.

During any medical emergency while care is being provided: do not perform resuscitation (DNR); call 000 and notify Craig and Claudette as my support people/EPOA.

Primary family support: Craig (family, EPOA) and Claudette (family, EPOA). Contact details will be provided to the care provider and attached to my file.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will shower safely with dignity on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 9 a.m., with help for my back and hair washing, so I feel clean and reduce skin problems over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have limited mobility, lymphedema, and occasional skin ulcers. I prefer a female worker. Falls risk in the bathroom is present.

How will we do this? (Tasks): A female Salveo support worker will assist with showering, including washing my back and hair, setting up my shower chair, checking water temperature, drying thoroughly (especially skin folds), and documenting skin checks each visit.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Personal Care worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour, Monday/Wednesday/Friday at 9–10 a.m., weekly for 12 weeks. How much will it be cost?: Personal Care $85/hour; 3 hours/week x 4 weeks = $1,020/month (Independence Support).

Service Category: Clinical Care / Independence Support / Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will keep my home clean and manageable so I do not need to stand for long periods and my bathroom and linens are fresh each week for the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Standing increases my pain. I need help with vacuuming, mopping, changing bed sheets, and bathroom cleaning.

How will we do this? (Tasks): After my Monday shower, the worker will vacuum/mop high-traffic areas, clean the bathroom, and change my bed sheets. Tasks will be rotated if time is limited.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Domestic Assistance worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour every Monday 10–11 a.m., weekly for 12 weeks. How much will it be cost?: Domestic Assistance $85/hour; 1 hour/week x 4 weeks = $340/month (Everyday Living).

Service Category: Clinical Care / Independence Support / Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: Every second Tuesday, I will go to Karingal to pick up my magazines, do light shopping, and have a coffee (9 a.m.–12 p.m.) to maintain my independence and enjoyment of community life over the next 3 months (aim: at least 5 outings).

Abilities and considerations (risks): I use a walker, have hearing issues, and may tire; I prefer a worker to stay with me for safety and company.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo will provide door-to-door transport, accompany me with my walker, assist with shopping, and allow time for a coffee. Rest breaks will be taken as needed.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Social Support/Transport worker and me. When will it be done?: 3 hours fortnightly (Tuesdays 9 a.m.–12 p.m.) for 12 weeks. How much will it be cost?: Social Support/Transport $85/hour; ~6 hours/month = $510/month, plus $1.40/km for mileage (Everyday Living).

Service Category: Clinical Care / Independence Support / Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will maintain my foot health (hammer toes and other foot issues) to prevent ulcers and falls by completing podiatry visits as scheduled (target 2 sessions this quarter).

Abilities and considerations (risks): Diabetes and lymphedema increase skin and ulcer risk; I have foot deformities and need regular podiatry.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo will arrange allied health podiatry to trim nails, reduce callus/corns as required, assess footwear, and update my foot care plan. Workers will observe and report any foot skin changes.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Podiatry) and me. When will it be done?: 1-hour sessions, approximately every 6 weeks (2 sessions in 12 weeks). How much will it be cost?: Allied Health Therapist (Podiatry) $180/hour; average ~$120/month (2 sessions/quarter = $360/quarter). Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded).

Service Category: Clinical Care / Independence Support / Everyday Living

GOAL 5 Goal: I will complete an Occupational Therapy home safety and equipment assessment to confirm my equipment is optimal and reduce falls risk this quarter.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I already use a walker, shower chair, and handrails; I have bathroom and transfer risks.

How will we do this? (Tasks): A Salveo OT will conduct a 2-hour IAT-aligned assessment, review transfers and bathroom setup, and provide recommendations (e.g., layout, technique, minor AT). Any changes will be explained and, if agreed, implemented.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health Therapist (OT), Care Partner, and me. When will it be done?: One 2-hour assessment within 12 weeks. How much will it be cost?: $180/hour x 2 hours = $360 (one-off this quarter). Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded).

Service Category: Clinical Care / Independence Support / Everyday Living

GOAL 6 Goal: I will keep my home safe and maintained (gutters, windows, and minor repairs like loose nails/boards) to reduce trip hazards and water ingress, with seasonal work scheduled over the year.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Outdoor tasks are unsafe for me due to mobility and balance limitations.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo will book Light Home & Gardening Maintenance for 3 hours twice per year. Tasks will include gutter clearing, window cleaning, and minor safety fixes. If due this quarter, one visit will be completed.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Home & Garden Maintenance team and me. When will it be done?: 3 hours twice per year (schedule as seasonally due). How much will it be cost?: $85/hour; 6 hours/year = $510/year (~$42.50/month; ~$127.50/quarter) (Everyday Living).

Service Category: Clinical Care / Independence Support / Everyday Living

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

  • Personal Care (Independence Support): 3 hours/week at $85/hour = $1,020/month; ~$3,060/quarter.
  • Domestic Assistance (Everyday Living): 1 hour/week at $85/hour = $340/month; ~$1,020/quarter.
  • Social Support/Transport (Everyday Living): ~6 hours/month at $85/hour = ~$510/month; ~$1,530/quarter, plus $1.40/km mileage.
  • Light Home & Gardening Maintenance (Everyday Living): 6 hours/year at $85/hour = $510/year; ~$42.50/month; ~$127.50/quarter.
  • Allied Health – Podiatry (Clinical Care): ~$180/hour; ~2 sessions/quarter = $360/quarter (avg. $120/month).
  • Allied Health – OT Assessment (Clinical Care): 2 hours x $180 = $360 (one-off this quarter).
  • Personal Alarm Subscription (Everyday Living): ~$75/year; ~$6.25/month; ~$18.75/quarter.

Quarterly Budget Allocation

  • Clinical Care (government funded): ~$720/quarter (OT $360 once + Podiatry $360). Subsequent quarters typically ~$360 for podiatry unless another OT review is required.
  • Independence Support: ~$3,060/quarter (Personal Care).
  • Everyday Living: ~$2,696.25/quarter (Domestic Assistance $1,020 + Social/Transport $1,530 + Maintenance $127.50 + Alarm $18.75), plus mileage at $1.40/km for transport.
  • Estimated total this quarter: ~$6,476.25 + mileage.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

I agree with this care plan and the services outlined. I consent to share this plan with my GP (Dr Dina Halawani, HAFI Medical Centre), my in-house pharmacy, my Salveo care team, and my Enduring Power of Attorney holders (Claudette and Craig) for the purposes of coordinating my care. Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have severe breathlessness from emphysema/COPD and can only walk about 10 metres before I need to rest.

I have a history of depression and a recent suicide attempt (three-week admission to a mental health ward about six months ago). My mood is strongly affected by grief about my wife entering permanent care.

I have had recent falls (including falling backwards onto my buttock and cutting my leg). I currently do not use my recommended four-wheel walker because I find using and transporting it exhausting.

I prefer not to receive CPR (no resuscitation), however I do not currently have a formal Advance Care Directive/DNAR in place. I want staff to call 000 first and then call Darryl (my son).

I smoke and I sometimes leave heating on overnight, which affects my breathing. This increases my respiratory risk.

I live with a small dog (Rambo) which may present a trip hazard when I am short of breath.

I continue to drive but fatigue and breathlessness can affect my capacity.

I prefer a pendant-style personal alarm and have agreed to wear it daily once supplied.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 04 September 2025

Preferred Name: Ian

Full Name: Ian Hood

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan with Thomas (Salveo Care – Care Partner) and my son Darryl. I am the decision-maker for my care. I agree that Salveo Care will coordinate my services with my consent.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I did not identify any cultural factors that need to be considered when matching me with workers.

My values include staying in control of my choices, being treated with respect, and being supported to stay connected with my wife and my dog, Rambo.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I do not have a preference for worker gender, age, or cultural background.

I prefer my weekly social support on Wednesdays from 12:00 to 2:30 pm (2.5 hours). If this needs to change, please discuss the options with me.

If a worker arrives and I do not answer, please call me first. If there is still no response, please call Darryl.

Please communicate clearly. I do not require hearing or vision support at this time.

I have a dog (Rambo); please ensure the gate is closed and be mindful of trip hazards.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

My preferred contact and advocate is my son Darryl.

Other important people in my life include my wife (in permanent aged care), friends and neighbours: Bruce and Anne (across the road), Josie, Glenn and Cherry, Terri, Kevin, Brendan, Bernie, and Robin.

Informal Supports

Darryl assists me with many things including pension arrangements, coordinating meal deliveries, and general support. Friends and neighbours check in on me at times.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I grew up in Melbourne near the zoo with two brothers and three sisters. I worked at a malt house in Collingwood (James Hood & Company) as a young man and later owned a laundromat in Noble Park for around 20 years, which I sold about 1.5 years ago. I have three children and five grandchildren. I am deeply devoted to my wife, who is now in permanent care with Alzheimer’s disease.

Interests

I enjoy time with my dog Rambo, sitting outside in the sun, occasional visits to the pokies with a strict $20 limit, and listening to music. I used to love playing tennis and would like support to keep socially connected, including visiting my wife.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

I have emphysema/COPD with severe breathlessness and limited exercise tolerance (about 10 metres before stopping). I have a history of depression and was admitted to a mental health ward for three weeks around six months ago following a suicide attempt. I have a brain aneurysm that is not suitable for surgery due to my age. I had prostate cancer treated with radiation (circa 2007) and had a skin cancer removed about two years ago. I report frustration and low mood, often triggered by grief about my wife.

Medication:

I take medications morning and night and use a puffer. My medicines are supplied in a Webster/blister pack by Chemist Warehouse. I manage my own medications and do not need prompts currently.

Mobility and Equipment:

My mobility is limited by breathlessness and fatigue. I have been recommended a four-wheel walker but I do not use it because getting it in and out of the car and using it is exhausting. I have had recent falls. I have handrails in the toilet, bathroom, shower, and at the back door. I do not have a shower chair, raised toilet seat, or bed transfer pole. An OT assessment was discussed and may be scheduled depending on whether I move to Darryl’s home.

GP / Pharmacy:

My GP is Dr Atul Desai (Forest Hill Medical Centre). My current pharmacy is Chemist Warehouse, 415 Springvale Road (Forest Hill). If I move to Darryl’s home, I prefer to transfer my pharmacy to one closer to Croydon.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No.

Living with disability (mobility): Yes – severe breathlessness, limited endurance, recent falls.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes – diagnosed depression; recent suicide attempt; grief related to wife’s illness; social isolation risk.

Specific Risks

  • Falls: Recent falls, limited endurance, does not use recommended walker, dog underfoot.
  • Respiratory: Severe breathlessness (emphysema/COPD); smoking; heating left on overnight worsened morning breath.
  • Mood and suicide risk: Past suicide attempt; ongoing low mood and grief; limited daily structure.
  • Driving: Still driving despite fatigue and breathlessness.
  • Home environment: No shower chair or raised toilet seat; potential bathroom transfer risks.
  • Emergency response: Preference for no CPR without a formal DNAR; pendant alarm not yet supplied.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If I experience a medical emergency while support is being provided, I want staff to call Triple Zero (000) first and then call Darryl.

I prefer not to receive CPR. I understand that without a formal medical order, ambulance staff may still perform resuscitation. I agree to discuss formalising my Advance Care Directive/DNAR with my GP.

If a support worker arrives for a scheduled visit and I do not respond: call me first, then call Darryl. Follow Salveo escalation if no contact is made.

Primary Emergency Contact: Darryl (son). Phone: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Other Contacts: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will have a consistent weekly companion to help me get out, visit my wife, or have company at home so I feel less lonely and keep my routine.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I get short of breath after about 10 metres and tire easily. I have recently fallen. My mood is affected by grief. I do best with support scheduled in the middle of the week.

How will we do this? (Tasks): A Salveo HomeCare support worker will visit every Wednesday 12:00–2:30 pm (2.5 hours) for social support and escorted outings as I choose (for example, visiting my wife, short outings such as the shops or pokies with my $20 limit, or company at home). The worker will monitor my breathlessness, prompt rest breaks, manage the dog gate, and encourage safe pacing.

Who is responsible?: I agree to this plan; Salveo Care will roster a suitable worker and maintain continuity. When will it be done?: Weekly for the next 3 months (quarter), starting the week of the 25th. How much will it cost?: Social Support at $85/hour (day rates) for 2.5 hours weekly = $212.50/week (about $850/month), plus transport if used at $1.40/km.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 2 Goal: I will improve my safety at home and when alone by using a pendant-style personal alarm every day so I can get help quickly if I fall or feel unwell.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have had recent falls and severe breathlessness. I prefer a neck pendant that I can put on with my morning medications and wear until bedtime.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo will purchase a pendant alarm with fall detection and GPS. Darryl and I will nominate responders. I will put the pendant on each morning with my medications and wear it through the day. Salveo will confirm activation and test calls.

Who is responsible?: I will wear the pendant daily; Salveo Care will procure, set up, and test it; Darryl will be a listed responder. When will it be done?: Within the next 2 weeks from plan start. How much will it cost?: One-off equipment purchase $567 (no ongoing fee as discussed).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: I will keep my block tidy and safe with regular lawn mowing so my home does not look unattended and I reduce outdoor trip hazards.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot manage physical garden work due to breathlessness. A tidy frontage also reduces the risk of the property looking vacant if I am away.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo will arrange Light Home & Gardening Maintenance for lawn mowing and light tidy once a month (about 1 hour) with attention to paths and gates for safe access.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Care will schedule a regular gardener; I will let the office know if timing needs to change. When will it be done?: Monthly for the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 1 hour monthly = $85/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will complete an Occupational Therapy (OT) assessment to review safer mobility options (for example, an ultra-light 4WW or wheelchair for outings) so I can comfortably get to places I enjoy, including visiting my wife.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I currently avoid my walker due to effort and breathlessness. I have had recent falls. The assessment timing depends on whether I remain at my current address or move to Darryl’s home.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo will arrange an Allied Health OT assessment (home safety and mobility equipment). I will trial any clinician-recommended devices and decide what I will use. Equipment will only be purchased if clinically justified and agreed by me.

Who is responsible?: Salveo Care to coordinate; I will participate and provide consent. When will it be done?: Within the next 3 months if I remain at my current address, or rescheduled promptly after any move. How much will it cost?: Allied Health Therapist (OT) $180/hour x 2 hours = $360 (one-off).

Service Category: Clinical Care

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

Quarterly Budget Allocation

  • Independence Support – Social Support: 2.5 hours/week at $85/hour ≈ $850/month ≈ $2,550 per quarter (plus transport if used at $1.40/km).
  • Everyday Living – Gardening/Lawn Mowing: 1 hour/month at $85/hour ≈ $85/month ≈ $255 per quarter.
  • Everyday Living – Personal Alarm (pendant): One-off $567 (planned in first quarter).
  • Everyday Living – Meal Support (Light & Easy): Budgeted at $66/month as discussed; Action agreed to organise fortnightly deliveries; final quarterly amount will reflect supplier invoices (current placeholder ≈ $198 per quarter, subject to change).
  • Clinical Care – Allied Health (OT assessment): One-off $360 (timing dependent on my address).

Estimated Quarter Total (services above, excluding per-km transport and pending meal invoice changes): approximately $3,570 in the first quarter.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I confirm this plan reflects my choices and preferences. I consent to Salveo Care coordinating and delivering the services described. I consent to share this Care Plan with my GP, my pharmacy, and my son Darryl to support safe care. I understand this plan will be reviewed quarterly or sooner if my needs or circumstances change (for example, if I move to Darryl’s home or have a hospital admission).

I was informed that I am “the boss” of my care. I chose a pendant alarm over a smartwatch, selected weekly social support on Wednesdays 12:00–2:30 pm, and stated my preference not to receive CPR. My preferences about worker characteristics and timing were respected.

My assessment covered health, mood, mobility, falls, home environment, equipment, and social needs. An OT assessment was discussed and will be scheduled based on my living arrangements. The plan will be reviewed quarterly, and a package level increase will be pursued.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care

I currently manage my personal care and medications independently with a Webster pack. Clinical needs (emphysema, depression, past cancer, brain aneurysm) are acknowledged. A formal ACP/DNAR will be discussed with my GP. Allied Health OT input is planned to address mobility safety.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living

Weekly social support is scheduled. Monthly gardening is included. Light & Easy meals will be arranged and funded within the agreed budget. Transport may be used for escorted outings as I choose.

Workers will respect my home, dog, and safety. If I do not answer at a scheduled time, staff will call me first and then call Darryl. Safety equipment (pendant alarm) will be provided and tested.

Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have significant hearing impairment in both ears (worse in my right ear); please speak clearly, slowly, and a little louder, and confirm my understanding.

I have an Advance Care Plan (ACP) held with Geelong Hospital, and my children hold Enduring Power of Attorney; Stuart is my main point of contact.

I report occasional headaches (around 6/10) triggered by stress or tension; I sometimes take a Panadol before bed.

I experience prostate-related nocturia and get up regularly at night to toilet.

I have a history of multiple skin cancers removed and a current spot on my neck that may need removal.

I have no known allergies and I am not taking any prescribed medications.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 04 September 2025

Preferred Name: Ralph

Full Name: Ralph Wakely

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan with support from June and Stuart (main point of contact and Enduring Power of Attorney holder), and the Care Partner.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I have no specific cultural or diversity considerations for matching me with workers.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer workers to communicate by speaking clearly, slowly, and a little louder due to my hearing impairment, and to check my understanding.

I am comfortable with any suitable support worker and do not have specific matching requirements.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

Stuart is my main point of contact and EPOA holder.

My family includes three children and eleven grandchildren.

I sometimes spend time with friends Julian Vyde and Graham Dawson.

My neighbour Cynthia lives across the road.

Informal Supports

My family and neighbour provide informal support and social connection.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I was born in Hamilton and moved to Portland when I was about three.

I worked for a builder, then at the Meatworks boning, and later owned a small farm, a dairy farm, and a hobby farm before moving to my current home.

I experienced a significant financial loss from an investment which affected our lives.

Interests

I enjoy walking, gardening, and going out for a coffee.

I like watching football and enjoy watching my grandkids play.

I value getting outside and doing something physical on good days.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

I have a history of a hernia operation, radiation treatment in Geelong, and multiple skin cancer removals including surgery on my right ear around two to three years ago.

I have prostate-related nocturia that wakes me at night.

I have occasional headaches (around 6/10) triggered by stress or tension.

I have no known allergies and have not been recently assessed for dementia, though I am frustrated by name recall; my GP advised a couple of years ago that I do not have dementia.

Medication:

I am not taking any prescribed medications.

I take multivitamins and sometimes take a Panadol before bed.

Mobility and Equipment:

I am independent with mobility and do not use walking aids.

I can get in and out of the car independently and have no recent falls except a past ladder fall.

I have a gopher (mobility scooter) from earlier days at the golf course but I am not currently using it.

GP / Pharmacy:

My GP is Dr. Mayna at South Portland Medical Centre.

My pharmacy is South Portland Pharmacy.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No.

Living with disability (mobility): I am independent without aids; I have reduced endurance compared to the past.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I can feel low or “trapped indoors” on bad weather days; social contact helps.

Specific Risks:

  • Hearing impairment in both ears increases risk of miscommunication and missed cues.
  • Night-time toileting due to nocturia increases trip/fall risk in low light.
  • Occasional headaches (6/10) triggered by stress/tension may limit activity and affect sleep.
  • History of skin cancers with a current neck spot that may require removal.
  • Past ladder fall and ongoing home/garden tasks present environmental risk if using ladders or uneven ground.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If I am found unresponsive: call Triple Zero (000), commence first aid as appropriate, notify Stuart, and follow my Advance Care Plan held by Geelong Hospital.

Primary contact: Stuart (Enduring Power of Attorney). Phone: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Secondary contacts: My family and neighbour Cynthia. Details: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: Over the next 3 months, I will keep my garden safe and tidy so I can get outside most days, do light tasks, and feel less “trapped indoors.”

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with mobility but do not walk as far as I used to; I have occasional headaches and a past ladder fall; uneven ground and ladders increase risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Light Home & Gardening Maintenance to mow, edge, weed, clear paths, remove trip hazards, and support me to participate in light gardening safely (no ladder use). Workers will communicate clearly and slowly due to my hearing.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker | When will it be done?: 1 hour monthly for 3 months | How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $85/month (approx. $255 for the quarter). Additional home maintenance tasks (gutters/windows/air-con filter clean twice) to be scheduled as needed at $85/hour.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: Over the next 3 months, when bad weather or low mood keeps me indoors, I will get out to meet friends or have a coffee so I have more good days than bad and feel less isolated.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Social interaction helps my wellbeing; hearing impairment requires clear communication; transport may be needed on the day; headaches can limit activity.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Social Support with transport to local venues (e.g., coffee, visit the golf club socially, watch grandkids’ football) and companion support at home or in the garden when outings are not suitable. Workers will speak clearly, slowly, and loudly.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker | When will it be done?: 2 hours fortnightly for 3 months (target at least 2 outings per month) | How much will it cost?: $85/hour, $340/month plus $1.40/km transport (distance-dependent).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 3 Goal: Over the next 3 months, I will maintain and safely improve my comfortable walking so I can keep up my daily walks and gardening, after noticing I “can’t walk as far.”

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent without aids; endurance is reduced; outdoor surfaces may be uneven; headaches and weather can limit activity.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare Allied Health (Physiotherapy) will review my walking and balance, set a home exercise program, and monitor progress. We will measure my comfortable walk time/distance at the first session and aim for a 10–15% improvement by 12 weeks, adjusting for symptoms and weather.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health Therapist (Physio) | When will it be done?: 1 hour monthly for 3 months with daily home exercises | How much will it cost?: $180/hour, $180/month (approx. $540 for the quarter). Clinical Care services are government funded under Support at Home as applicable.

Service Category: Clinical Care

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

  • Everyday Living: Light Home & Gardening Maintenance 1 hour monthly ($85/hour = $85/month).
  • Independence Support: Social Support 2 hours fortnightly ($85/hour = $340/month) plus transport $1.40/km as used.
  • Clinical Care: Allied Health Therapist (Physio) 1 hour monthly ($180/hour = $180/month), subject to funding eligibility under Support at Home Clinical Care.

Quarterly Budget Allocation: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I agree to the supports listed and understand services are delivered under the Support at Home Program with quarterly reviews.

I consent to share this plan with Salveo HomeCare, my primary contact Stuart, and other providers involved in my care (e.g., GP and allied health) as needed.

I understand my ACP is held by Geelong Hospital and that my children hold EPOA; Stuart is my main contact.

Transcript Summary – Ralph Wakely (map to Standards 1–8)

Standard 1 – Consumer dignity and choice: I expressed my preferences for communication (clear, slow, louder speech) and my priorities (walking, gardening, social connection). I have an ACP with Geelong Hospital and EPOA with my children; Stuart is my main contact.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers: The assessment covered my medical history, daily routines, risks, and supports. Goals were co-designed around outdoor activity, social connection, and mobility, with quarterly review.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care: I have no current personal care needs. My clinical needs include hearing impairment, skin cancer history, nocturia, and occasional headaches. Physiotherapy is planned to maintain safe mobility.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living: I receive monthly gardening support and home maintenance (gutters/windows, air-con filter cleaning). Social Support with transport is planned to maintain community access.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment: Workers will ensure safe outdoor work practices (no ladders) and communicate clearly to accommodate my hearing impairment.

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance: I can contact Salveo HomeCare or Stuart to provide feedback or request changes. Qualified personnel will deliver services aligned to Support at Home. Documentation (ACP/EPOA) will be kept accessible for hospitals if requested.

Dignity of Risk Assessment (Narrative + Table)

I choose to remain active with walking and gardening because being outside and doing something physical helps me have more good days and feel less “trapped indoors.” I understand there are risks (uneven ground, fatigue, headaches), and I agree to reasonable strategies such as avoiding ladders, keeping paths clear, using night lighting, and having support workers communicate clearly due to my hearing impairment. I accept some residual risk to maintain my independence and quality of life.
