saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I prefer care workers who speak English clearly, are respectful, easy to get along with, and do not discuss or preach religion while providing services.

I prefer a female cleaner. I am easygoing about who attends for my supports as long as they meet my preferences above.

I consent to resuscitation. In an emergency: call 000 first, then contact my daughter Elizabeth.

If there is no answer at a scheduled visit: please call me first, leave a message, and if you cannot reach me, contact Elizabeth.

I have hearing loss in my left ear. Please speak clearly and face me when talking.

I have Type 2 diabetes, a heart murmur (monitoring planned), sleep apnea, and depression (now well managed). I do not have known medication allergies documented here.

I have had bilateral knee replacements and an old right-wrist injury. I am independent with mobility, with occasional stiffness or pain (worse in cold weather).

I do not have a personal alarm or key lockbox and do not wish to install them at present.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 11 September 2025

Preferred Name: Graeme

Full Name: Graeme Bushby

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I developed this plan with my Care Partner during my assessment. My daughter Elizabeth is my preferred contact. My wife Janet’s needs were discussed in relation to scheduling, though this plan is for me, Graeme.

Care Partner (name not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided).

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I do not practice a religion and prefer that care workers keep their religious beliefs to themselves while working. Being respectful, speaking good English, being easy to get along with, and having a sense of humour are important to me.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer workers who are respectful, punctual, communicate clearly in English, and can have a friendly laugh while they work.

Please speak clearly and face me due to hearing loss in my left ear.

Cleaning is scheduled for Tuesdays at 10:00 AM for 1.5 hours. Meal preparation support is every other Tuesday at 11:30 AM for 1.5 hours. Gardening is for 2 hours every three weeks (ad hoc scheduling).

If I do not answer at a scheduled visit, please call me and leave a message. If you cannot reach me, contact Elizabeth.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

My wife Janet.

My daughters Elizabeth and Kate.

My friend Penny (former neighbour).

My community connections through local football clubs, the Men’s Shed, and Good Friday Appeal colleagues.

Informal Supports

My children assist me as needed. I also have supportive friends and community contacts through football clubs, the Men’s Shed, and charity events.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I grew up in Horsham with my brothers Brian (now living with dementia), Gary and John. My childhood was tough. I worked most of my life selling car parts and managing parts/service operations, including at Jetty Toyota for 10–15 years. I retired about five years ago after knee replacements.

Interests

I am active in local football clubs (3–4 days a week), attend the Men’s Shed twice weekly, and help with community and charity events such as the Good Friday Appeal, MS Australia bike rides, and the Great Vic Bike Ride. I enjoy staying active, helping others, and being part of my community.

My Medical Information

Medical History

Type 2 diabetes.

Heart murmur; periodic cardiac monitoring is planned in about two months.

Sleep apnea.

Depression (previously significant low mood; now improved with supports and staying active).

Bilateral total knee replacements (functioning well). Old right wrist injury with reduced function and stiffness.

No falls history reported.

Medication

I take my prescribed medications daily. My medicines are supplied in a blister pack through my pharmacy. I self-manage and do not need assistance. No allergies were reported in this transcript.

Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Mobility and Equipment

I mobilise independently without walking aids and continue to drive. I can get in and out of the car independently.

I have a recliner/lift chair. I do not use a shower chair or handrails (these are in the home for Janet).

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr Morrison, Monash Health Centre (address not documented in this transcript).

Pharmacy: Cranburn Community Pharmacy, 32–36 Remont Way.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Living with disability (mobility): I have had both knees replaced and an old right wrist injury; I mobilise independently but can be stiff or sore with cold weather.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I have a history of depression and reported past thoughts of suicidality earlier in the year; I am currently stable and supported by family, friends, and community activities.

Specific Risks

  • No key lockbox and no personal alarm by choice, which could delay emergency access.
  • Hearing impairment (left ear) may affect communication if not addressed.
  • Diabetes self-management requires ongoing adherence to medication and diet.
  • Intermittent knee and wrist pain (worse in cold weather) may affect function on some days.
  • No formal written Advance Care Directive or Enduring Power of Attorney in place; daughter Elizabeth is nominated verbally.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Primary contact: Elizabeth (daughter). Phone not documented in this transcript.

Other important people: Janet (wife), Kate (daughter).

Emergency instructions while workers are present: Call 000 first, commence resuscitation if required, then contact Elizabeth.

If no response at a scheduled visit: Call me and leave a message. If I cannot be reached, contact Elizabeth.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my home clean and safe so I am not straining my knees or wrist, and so I can stay active with my football clubs and Men’s Shed.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent but experience knee and wrist pain in cold weather. A consistent weekly clean reduces physical strain and trip hazards.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Domestic Assistance to vacuum, mop, clean bathrooms, dust benches, and manage linens weekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM (1.5 hours).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me to guide priorities. When will it be done?: Weekly, over the next 3 months (quarter), Tuesdays 10:00–11:30 AM. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 1.5 hours x 4 weeks = $510/month (approx. $1,530 per quarter).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I will maintain my yard and outdoor access so pathways are safe and tidy, supporting my independence and community activities.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can manage most tasks but outdoor work can aggravate my knees and wrist.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Light Home & Gardening Maintenance for mowing, weeding, and light pruning for 2 hours every three weeks (ad hoc scheduling).

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare gardener and me to specify tasks. When will it be done?: Every three weeks over the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 2 hours every 3 weeks ≈ $227/month (approx. $680 per quarter).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: I will have help with meal preparation every fortnight so that meals are ready and safe to manage at home, especially when my wrist is sore and to support Janet when needed.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I eat well and take my medications; occasional wrist and knee pain can make meal tasks harder.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide assistance with meal preparation and kitchen clean-up for 1.5 hours every other Tuesday at 11:30 AM, including optional supported shopping if required.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me to choose menus and tasks. When will it be done?: Fortnightly over the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 1.5 hours x 2 visits/month = $255/month (approx. $765 per quarter).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 4 Goal: I will maintain my foot health to stay active and safe on my feet for football club work and Men’s Shed.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am active with diabetes and rely on good foot care to prevent problems.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will arrange a Podiatry appointment once per quarter and assist with booking and reminders. Session length: 1 hour per quarter.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare (care coordination) and me to attend. When will it be done?: Once per quarter (next within 3 months). How much will it cost?: Clinical Care (100% government funded). Where a fee applies, the standard Allied Health Therapist rate is $180/hour (indicative only; funded under Clinical Care).

Service Category: Clinical Care

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

Quarterly Budget Allocation:

  • Everyday Living: Domestic Assistance ($1,530/quarter) + Light Home & Gardening Maintenance (approx. $680/quarter) + Meal Preparation ($765/quarter) = approx. $2,975/quarter.
  • Clinical Care: Podiatry 1 hour/quarter = $180/quarter (not charged to me; funded under Clinical Care).
  • Independence Support: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I confirm this plan reflects my preferences and agreed supports. I consent to Salveo HomeCare coordinating and delivering the services outlined, and to share this plan with my GP, relevant allied health providers, and my nominated contacts to support safe care. I understand this plan will be reviewed quarterly or sooner if my needs change.

Prepared By

Name: __________ | Role: Care Partner, Date: Today | Review Date: Quarterly (every 3 months) | Signature: __________

Transcript Summary – Graeme Bushby (map to Standards 1–8)

Standard 1 – Consumer dignity and choice

I expressed clear preferences: respectful, easygoing workers with good English who do not discuss religion; a female cleaner is preferred. I make my own decisions and want services scheduled on Tuesdays with flexibility.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers

I discussed my health conditions, routines, risks, and priorities. We agreed on weekly cleaning, gardening every three weeks, fortnightly meal prep, and quarterly podiatry. I consented to resuscitation and outlined emergency contact preferences. We will review this plan every three months.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care

I self-manage medications in blister packs. I have diabetes, sleep apnea, a heart murmur (monitoring planned), and depression (stable). Podiatry is arranged quarterly. I reported pain fluctuations and hearing loss in my left ear; staff will communicate clearly and monitor for changes.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living

Domestic Assistance, meal preparation support, and gardening are in place to reduce strain on my knees and wrist and maintain a safe home so I can stay active in my community roles.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment

Workers will maintain a safe, respectful environment, follow my communication preferences, and use agreed entry/emergency procedures (call me first, then Elizabeth, and 000 as needed).

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance

I understand how to provide feedback to Salveo HomeCare at any time. Workers will hold appropriate checks and skills. My services and risks will be monitored and reviewed quarterly in line with governance requirements under the Support at Home Program.

Dignity of Risk Assessment (Narrative + Table)

I choose to remain independent and active in my community. I understand there are risks (e.g., no lockbox/personal alarm, driving, fluctuating pain, diabetes, and not having formal power of attorney/advance care documents). I accept these risks and agree to mitigation strategies so I can continue doing what matters to me.

Risk identified Client's choice / decision Potential consequences Mitigation strategies Acknowledgement Date
No key lockbox at home I choose not to install a lockbox while renting. Delayed emergency access if I cannot answer the door. Workers to call me first, leave a message, then contact Elizabeth; consider reassessing lockbox option at the quarterly review. I understand and accept this risk. 11 Sep 2025
No personal alarm I choose not to use a personal alarm at this time. Delayed response if I fall or become unwell when alone. Keep mobile phone charged and nearby; maintain regular visits; review alarm option if my risk or circumstances change. I understand and accept this risk. 11 Sep 2025
Driving with intermittent knee/wrist pain and hearing loss (left ear) I choose to continue driving. Increased risk of incident on days with pain or reduced hearing awareness. Avoid driving on high-pain days; use heat/rest before activities; ensure hearing aids are arranged and used; consider alternative transport if unwell. I understand and accept this risk. 11 Sep 2025
Depression with history of low mood and past suicidal thoughts I choose to remain active and manage my mood through community involvement and talking with trusted people. Risk of deterioration during stress (e.g., worries about Janet’s health). Maintain regular social activities; talk with family/friends; contact GP if mood worsens; workers to escalate concerns with my consent. I understand and accept this plan. 11 Sep 2025
Diabetes self-management I choose to self-manage medications and diet. Risk of hypo/hyperglycaemia if routines are not followed. Continue blister pack use; maintain healthy meals via fortnightly support; seek GP advice for any concerns. I understand and accept this plan. 11 Sep 2025
No formalised Advance Care Directive or Power of Attorney documentation I nominate Elizabeth verbally but have not completed written documents yet. Delays or uncertainty in decision-making if I lose capacity. Care Partner to support me to discuss and formalise documents; I will consider completing these before the next quarterly review. I understand and intend to address this. 11 Sep 2025
Pain management without analgesics I choose not to take regular pain medication. Potential for increased pain limiting activities on cold days. Use heat/rest; pace activities; seek GP advice if pain exceeds 7–8/10 or function declines; schedule heavier tasks when workers attend. I understand and accept this risk. 11 Sep 2025

saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I am hard of hearing and I need care workers to speak slowly, clearly and loudly in English so I can understand.

I have a falls risk due to reduced balance and I must use my four-wheel walker at all times when mobilising.

I am currently taking blood thinners and I bruise easily, so I have an increased risk of bleeding if I fall or sustain a cut.

I have a chronic head wound that has been stable for months and I self-manage a dry dressing nightly.

I experience arthritis pain in my fingers, elbows and knees, a right-leg spasm, and burning feet at night which can disturb my sleep and mobility.

I have a wheeze that has been worse since COVID, and I am an ex-smoker who quit about 50 years ago.

I am virtually blind in my left eye which increases my falls risk, especially in low light.

I have slight urinary incontinence and use level 2 continence pads (Tenar brand) at approximately $40 per month.

I am allergic to house dust mites and regular dusting and linen changes help reduce symptoms.

I have a personal alarm through my retirement village that I can press to call for help, and it is not a falls detector.

I prefer workers to knock and enter to check on me if I do not answer for a scheduled visit, as the door is usually unlocked during the day.

I have a key lockbox for emergencies only (code 8933) and workers must use it only if there is no other way to safely enter.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 15 September 2025

Preferred Name: Peter

Full Name: Peter Cram

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

I participated in this assessment and I make my own decisions.

My family member attended the assessment and supports me, and I have an Enduring Power of Attorney held by a family member.

The care partner/assessor facilitated this care planning discussion, and my ongoing Care Partner will be Cassie (as introduced by the provider).

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I was born in Metara, Australia, and I do not currently practice a religion.

My core values are family, independence, honesty and integrity, and I want my care to respect these values.

I do not have specific cultural customs or diversity needs I want recognised beyond my communication needs related to hearing.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer workers who speak clear English and will talk slowly, clearly and loudly because I am hard of hearing.

I want workers to knock first and use the door to enter for scheduled visits, and to use the lockbox only in an emergency.

I want regular and reliable scheduling: Domestic Assistance on Tuesdays 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM and Social Support on Thursdays 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM.

I prefer companionship-based Social Support that includes playing Scrabble and conversation, and I do not want to go shopping as I shop online.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination.

My Preferred Support People

My family, including my two sons and grandchildren, are important to me and are my preferred support people.

Staff at my retirement village are supportive and available if needed.

Informal Supports

I live in a retirement village where staff can assist in emergencies and there is a site fire plan.

I keep in touch with family, including Zoom calls with my son twice a week.

I attend a book club and monthly social dinners at my residence.

I will continue with my physiotherapy through Polina Healthcare, and I see a podiatrist for foot care.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I grew up in a small country town and went to boarding school from age 10 for three years, which I enjoyed.

I was a pharmacist and owned pharmacies in Castelan and Geelong, and I also worked as a relieving pharmacist.

My late wife was also a pharmacist, we met at pharmacy college, and we were married for 64 years, knowing each other for nearly 70 years.

I have two sons and family is very important to me.

I played football until age 27 and used to enjoy bowls and going to the gym regularly.

Interests

I enjoy reading books and the newspaper, watching television including football, cricket and documentaries, and I have an interest in politics.

I attend a book club and monthly social dinners at my retirement village.

Loneliness is my biggest problem and I value companionship, including having someone to play Scrabble with me.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have a history of a broken leg around three years ago and I am cautious about falls.

I have had cancer treatments about three years ago.

I have high blood pressure that is under control and a heart flutter.

I have GORD (gastroesophageal reflux disease) that is under control.

I have hearing loss and wear hearing aids.

I have a chronic head wound that has been stable for months and I self-manage a nightly dry dressing.

I experience arthritis in my fingers, elbows and knees, and a right-leg spasm that is being monitored.

I experience burning feet syndrome that is worse at night.

I have a wheeze that has been worse since I had COVID; I am an ex-smoker who quit about 50 years ago.

I have slight urinary incontinence and require one pad per day.

I am virtually blind in my left eye.

I notice some forgetfulness but I have not been assessed for dementia.

Medication

I self-manage my medications and do not need assistance.

I take Pelixia twice daily and paracetamol for arthritis pain.

I have been on blood thinners for a couple of months.

I use liniment on my knees and elbows when needed.

I have an allergy to house dust mites and no known medication allergies.

Mobility and Equipment

I cannot walk without my four-wheel walker and I sometimes use walking sticks for short trips.

I have a shower chair, handrails in the shower, a recliner chair, a bed transfer pole and a personal alarm.

I do not have a raised toilet seat and I do not use any mechanical lifters.

GP / Pharmacy

GP: Dr. Mabo, Manningham General Practice (200 High Street).

Pharmacy: Terry White Pharmacy, 45 Were Street, Montmorency.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: No, I am Australian-born and speak English.

Living with disability (mobility): Yes, I have reduced balance and require a four-wheel walker.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes, I report loneliness and I value companionship.

Specific Risks

I am at risk of falls due to impaired balance, vision changes and fatigue.

I am at increased bleeding risk due to blood thinners and easy bruising.

I have a chronic head wound that can ooze at night and may become infected if not monitored.

I have hearing impairment which can affect communication and safety if instructions are missed.

I have a wheeze post-COVID which may affect my breathing and exercise tolerance.

I have burning feet at night which may disturb sleep and contribute to unsteadiness.

I have slight urinary incontinence which may increase skin irritation risk and slipping risk if pads are not managed.

I prefer my door to be unlocked during the day and I allow entry if I do not answer, which requires clear worker identification and safety protocols.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

In a medical emergency, I want workers to call Triple Zero (000), commence first aid/CPR as trained, and notify my family/EPOA.

My personal alarm connects me to the monitoring service when I press the button and they will stay on the phone until help arrives.

If I do not answer for a scheduled visit, I want workers to enter and check on me, as my door is usually unlocked during the day.

The key lockbox code is 8933 and it is for emergency use only.

There is a site fire plan in my retirement village and staff can assist during facility emergencies.

Emergency contact names and phone numbers: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will feel less lonely by having a Salveo HomeCare support worker visit to play Scrabble and provide companionship every Thursday 11:00 AM–1:30 PM so I can enjoy conversation and mental stimulation.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am independent with personal care but I am hard of hearing, I fatigue easily, and I have a falls risk; I prefer to stay in rather than go shopping.

How will we do this? (Tasks): The worker will arrive on time, speak slowly and clearly, play Scrabble and other brain teasers with me, and check in on my wellbeing. If I choose to go for a short walk or coffee, the worker will support me with my four-wheel walker and transport if planned.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo HomeCare Social Support. When will it be done?: Weekly for 2.5 hours on Thursdays, over the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: Social Support $85/hour x 2.5 hours weekly ≈ $850/month (transport if used: $1.40/km, ad hoc).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 2 Goal: I will maintain a clean, low-dust and safe home so I can live independently and comfortably, with focus on dusting and linen changes to reduce my house-dust mite allergy.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I cannot safely do heavier cleaning due to reduced balance, fatigue and arthritis; I am at increased bleeding risk on blood thinners.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo HomeCare will provide Domestic Assistance on Tuesdays 11:00 AM–1:00 PM for vacuuming, mopping, bathroom/toilet clean, kitchen surfaces, dusting shelves and high-touch areas, and changing bed linen weekly to reduce dust mites.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo HomeCare Domestic Assistance. When will it be done?: Weekly for 2 hours on Tuesdays, over the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: Domestic Assistance $85/hour x 2 hours weekly ≈ $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: I will keep my mobility and balance by continuing weekly physiotherapy and my home exercise program so I can walk safely with my four-wheel walker for 10–15 minutes most days and reduce right-leg spasms.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I require my four-wheel walker for all walking, I have a falls risk, a left-eye vision deficit, and I fatigue during the day.

How will we do this? (Tasks): I will receive Allied Health therapy (physiotherapy) weekly for 1 hour to progress balance and gait, and I will complete my physio home exercises for 10–15 minutes at least 5 days per week. Social Support will prompt short supported corridor walks if I choose. I will report any increase in spasms, pain or wheeze to my GP/physio.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo HomeCare Allied Health Therapist (Physio). When will it be done?: Weekly for 1 hour, over the next 3 months. How much will it cost?: Allied Health Therapist (Physio) $180/hour x 1 hour weekly ≈ $720/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

Budget and Service Classifications

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I have participated in developing this care plan and I agree that it reflects my goals, preferences and current supports.

I consent to the services outlined and to information sharing with my chosen support people, my GP and allied health providers as needed for my care.

I want a copy of this care plan provided to me and, with my consent, to my Enduring Power of Attorney.

Prepared By (Name: __________ | Role: Care Partner, Date: Today | Review Date: Quarterly (every 3 months) | Signature: __________)

Transcript Summary – Peter Cram (map to Standards 1–8)

Standard 1 – Consumer dignity and choice

I stated my preferences clearly, including being called Peter, communicating slowly and clearly due to hearing loss, and having companionship focused on Scrabble rather than shopping.

My values (family, independence, honesty, integrity) were documented and my desire for a simple end-of-life arrangement was noted.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers

A comprehensive assessment covered my health, mobility, equipment, informal supports, routines and risks, and resulted in co-designed SMARTA goals with quarterly review.

My decision-making capacity was confirmed and my Enduring Power of Attorney was noted with a plan to obtain a copy.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care

I self-manage personal care and medications and I will continue weekly physiotherapy; risks from blood thinners, chronic wound care and respiratory wheeze were documented with escalation pathways.

My chronic head wound management, arthritis pain strategies and continence needs were recorded.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living

Domestic Assistance and Social Support were scheduled at times I chose to maintain a clean and safe home and reduce loneliness.

Meals are provided by my retirement village five times weekly and my preference for online shopping was recorded.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment

I live in a retirement village with a site fire plan and a personal alarm; safe entry procedures and emergency lockbox use were agreed.

Workers will identify themselves, knock first and speak clearly to meet my communication needs.

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance

I was provided with contact details for the provider and care partner and informed about service transfer dates and cancellation policies.

My plan aligns to Support at Home changes (quarterly budgeting and equipment budget) and will be reviewed every three months with my input.

Dignity of Risk Assessment (Narrative + Table)

I understand that living independently and remaining active involves some risks, and I choose to balance safety with quality of life. I accept support to reduce risks where practical, while keeping my preferences at the centre. The strategies below reflect my informed choices and how risks will be mitigated.

Risk identified Client's choice / decision Potential consequences Mitigation strategies Acknowledgement Date
Falls risk due to impaired balance and vision I choose to continue walking daily with my four-wheel walker and to do short corridor walks for fitness. Fall, injury or bleeding (on blood thinners) Use four-wheel walker at all times, keep walkways clear, good lighting, complete weekly physio and daily home exercises, supervise short walks during Social Support if I choose, report near-misses. I understand the risk and agree to the plan to reduce it. 15 September 2025
Unlocked door during day and entry if I do not answer I prefer workers to enter and check on me if I do not respond for a scheduled visit. Full Name: Bruce Ruxton

I prefer practical, respectful support that helps me stay independent at home.

My daughter, Sarah, lives about 15 minutes away and visits often.

My son, David, lives interstate and calls regularly.

I have a few good mates I catch up with for a beer once a week.

Informal Supports

Sarah brings meals a couple of times a week and visits regularly.

David provides emotional support by calling regularly.

My mates provide social connection when we meet weekly.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I live alone in my three-bedroom home and have been there for about 40 years.

Interests

I love my garden and want to keep enjoying it even if I cannot do as much as before.

I would like to get out more and go to the local club for a game of snooker like I used to.

I like good, plain food (nothing too spicy) and enjoy a roast with vegetables.

My Medical Information

Medical History

I have type 2 diabetes managed with medication.

I have high blood pressure.

I had a fall last year and feel a bit unsteady at times.

Medication

I take Metformin for diabetes and Lisinopril for blood pressure.

I sometimes forget to take my diabetes medication.

Mobility and Equipment

I am a bit wobbly on my feet and have had near misses with falls.

Showering can be difficult when getting in and out; aids were discussed as a possibility.

No specific mobility or bathroom equipment is documented in this transcript.

GP / Pharmacy

My GP is Dr. Chen at the local medical centre.

Pharmacy: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Vulnerable Person (CALD: Not identified in this transcript, Living with disability (mobility): Yes – unsteady gait and prior fall, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Some risk due to living alone; I want to get out more and stay socially connected.)

Specific Risks

  • Falls risk in bathroom and around home due to unsteadiness and prior fall.

  • Shower access/transfer risk when getting in and out.

  • Medication non-adherence (forgetting diabetes medication).

  • Living alone with intermittent informal supports.

  • Community outings (weekly beer with mates) to be balanced with diabetes management.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Primary: Sarah (daughter) – lives 15 minutes away.

Secondary: David (son) – lives interstate.

Instructions: In an emergency, call 000 first. Notify Sarah as soon as practicable. For non-urgent health issues, contact Dr. Chen at the local medical centre.

Contact phone numbers and additional details: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

GOAL 1 Goal: I will shower safely and maintain my personal hygiene without falls, with support when needed, so I can keep living at home.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I am mostly independent but sometimes struggle getting in and out of the shower; I am at risk of falls.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Provide Personal Care support for shower entry/exit, drying and dressing; check non-slip mats; discuss and action an Occupational Therapy home safety assessment for bathroom aids if recommended.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me. When will it be done?: Twice weekly (1 hour each) for 3 months, starting immediately. How much will it cost?: 8 hours/month at $85/hour = $680/month.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 2 Goal: I will keep my home clean and safe by getting help with heavier cleaning so I can focus on living well at home.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can do light dusting, but I need help with heavier tasks; fatigue and balance increase fall risk during heavier cleaning.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Domestic Assistance for vacuuming, mopping, bathroom and kitchen clean, laundry and linen change as needed.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Domestic Assistance worker and me. When will it be done?: Fortnightly (2 hours/visit) for 3 months. How much will it cost?: 4 hours/month at $85/hour = $340/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: I will have simple, plain meals ready that suit my preferences and diabetes, so I eat well and maintain energy.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Cooking is a struggle; my daughter brings meals a couple of times a week; risk of poor nutrition on other days.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Domestic Assistance to plan and prepare plain meals (e.g., roast with vegetables), portion and refrigerate or freeze; support safe food handling and kitchen clean-up.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Domestic Assistance worker and me. When will it be done?: Weekly (1.5 hours) for 3 months. How much will it cost?: 6 hours/month at $85/hour = $510/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

Abilities and considerations (risks): Prior fall and near misses; unsteady gait; bathroom transfers are difficult.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Allied Health Therapist (Physio/OT) assessment and tailored balance/strength exercises; OT home safety review for bathroom aids if recommended; review progress monthly.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health Therapist and me. When will it be done?: Fortnightly (1 hour) for 3 months. How much will it cost?: 2 hours/month at $180/hour = $360/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

Abilities and considerations (risks): I sometimes forget to take my medication.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Enrolled Nurse to review my medication routine, set up a simple medication prompt plan (e.g., chart and agreed reminders), and check adherence monthly.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Enrolled Nurse and me. When will it be done?: Monthly (1 hour) for 3 months. How much will it cost?: 1 hour/month at $121/hour = $121/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 6 Goal: I will get out to my local club for a game of snooker once a week to stay social and active.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have mates I meet weekly; I am a bit unsteady and want safe transport and company.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Social Support and Transport to and from the club; companion support during the visit as needed; ensure I have eaten and feel well.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Social Support/Transport worker and me. When will it be done?: Weekly (3 hours per outing) for 3 months. How much will it cost?: 12 hours/month at $85/hour = $1,020/month, plus mileage at $1.40/km (return distance to be confirmed).

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 7 Goal: I will keep my garden tidy and safe so I can enjoy being outside without overexerting myself.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I love my garden but cannot manage heavier tasks; bending/ladders increase fall risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Light Home & Gardening Maintenance for mowing, weeding, sweeping pathways, and removing trip hazards.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Home & Garden worker and me. When will it be done?: Fortnightly (1.5 hours) for 3 months. How much will it cost?: 3 hours/month at $85/hour = $255/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

  • Everyday Living: Domestic Assistance (cleaning) 4 hours/month at $85 = $340/month; Domestic Assistance (meal prep) 6 hours/month at $85 = $510/month; Light Home & Gardening 3 hours/month at $85 = $255/month. Total Everyday Living monthly = $1,105; Quarterly = $3,315.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I want help preparing my meals at home so I can eat safely and consistently while living independently over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can live independently but my mobility issues make standing and preparing meals harder. I have diabetes and benefit from regular, timely meals.

How will we do this? (Tasks): A Salveo HomeCare support worker will assist me with meal planning, meal preparation and clean-up at home on set days each week, focusing on simple, easy-to-heat meals prepared in batches for the week.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me. When will it be done?: 3 sessions per week, 1 hour each session, for the next 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 3 hours/week ≈ $1020/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 2 Goal: I want support to do my grocery shopping each week so I can get what I need and manage safely in the community over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): My mobility issues make carrying groceries and walking around the shops difficult. Shopping is important for me to maintain my independence at home.

How will we do this? (Tasks): A Salveo HomeCare support worker will accompany me to the supermarket, help me select items, reach shelves, carry groceries, and assist me to and from the car/home; transport mileage will be recorded as incurred.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare support worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 session per week, 2 hours each session, for the next 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 2 hours/week ≈ $680/month, plus mileage at $1.40/km (as incurred).

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 3 Goal: I want to improve my mobility so I can move more safely at home and during shopping over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have mobility issues that may increase my falls risk. I will benefit from a targeted exercise program and safe movement strategies.

How will we do this? (Tasks): An Allied Health Therapist (Physiotherapist) from Salveo HomeCare will assess me and provide a home exercise program, balance and mobility training, and review my progress regularly.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health Therapist (Physio) and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour fortnightly for 12 weeks, with home exercises between sessions. How much will it cost?: $180/hour x ~2 hours/month ≈ $360/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

I will receive supports under Everyday Living (meal preparation and shopping support) and Clinical Care (Allied Health Physiotherapy).

Quarterly Budget Allocation: Estimated monthly costs: Meal preparation $1020/month; Shopping support $680/month plus mileage at $1.40/km (as incurred); Allied Health Physiotherapy $360/month. Estimated total $2060/month (plus mileage), or approximately $6180 per quarter (plus mileage).

I have a high risk of falls (I reported approximately 10–12 falls in the last year, often when rushing to the bathroom due to urinary urgency).

I require wound care to my feet/legs three times per week (currently Monday, Wednesday and Friday). Please monitor for wet or soiled dressings, especially on the left foot.

I have OCD with a specific phobia of dust. Care workers should communicate calmly, explain tasks, and avoid creating visible dust where possible.

I have an allergy/sensitivity to theatre tape/adhesive (from past surgery). Avoid strong surgical tapes/adhesives where possible and monitor skin.

Emergency preference: If I am found unconscious or not breathing, call 000 first, commence resuscitation, then call my family.

I use a walker and have balance problems. Please cue me to slow down and turn safely.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 16 September 2025

Preferred Name: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Full Name: Denise Ruxton

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Interpreter required?: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

People involved in developing my care plan

I participated in this assessment and planning conversation with a care partner (assessor).

My husband Bruce contributed context about our daily routines.

My son Lee holds enduring power of attorney and has my advance care plan; he is a key support person for decisions.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I am Catholic and said that God is very important to me; I value God, family, and honesty. I would like to be more assertive.

I am comfortable with either male or female workers.

I identify as heterosexual.

At end of life I would like to speak with a priest or pastoral care (or a counsellor/social worker if preferred at the time).

My OCD (particularly a phobia of dust) affects how I feel in my home. Keeping visible surfaces clear helps reduce my anxiety.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I prefer workers to be on time, explain what they are going to do, check in about my anxiety/OCD on the day, and avoid creating dust. Calm, clear communication helps me.

I am comfortable with male or female workers.

When possible, I prefer to coordinate visits together (e.g., my nurse visit while Bruce’s personal care occurs) so our day is not broken up. Monday mornings around 9–10am have worked previously.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

Bruce (husband).

Amanda (daughter) and Lee (son). Lee’s wife Tracey.

Grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

For pastoral care, I would like access to a priest or church representative when needed.

Informal Supports

I live with my husband Bruce. My family (Amanda and Lee, and extended family) are important to me and can be contacted if needed. Lee is my enduring power of attorney.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I am the second of four sisters and was raised Catholic. I trained and worked as a nurse (including palliative care and night duty), took time out for social work training and worked with homeless men, then returned to nursing. I retired around age 59. Bruce and I married in 1962 and recently celebrated our 63rd anniversary. We are moving to a new home in Ballarat. We have children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

Interests

I enjoy time with Bruce and family. I like home tasks and keeping things in order, but my anxiety and OCD can make me feel I must stay inside to “keep up.” I would like to relax more and have breakfast earlier in the morning. I worry about visitors seeing a messy kitchen.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

Right knee replacement (limited ability to get the right leg far back; I enter cars from the left side).

Right mastectomy for a large cancer; multiple prior lumpectomies.

Minor stroke in 2010 with residual numbness on the left side (fingers more affected).

Multiple falls; three broken bones in my hand after a fall (around last Christmas).

Foot run over by a taxi about a year ago; wore a moon boot for seven weeks.

Foot problems: bunion on right foot and hammertoes (right worse than left).

Possible skin cancer on my face — plan to see a skin specialist.

History of nausea after anaesthetic in the distant past (noted during recovery years ago).

OCD with prominent phobia of dust; anxiety.

Medication:

I use blister packs and manage my own medications.

Pain: Panadol — I take two tablets when pain spikes (up to every four hours, not every day).

Previously on Lyrica for nerve pain, stopped due to sleepiness and increased falls.

Bladder urgency medication (name not recalled) prescribed by my GP.

Mobility and Equipment:

I use a walker and sometimes “furniture walk.” My main difficulty is balance, turning too quickly, and rushing (especially to the bathroom due to urgency). I get short of breath on inclines.

I have an over-toilet aid. I wear compression stockings that need washing weekly.

I currently sleep in a chair due to pain and would like OT help to get back to sleeping in bed.

GP / Pharmacy: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Living with disability (mobility): I have significant balance issues, use a walker, and have had multiple falls.

Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): I experience anxiety and OCD, and I can feel grumpy or stressed on bad days.

Specific Risks

I am at high risk of falls, particularly when rushing to the toilet due to urinary urgency and when turning quickly.

Wound complications risk if dressings become wet/soiled (left foot more prone to wet dressings).

Car transfer risk due to right knee limitations — I enter vehicles from the left side and need extra time.

Sleep in chair increases risk of poor sleep and potential skin issues; I want to transition back to bed with OT support.

My OCD and dust phobia can increase anxiety if surfaces are cluttered or dusty.

Adhesive sensitivity (theatre tape) may cause skin issues; avoid strong surgical tapes.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

Emergency instruction: If I am found unconscious or not breathing, call 000 first, commence resuscitation, then call my family.

Preferred family contacts: Bruce (husband); Amanda (daughter); Lee (son and enduring power of attorney); Tracey (daughter-in-law).

If there is no answer at a scheduled visit: call my mobile, check with neighbours/management, then call Amanda. A key will be held in the office (as arranged).

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will keep my foot/leg wounds clean, dry and healing with no signs of infection over the next 3 months so I can sleep better and move more comfortably.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can check my dressings and report wetness (left foot gets wet more often). I have constant foot pain and high falls risk.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo Registered Nurse to complete wound dressings and monitoring three times weekly (Mon/Wed/Fri); I will replace any saturated/wet dressing prior to nurse visits and report changes in pain, redness, or odour; nurses will educate me on signs of infection.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo Registered Nurse support; When will it be done?: Mon/Wed/Fri, 1 hour each visit, for the next 3 months; How much will it cost?: $148.50/hour, 3 hours per week ≈ $1,929/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 2 Goal: I will improve my balance and reduce falls by practising a tailored physio home program so that I have no more than 1 minor fall in the next 3 months and can turn safely with my walker.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I use a walker and can follow simple exercises but I rush, especially to the toilet, and I turn too quickly.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo Allied Health Physiotherapist to review me 1 hour monthly and set/adjust a daily home exercise program (10–15 minutes daily); I will keep a falls diary and practise slow turns and safe pacing to the bathroom.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo Allied Health Physiotherapist; When will it be done?: 1 hour monthly review plus daily exercises for 3 months; How much will it cost?: $180/hour, $180/month for physio (home exercises are no cost).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 3 Goal: I will complete an Occupational Therapy assessment to help me transition from sleeping in a chair back to sleeping in my bed and to optimise safe car transfers (entering from the left side) within the next 8 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Right knee limits leg position; I currently sleep in a chair due to pain and wake overnight from pain and bladder urgency.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo Allied Health OT to complete an initial home assessment, advise on bed setup/transfer techniques and bathroom/night-time strategies, and provide a written plan; I will follow the plan and trial recommendations.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo Allied Health Occupational Therapist; When will it be done?: One initial assessment within 4 weeks and implementation over the following month; How much will it cost?: $180/hour (assessment billed at $180; further sessions only if I agree).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 4 Goal: I will feel comfortable having visitors by keeping my kitchen benches clear and my compression stockings washed weekly, which helps my OCD anxiety, for the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can direct tasks and explain my preferences; anxiety and dust phobia increase when surfaces are cluttered.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo Domestic Assistance to attend weekly to wash/air-dry my stockings and do a focused kitchen clean/tidy (benches clear, wipe-down, bins out); I will identify priority areas each week.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo Domestic Assistance; When will it be done?: 1 hour weekly for 3 months; How much will it cost?: $85/hour, approximately $368/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 5 Goal: I will manage bunions/hammertoes and foot pain so I can sleep with fewer night awakenings (a reduction by at least 2 awakenings per week within 3 months).

Abilities and considerations (risks): Pain and fragile skin around toes; wound dressings can be tricky around hammertoes.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo Podiatry to review foot care and footwear and treat as needed every 6–8 weeks; I will follow podiatry advice and report any skin breakdown promptly.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo Podiatrist and Salveo Registered Nurse; When will it be done?: 1 hour every 6–8 weeks; How much will it cost?: $180 per visit (billed when delivered).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 6 Goal: I will have breakfast earlier on at least 5 days each week and practise relaxing rather than overworking on household tasks, to reduce my daily anxiety over the next 3 months.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can plan my day with support; I tend to worry and feel I must “keep at it,” which increases stress.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Salveo Social Support to visit fortnightly to help me set a simple weekly plan, cue breakfast before 10am, and practise brief calming strategies; I will track breakfast times and rate my anxiety (0–10) weekly.

Who is responsible?: I am, with Salveo Social Support worker; When will it be done?: 1 hour fortnightly for 3 months; How much will it cost?: $85/hour, approximately $184/month (no transport required).

Service Category: Independence Support

Budget and Service Classifications

Service Category: Clinical Care (100% government funded) / Independence Support / Everyday Living

Quarterly Budget Allocation: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Classification Level (1-8 under Support at Home): Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Approximate monthly service costs based on my goals:

- Clinical Care: Registered Nurse wound care ≈ $1,929/month; Physiotherapy $180/month; Podiatry $180 per visit (every 6–8 weeks).

- Everyday Living: Domestic Assistance ≈ $368/month.

- Independence Support: Social Support ≈ $184/month.

Other arrangements noted in my assessment: OT assessment (Clinical Care) billed at $180 for a 1-hour assessment when delivered; meal delivery service (“Grants”) to be ordered by me as needed (costs outside Salveo service pricing); taxi cards arranged for transport subsidy.

Care Plan Consent and Distribution

I agree with this care plan and the goals we have set together. I consent to Salveo HomeCare coordinating and delivering the services listed, and to sharing this plan with my chosen support people and relevant health professionals (e.g., my GP, nursing/allied health) for safe, coordinated care.

I understand this plan will be reviewed every 3 months, or sooner if my needs or preferences change.

Transcript Summary – Denise Ruxton (map to Standards 1–8)

Standard 1 – Consumer dignity and choice: I stated that God, family and honesty matter to me. I prefer calm, clear communication and either male or female workers. I want my OCD and dust phobia respected. I chose resuscitation (CPR) if found unconscious/not breathing. I wish to speak with a priest/pastoral care at end of life.

Standard 2 – Ongoing assessment and planning with consumers: I contributed to this assessment, describing my history, daily routines, risks, preferences, and goals. Services were co-designed: nursing M/W/F, domestic assistance weekly, physio monthly, OT assessment, podiatry 6–8 weekly, meal delivery, and taxi cards. Reviews are set quarterly.

Standard 3 – Personal care and clinical care: I need regular wound care, pain monitoring, and falls prevention via physiotherapy. I have allergies/sensitivities (theatre tape) documented. My stroke history, mobility limits, and foot conditions inform safe clinical care. End-of-life pastoral access was noted.

Standard 4 – Services and supports for daily living: Domestic Assistance focuses on stockings and kitchen benches to reduce anxiety and support visitors. Social Support will help me structure mornings and practise relaxing. Meal delivery (“Grants”) was requested to simplify meals.

Standard 5 – Organisation's service environment: Visits will be coordinated to minimise disruption (e.g., Monday mornings aligned with Bruce’s support). Entry protocols and a held key were discussed to ensure safe access.

Standards 6–8 – Feedback & complaints; Human resources; Organisational governance: I will provide feedback at reviews or sooner if concerns arise. Qualified staff will deliver clinical and support services within scope (RN/allied health/personal and domestic support). Governance includes emergency protocols (000, CPR, call family), documentation of allergies, and quarterly reviews under the Support at Home framework.

saved_care_plans.html:
Care Plan

Care Alerts

I have a diagnosed Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) with a phobia of dust; please keep visible surfaces clear and avoid stirring up dust during visits.

I am allergic/sensitive to theatre tape (historical issue post-surgery); avoid using theatre tape on my skin.

I have had 10–12 falls in the past year; I use a walker and have balance issues, especially when rushing to the bathroom due to urinary urgency.

I require wound care/dressings three times per week (currently feet), with the left foot more prone to wet/macerated dressings.

Pain in my feet is constant and can disturb my sleep; I take Panadol as needed (two tablets when pain spikes).

I prefer workers to call triple zero (000) first in an emergency, commence resuscitation (CPR), then call my family.

I accept male or female care workers; please communicate clearly, allow extra time for decisions, and provide reassurance when my anxiety is heightened.

My Care Plan

Date of this Care Plan: 16 September 2025

Preferred Name: Denise

Full Name: Denise Ruxton

Purpose of this Care Plan: To outline services and supports under the Support at Home Program (November 2025)

Preferred Language: English

Interpreter required?: No

People involved in developing my care plan

  • I, Denise Ruxton, participated in the assessment and co-designed this plan.

  • Care Partner (assessor) facilitated the assessment and planning.

  • Bruce (my husband) contributed during the discussion.

  • Lee (my son and enduring power of attorney) holds my advance care plan and can be consulted as required.

Things to consider about my cultural, diversity, values and belief

I am Catholic; God and family are very important to me, along with honesty. I would like to be more assertive.

I identify as heterosexual.

I have OCD with a strong phobia of dust. Please be mindful of cleaning approaches and reassurance to reduce anxiety.

At end of life, I would like to speak with a priest or pastoral care representative.

My care worker, communication and service delivery preferences

I am comfortable with male or female workers.

Please communicate clearly, give me time to make decisions, and provide gentle prompts to slow down for safety.

Please schedule wound care on Monday/Wednesday/Friday mornings (around 9–10 am) and align with Bruce’s routine where possible to minimise disruption to our day.

Please keep visible surfaces free of dust and clutter to reduce my anxiety; kitchen benches are a particular trigger for me.

Single Provider Model: Under Support at Home, one provider manages all care coordination

My Preferred Support People

  • Bruce (husband)

  • Amanda (daughter)

  • Lee (son, enduring power of attorney)

  • Tracey (daughter-in-law)

Informal Supports

Bruce is my primary support at home. We plan to build routines together in our new home in Ballarat, including eating breakfast out every second day.

Important things to know about me

Family Background and Life History

I am the second of four sisters and was raised in a Catholic family. I trained as a nurse at St Vincent’s Hospital in Melbourne and worked in nursing for many years, including palliative care and night duty. I also trained in social work and worked with homeless men in North Melbourne before returning to nursing. I married Bruce in 1962; we recently celebrated our 63rd anniversary. I retired around age 59.

Interests

I like getting household tasks done and feel best when I’ve had breakfast early and can get started. I would like to have time to read (e.g., Country Life magazine) and to build more social routines. Going out with Bruce (e.g., breakfast) makes me happy. I want my kitchen to look tidy for visitors.

My Medical Information

Medical History:

  • OCD with phobia of dust; high anxiety/worry.

  • Mental health “breakdown” in 1984; completed an OCD program with some improvement.

  • Right knee replacement (reduced right-leg flexibility).

  • Right mastectomy for large cancer; multiple prior lumpectomies.

  • Minor stroke in 2010 with residual left-sided numbness (fingers feel “wooden”).

  • Foot injuries including three broken bones in the foot (wore a moon boot for 7 weeks), prior broken toe; taxi ran over foot approximately a year ago.

  • Three broken bones in hand (just before last Christmas).

  • Bunions (right worse) and hammertoes (right worse), complicating dressings.

  • Possible facial skin lesion (to be reviewed by skin specialist after move).

  • Shortness of breath on inclines.

Medication:

  • Blister-packed regular medications (names not recorded in this transcript).

  • Bladder urgency medication (name not recorded) to help with urinary urgency.

  • Panadol as needed for pain (typically two tablets when pain spikes; not every day).

  • Lyrica ceased due to sleepiness and increased falls.

Mobility and Equipment:

  • I use a walker; I also “furniture-walk.” Indoor walker use has been recommended.

  • Balance is my main difficulty; I tend to turn too quickly and rush, particularly to the bathroom.

  • I approach car entry from the left side due to right knee limitations.

  • I have an over-toilet aid and use continence pads.

  • I often sleep in a recliner due to pain but want OT help to return to bed sleeping.

GP / Pharmacy: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

Risk Assessment

Vulnerable Person (CALD:, Living with disability (mobility):, Mental health (low mood/isolation risk):)

CALD: Not identified. Living with disability (mobility): Yes – high falls risk, walker-dependent. Mental health (low mood/isolation risk): Yes – anxiety/OCD and worry.

Specific Risks

  • Falls risk: 10–12 falls in the past year; worsens when rushing to the bathroom due to urinary urgency; balance impairments and quick turns.

  • Wound risk: Left foot dressings can become wet; risk of maceration/infection.

  • Pain-related sleep disturbance leading to fatigue and reduced function; currently sleeping in a chair.

  • Transfer risk: Difficult car entry/exit; right knee limited flexion.

  • Mental health: Anxiety/OCD with dust phobia; cluttered kitchen triggers anxiety.

  • Allergy/sensitivity to theatre tape; avoid use on skin.

  • Breathlessness on inclines; pace activities to avoid overexertion.

Emergency Contacts & Instructions

If there is no answer for a scheduled visit: call my mobile, check with neighbours/management, then contact my family. There will be a key available through the office/management.

If I am found unconscious or not breathing during a visit: call triple zero (000) immediately, commence resuscitation (CPR), then call my family.

  • Primary contacts: Bruce (husband); Amanda (daughter); Lee (son and EPOA). Contact numbers: Not documented in this transcript; this section will be updated as further details are provided.

End-of-life preference: I would like a priest or pastoral care representative to be contacted.

My Goals

GOAL 1 Goal: I will have my foot wounds managed so dressings stay dry/intact and my skin shows no signs of infection, allowing me to walk safely with my walker over the next 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have constant foot pain, wet dressings (left worse), bunions/hammertoes, and high falls risk. Allergy to theatre tape.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Registered Nurse to attend Monday/Wednesday/Friday to assess, cleanse and re-dress wounds; monitor exudate, skin condition, and pain; educate me on when to change a wet dressing; liaise with podiatry/GP as needed.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Registered Nurse; I will report wet dressings and pain levels. When will it be done?: Mon/Wed/Fri around 9–10 am for the next 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: RN $148.50/hour x ~12 hours/month ≈ $1,782/month (dressings billed to package as required).

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 2 Goal: I will reduce my falls by building balance and safe walking habits so I have no more than 1 fall in the next 3 months and can complete my home exercise program 5 days/week.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I use a walker, turn too quickly, and rush to the bathroom due to urgency; 10–12 falls in past year.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Allied Health Physiotherapist to review and progress a home exercise and gait training program; practice slow turns, pacing and indoor walker use; consider TUG or similar functional measure at baseline and 12 weeks.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health Therapist (Physio) and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour monthly with daily home practice (5 days/week) over 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: Physio $180/hour = $180/month.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 3 Goal: I will safely return to sleeping in my bed (not the chair) at least 5 nights per week within 12 weeks by implementing OT recommendations and transfer strategies.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Pain disturbs sleep; I currently sleep in a recliner; bed transfers feel difficult; risk of pressure and poor rest if I remain in the chair.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Occupational Therapist comprehensive assessment of bed/chair transfers, environment, and equipment needs; teach techniques and stage a graded plan to move back to bed; follow-up to review progress.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Allied Health Therapist (OT) and me. When will it be done?: Initial 2 hours in Month 1; 1-hour follow-up in Month 2; self-practice nightly. How much will it cost?: OT $180/hour (Quarter total ≈ $540; average ≈ $180/month). Any equipment recommended will be separately costed/approved.

Service Category: Clinical Care

GOAL 4 Goal: I will keep my kitchen and high-dust areas visibly tidy each week so I feel comfortable when visitors arrive and my OCD/dust anxiety is lowered by at least 2 points (self-rated 0–10) by 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Dust is a phobia trigger; I worry about cluttered benches; I appreciate help with washing my compression stockings and kitchen cleaning.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Domestic Assistance to focus on kitchen benches, visible surfaces, light dusting, floor/vacuum, and washing/air-drying compression stockings; quick weekly tidy and bin-out; avoid stirring dust.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Domestic Assistance team; I will identify priority areas each visit. When will it be done?: 2 hours weekly (preferably Thursdays). How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 2 hours/week ≈ $680/month.

Service Category: Everyday Living

GOAL 5 Goal: I will establish a calmer morning routine so I have breakfast before 9:30 am on at least 5 days per week and feel less anxious (reduce by 2 points on a 0–10 scale) within 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I can become grumpy/anxious; decision-making can be slow; I benefit from gentle prompts and reassurance.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Weekly Social Support visit to prompt pacing, gentle planning, and brief check-in; create a simple morning checklist; reinforce relaxation strategies taught previously.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Social Support worker and me. When will it be done?: 1 hour weekly for 12 weeks. How much will it cost?: $85/hour ≈ $340/month.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 6 Goal: I will get out of the house to a local café for breakfast with Bruce twice per week to build social connection and routine over the next 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): I have difficulty with car transfers and low confidence going out; I aim to go every second day but will start with twice weekly.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Transport support for two local café outings per week; allow extra time to approach the car from the left; worker standby for safe transfers; plan routes that avoid steep inclines.

Who is responsible?: Salveo HomeCare Transport service; I will plan preferred days. When will it be done?: 2 outings/week, 1 hour per outing. How much will it cost?: $85/hour x 2 hours/week ≈ $680/month plus $1.40/km (estimate 40 km/month ≈ $56). Taxi subsidy/card may be used where applicable.

Service Category: Independence Support

GOAL 7 Goal: I will maintain my foot health so there are no new skin breakdowns and pain is reduced by 2 points (0–10) within 12 weeks.

Abilities and considerations (risks): Bunions and hammertoes (right worse) complicate dressing; prior skin tears between toes; ongoing pain.

How will we do this? (Tasks): Podiatry home visits for assessment, nail/skin care, offloading advice; align with RN wound plan; footwear review.

risks.description: History of approximately 10–12 falls in the past year, often when rushing to the bathroom due to urinary urgency; balance issues and tendency to turn too quickly; uses a walker. Has hit head and required CT scans after some falls.
Chronic foot wounds/skin tears with bunions and hammertoes; requires dressings three times weekly. Dressings sometimes become wet, particularly on the left foot.
Constant foot pain affecting sleep and mood; wakes at night. Often sleeps in a chair due to pain.
OCD with dust phobia and high generalized anxiety; past mental breakdown in 1984. Reports increased anger related to stress and pain.
Urinary urgency; uses continence pads. Urgency contributes to rushing and falls on the way to the toilet.
Difficulty getting into cars due to limited right knee flexion post knee replacement; must enter from left side. Balance issues and furniture walking at home.
Mild shortness of breath on inclines.
Allergic reaction to theatre tape/adhesives reported after prior surgery.
Tends to stay indoors and not engage in village activities; worries about visitors seeing a messy kitchen.
Minor stroke in 2010 with residual left-sided hand numbness.
Possible facial skin cancer lesion awaiting specialist review.

Previously took Lyrica (pregabalin) for nerve pain but ceased due to sleepiness and falls. No patches or injections.

preferences.culturalConsiderations: Catholic; God and family are very important. Wishes to speak with a priest or pastoral care at end of life. No specific cultural factors required for worker matching.
preferences.serviceDeliveryPreferences: Emergency: call 000, commence resuscitation, then call family. Nursing for wound care three times weekly (Mon/Wed/Fri), ideally around 9–10am and coordinated with Bruce’s personal care to minimise waiting. Domestic assistance on Thursdays. Physiotherapy monthly (1 hour), OT assessment, and podiatry every 6–8 weeks at home. Meal delivery service (Grants) desired. Taxi subsidy/card for transport. Prefers early breakfast and morning appointments; avoid weekend nursing if possible.
